groups.overview: `core/abc` is the package that holds the shared contracts and base classes for Agent, Tool, Source, LLM, Harness, and so on. Its modules import only from inside `core/abc` and the pure Python values in `core/builtin/domain`, and do not depend on ORM, Store, Provider, HTTP, or queue implementations. The center of this group, `agent.py`, defines the concrete base class `BaseAgent`: the `@final` `run` is the single execution boundary and uniformly handles Harness evaluation, the LLM loop, dispatching Tools and child agents, arbitration of the Tool failure ledger, and execution logging. Every agent in the version-owned `agent/` folder inherits from it; `core/builtin/compose.build_agents` instantiates each one once by name (child agent instances are not bound; children are obtained by name through `ctx.agents` at execution time), and `Runtime._call` in the runtime process calls the entry agent's `run`.

modules.role: Entry point of the `core/abc` package; declares that this is the layer holding the shared contracts and base classes for Agent, Tool, Source, and LLM.
modules.summary: Contains only a docstring; it re-exports no names and performs no imports. The docstring states the policy: use the values and in-execution state of `core.builtin.domain`, which does not depend on the ORM, and do not import concrete Store, Provider, HTTP, or queue implementations. Callers always import absolutely from submodules, e.g. `from trackeverything.core.abc.agent import BaseAgent`.
modules.flow: Loaded as the parent package whenever any `trackeverything.core.abc.*` submodule is imported. Both the queue and runtime processes load it, but it executes no code itself.
invariants: Modules in `core/abc` import only from inside `core/abc` and `core/builtin/domain`, and do not depend on ORM, Store, Provider, HTTP, or queue implementations.
pitfalls: The package re-exports no names, so `from trackeverything.core.abc import BaseAgent` does not work; you must import from the specific submodule.

modules.role: Provides the concrete base class `BaseAgent`, responsible for the agent execution boundary, Harness evaluation, the LLM loop, dispatching Tools and child agents, arbitration of Tool failures, and execution logging.
modules.summary: `BaseAgent` declares its composition through class variables (Tools and Harnesses by type; child agents, LLM, and Skills by name): `tools` (Tool types, instantiated without arguments in `__init__`), `pre / post / on_error` (Harness types, instantiated with this agent's `LLMClient`), `agents` (child agent names; `__init__` neither creates nor binds instances, and at execution time `call_agent` and `_build_callables` obtain them by name through `ctx.agents`), and `llm` (a key of `HostServices.llms`: `max`, `high`, `low`, `flash`, `flash_low`). The `@final` `run` is the single execution boundary: `_enter` puts the run ID, this execution's ID, the parent execution ID, a new `AgentToolScope`, and the instance's component version `version_label` (set by the version store to `c.<first 8 chars of the version id>`) into ContextVars; after checking the delegation depth it runs, in order, the pre Harnesses, `_execute`, the post Harnesses (only for an ok result), and `_adjudicate`, records the `agent` event, and then runs the on_error Harnesses when the result is error. The default `_execute` calls `_execute_llm_loop`, which consumes the shared step budget through `ctx.advance_step()` on each step and calls the LLM once with callables rebuilt on every step, until a `FinalAnswer` or the budget runs out. A `Calls` response is dispatched by `_dispatch_calls`: consecutive child agent calls run in parallel through `call_agent`, Tool calls run one at a time through `call_tool` after the preceding child group finishes (a barrier), and the observations are appended in request order as `tool`-role messages. `call_tool` converts exceptions to `ToolResult(ok=False)` and records or resolves failures in `ctx.tool_failures` by `Tool.error_key`; when `run` ends, `_adjudicate` consumes this execution's unresolved failures, and only failures of `fatal_tools` flip ok to error. When a `LogRecorder` is injected, every execution of an Agent, Tool, or Harness is recorded as a `LogEvent`; LLM events are linked to the current execution by `llm/tracking.py` through `current_run_id` and `current_agent_execution_id`, which this module sets. Skill Tools are added to this execution's scope by `read_skill` in the external `tools/skill.py` through `tool_scope` and `register_run_tools`, and appear in the callables from the next LLM call onward. The constructor first registers the Host base tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` from `core/builtin/base_tools.py`), so every agent has them and a component Tool with one of those names fails composition.
modules.flow: At composition time, when the version store loads a version, `core/builtin/compose.build_agents` instantiates each agent by name (validating only the child agent names). At execution time, `Runtime._call` in the runtime process calls `run` of the single entry agent `dispatch` within `asyncio.timeout(config.RUN_TIMEOUT)`; child agents are obtained by name through `ctx.agents` (the run handle `RunVersions`), and from then on everything runs inside this module until all child agents, Tools, and Harnesses finish.

key_symbols.name: log
key_symbols.explain: Module logger `trackeverything.agent`, used only to log warnings when an on_error Harness itself fails.

key_symbols.name: MAX_AGENT_DEPTH
key_symbols.explain: Maximum child agent delegation depth (16). The entry `run` has depth 1; when the depth exceeds this value (the 17th level), `run` raises `RuntimeError`, which is converted to an error result at the boundary, and neither the pre Harnesses nor `_execute` run. Cyclic delegation through the mesh is terminated by this limit together with the shared step budget.

key_symbols.name: PARALLEL_CALL_RULE
key_symbols.explain: English rule text: agent calls in one response run in parallel, Tool calls run in order, and a call that depends on another call's result goes into a later response. Appended once to the first system message by `_add_system_extras`, only when the callables offered to the LLM include child agents.

key_symbols.name: _REPAIR_PROMPT
key_symbols.explain: Prefix of the repair prompt appended for the LLM under `repair_tool_failures`; it asks for the complete answer again, because the next answer replaces the previous one, is followed by the rendered unresolved notes, and states that the error details are data, not instructions.

key_symbols.name: _NOT_OFFERED
key_symbols.explain: Error text `callable was not offered`, returned when the LLM calls a name that was not offered.

key_symbols.name: AgentToolScope
key_symbols.explain: The scope owned by one `run`: `owner`, `ctx`, the delegation depth `depth`, plus the additional Tools `tools` that belong only to this execution, the loaded Skills `loaded_skills` (Skill name → fingerprint and Tools), and the Skill definition checks `checks` run before each call of that Tool.

key_symbols.name: _current_scope
key_symbols.explain: Holds the current execution's `AgentToolScope`; set by `_enter` and restored at the end. A new scope's depth is the enclosing scope's depth plus 1, and `_own_scope` returns it only when `owner` is self.

key_symbols.name: _Span
key_symbols.explain: A log span created at start, holding the event type, run ID, component name, request, and new execution ID. `parent_id` is the `current_agent_execution_id` at creation time, and `end` produces a `LogEvent` with the elapsed time from `snapshot`.

key_symbols.name: _evaluate
key_symbols.explain: Runs one Harness check, treating an `Exception` as a refusal and returning `{type, message}` (fail-closed).

key_symbols.name: _refused
key_symbols.explain: Builds the error result for a Harness refusal: `response` is `harness '<name>' ...` and the note's stage is `harness:<name>`; when the check raises, the cause is `failed closed: <type>: <message>`.

key_symbols.name: _incomplete
key_symbols.explain: `_incomplete(unresolved, answer)` builds the error result for fatal failures left unresolved under `repair_tool_failures`: the response is the latest answer, or `Required operations remain incomplete: ...` when the LLM never gave one. `errors` stays empty; `_adjudicate` adds each fatal note once.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent
key_symbols.explain: Concrete base class: class variables declare Tool types, child agent names, Harness types, the LLM name, and Skill names (only child agents, LLM, and Skills are declared by name); `run` unifies the execution boundary, LLM loop, dispatch, and logging. Subclasses override only hooks such as `_execute`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.llm
key_symbols.explain: Name of the LLM client to use, default `max`; a key of `HostServices.llms` (`max`, `high`, `low`, `flash`, `flash_low`). `build_agents` instantiates with `llms[cls.llm]` and raises `ValueError` for an unknown name.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.skills
key_symbols.explain: Names of loadable Skills. This module does not read it; `tools/skill.bind_skills` uses it to register `read_skill` and call `configure_skills`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.agents
key_symbols.explain: Tuple of child agent names. `__init__` deduplicates it into `_agent_names` and neither creates nor binds instances. At execution time `call_agent` obtains the instance by name through `ctx.agents` (fixed within a run to the version obtained first), and `build_agents` only validates that the names exist in the same version.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.fatal_tools
key_symbols.explain: Set of Tool names whose unresolved failures flip ok to error in `_adjudicate`, and trigger the repair prompt when `repair_tool_failures=True`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.hidden_callables
key_symbols.explain: Names of Tools and child agents called only from Python control. `_build_callables` merges the sets that each class in the whole MRO declares itself and excludes them from the callables.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.__init__
key_symbols.explain: Stores the `LLMClient` and the optional `LogRecorder`, deduplicates `agents` into `_agent_names`, initializes `version_label` (the `c.<first 8 chars of the version id>` of the component version the instance belongs to, set by the version store) to `None`, instantiates `tools` without arguments, and instantiates and registers `pre / post / on_error` with the same LLM. It creates no child agents and never replaces the LLM during execution.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.register
key_symbols.explain: Registers a Tool by name; a duplicate name is rejected with `ValueError`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.extend_callables
key_symbols.explain: `extend_callables(tools, agent_names)`: lets `core/builtin/callable_mesh.wire_full_mesh` add shared Tool instances and child agent names. Existing names take precedence, empty names and its own name are skipped, and only names are added; no child agent instances are added.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.register_pre_harness
key_symbols.explain: Appends a pre Harness by name; duplicate names are rejected, and it is ordered after the class-declared `pre`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.register_post_harness
key_symbols.explain: Appends a post Harness by name; duplicate names are rejected, and it is ordered after the class-declared `post`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.register_error_harness
key_symbols.explain: Appends an on_error Harness by name; duplicate names are rejected, and it is ordered after the class-declared `on_error`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.configure_skills
key_symbols.explain: Binds the Skill catalog string at composition time; `_add_system_extras` appends it to the first system message.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.list_tools
key_symbols.explain: Returns the registered Tools (the class-declared `tools`, plus `BASE_TOOLS`, `fetch_source`, and `read_skill` registered through `register` at composition, and the mesh Tools appended by `extend_callables`), plus the Skill Tools in the current scope when called inside its own execution.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.list_agent_names
key_symbols.explain: Returns the child agent names (class-declared and mesh-added), used by validation in `build_agents`, parent-child links in `core/builtin/catalog`, and conflict checks in `tools/skill.bind_skills`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.list_pre_harnesses
key_symbols.explain: Returns the registered pre Harness instances, used by `core/builtin/catalog` to list the component catalog.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.list_post_harnesses
key_symbols.explain: Returns the registered post Harness instances, used by `core/builtin/catalog` to list the component catalog.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.has_agent
key_symbols.explain: Checks whether a name is a declared child agent (does not obtain the instance). `agent/dispatch.py` uses it before delegating to an entrance, and `agent/conversation.py` before delegating to the investigator.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.child_meta
key_symbols.explain: `child_meta(name, ctx)` obtains the child instance from `ctx.agents` and returns the `name`, `description`, and `arguments` shown to the LLM. Raises `KeyError` for an undeclared name, a missing run handle, or a child instance that cannot be obtained.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._lookup_child
key_symbols.explain: Returns `ctx.agents.agent(name)` when the name is a child name and `ctx.agents` exists, otherwise None. `call_agent`, `child_meta`, and `_build_callables` share it to obtain child instances.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.tool_scope
key_symbols.explain: Returns the current scope whose `owner` is self and whose `ctx` is the same object; otherwise raises `ValueError("current Agent execution is required")`. Skill-related Tools use it to verify the real caller instead of what the JSON claims.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.register_run_tools
key_symbols.explain: Registers Skill Tools in the current execution scope: if the same Skill is already loaded, an identical fingerprint is a no-op and a different one is rejected. All name conflicts (same name as a child agent, same name as an existing Tool of a different instance, duplicates within the list) are checked first, then everything is appended at once; an existing identical instance is not added again. A `validate` check is registered for every Tool name.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._own_scope
key_symbols.explain: Returns `_current_scope` only when its `owner` is self; otherwise returns `None`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._resolve_tool
key_symbols.explain: Resolves a Tool by name among the registered Tools (including `BASE_TOOLS` and others registered at composition) and the Tools in its own execution scope; returns `None` if not found.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.run
key_symbols.explain: The `@final` execution boundary: creates an `agent` span (the request is a snapshot of `request` and `ctx.data`), checks the depth inside `_enter`, runs pre, `_execute`, post and `_adjudicate` when ok, records the `agent` event, and runs on_error on error. An `Exception` becomes an error result with an `execution` note plus all unresolved failures; cancellation records `cancelled` and re-raises.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._enter
key_symbols.explain: Context manager that sets `current_run_id`, `current_agent_execution_id`, `current_parent_agent_execution_id`, and a new `AgentToolScope` (depth = enclosing + 1) in ContextVars, also sets `current_component_version` to the instance's `version_label` when it has one, and restores them in reverse order at the end.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._adjudicate
key_symbols.explain: Consumes this execution's unresolved Tool failures with `take()`: an ok result with `fatal_tools` failures flips to error (errors are the fatal notes); an ok result without fatal failures is unchanged and the failures appear only as log notes. For a non-ok result, errors are the original notes plus the fatal notes; if still empty, `max_steps` gets a `budget` note and anything else gets a note whose stage is the agent name.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._check_pre
key_symbols.explain: Evaluates pre in order, recording a `harness` event (`ok` or `blocked`) for each; the first refusal returns the `_refused` error result.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._check_post
key_symbols.explain: Evaluates post in order, recording a `harness` event (`ok` or `rejected`) for each; on refusal it keeps `original_result` in the event result and returns an error result.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._handle_error
key_symbols.explain: Calls each on_error `handle` in order; exceptions are written only to a warning log and a `failed` event, and never replace the original result.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._log
key_symbols.explain: Ends the span as a `LogEvent` and records it, only when a `LogRecorder` was injected.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._execute
key_symbols.explain: Extension point for subclasses to change control; by default calls `_execute_llm_loop`.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._execute_llm_loop
key_symbols.explain: Builds the messages and appends the system extras once, then loops: rebuild callables, `_respond_one_step`. `FinalAnswer` returns ok; on `Calls` it appends the assistant message with `raw` and the observations from `_dispatch_calls`. When the budget runs out it returns `max_steps`. With `repair_tool_failures=True`, the first `FinalAnswer` that leaves fatal failures unresolved is kept as the latest answer and gets the repair prompt once; a later `FinalAnswer` that still leaves them, or a budget that runs out while they remain, returns `_incomplete` with the latest answer (the fixed text only when no answer was given).

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._add_system_extras
key_symbols.explain: Appends the Skill catalog and the `PARALLEL_CALL_RULE` (when `_build_callables(ctx)` includes child agents), joined by blank lines, to the first system message; inserts one at the start if there is no system message, and does not append again if the end is already identical.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._respond_one_step
key_symbols.explain: Consumes one unit of the shared step budget and then calls this agent's LLM once; returns `None` when the budget is exhausted. Custom control in subclasses also goes through it to respect the budget.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.get_prompt
key_symbols.explain: Hook for the system prompt; returns an empty string by default.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._build_messages
key_symbols.explain: Returns `[system(get_prompt()), user(_build_user_message)]` by default, where the user message is the JSON of `request` and `ctx.data`; subclasses that need to prepend conversation history override it.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._build_callables
key_symbols.explain: Converts the non-hidden Tools in `list_tools()` and the non-hidden child agents obtained through the run handle in `ctx` into `name / description / arguments`. `hidden_callables` is merged along the MRO, hidden children are not obtained, and without `ctx` no child agents are included.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._dispatch_calls
key_symbols.explain: Executes the calls in one response: a name that was not offered is not executed; it records a `tool` event and returns an error observation without breaking the child agent group. Consecutive child agents are accumulated first; when a Tool is reached, the accumulated child group runs first and then the Tool runs alone. Observations are returned in request order at the end.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._run_children
key_symbols.explain: Runs a single item in the current task and multiple items in parallel with `asyncio.TaskGroup`, returning observations by index.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._dispatch
key_symbols.explain: Tools take precedence: it calls `call_tool` with arguments converted by `tool.llm_args`, and the observation contains `ok / output / error`. Otherwise it calls `call_agent` with the `request` from the arguments, and the observation contains `ok / status / output / error` (`render(errors)`).

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.call_agent
key_symbols.explain: `@final`, the only execution path for child agents: obtains the child instance by name through `call.ctx.agents` and runs its `run` in the same Context with `call.child(request)`; hidden children can also be called. When the name is not a child name, there is no run handle, or the child cannot be obtained, it returns an error result with a `delegation` note (`agent not registered: <name>`).

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent.call_tool
key_symbols.explain: Runs a Tool and records a `tool` event (the request is the arguments; the output is not recorded): exceptions become `ToolResult(ok=False)`. On success it calls `resolve` for failures with the same `error_key` and failures with no target; on failure it calls `record` with the Tool name as the stage. Cancellation records `cancelled` and re-raises.

key_symbols.name: BaseAgent._invoke
key_symbols.explain: An unresolved Tool returns an `unknown tool: <name>` failure. Inside its own execution scope with the same `ctx`, it first runs all Skill definition checks registered for that Tool name, then calls `tool.run` with the `ctx` keyword.

invariants: `run` is `@final`; control changes go only in `_execute` (and hooks such as `_build_messages` and `get_prompt`). An `Exception` raised by the depth limit, `_execute`, or `_adjudicate` is converted to an `AgentResult` with `status="error"`, whose `errors` are the `execution` note plus all of this execution's unresolved Tool failures. Exceptions raised by the `check` of a pre/post Harness do not take this path: `_evaluate` catches them and treats them as refusals, so the result has a `harness:<name>` note (cause `failed closed: <type>: <message>`) and no `execution` note.
`asyncio.CancelledError` discards this execution's unresolved failures, records an `agent` event with `cancelled`, and re-raises; the on_error Harnesses do not run.

The execution order is fixed: depth check → pre → `_execute` → post (ok only) → `_adjudicate` → record the `agent` event → on_error (only when `status == "error"`; `max_steps` does not trigger it). Each Harness chain is evaluated in class declaration order, then in `register_*_harness` order, and short-circuits on the first refusal. An `Exception` raised by a pre or post check counts as a refusal (fail-closed); a failure of on_error itself only records a `failed` event and a warning log and does not replace the original result.

A non-ok result carries at least one `ErrorNote`: when there are no notes, `max_steps` gets a `budget` note and anything else gets a note whose stage is the agent name. Callers read `errors` instead of parsing `response`.

The Tool failure ledger is slotted by `current_agent_execution_id`; a child agent's Tool failures are consumed at the child's `run` boundary and do not enter the parent agent's arbitration. `fatal_tools` matches on `ErrorNote.stage` (the Tool name written by `call_tool`).

Consecutive child agent calls in one response run in parallel, and a Tool call waits for the preceding child group to finish and then runs alone; observations are returned in request order, and names that were not offered are never executed. A child agent's failure is returned as an `AgentResult` and does not cancel the other children in the group through the `TaskGroup`.

Child agents run only through `call_agent`; the child call is created by `call.child(request)` and shares the same `AgentContext` (`data`, step budget, failure ledger). When the LLM delegates to a child agent, only the `request` from the arguments is passed to the child.
The Context never goes into JSON arguments: on the LLM path the arguments are converted by `Tool.llm_args`, and `call_tool` injects `ctx` into `Tool.run` as a keyword.

Child agent instances are not bound at composition: `call_agent`, `child_meta`, and `_build_callables` obtain them by name through `ctx.agents` each time, and within one run the run handle fixes a child agent of a given name to the version obtained first. Children offered to the LLM are obtained when the callables are built; children in `hidden_callables` are not obtained until they are called.
pitfalls: `hidden_callables` is merged from `vars(cls)` of each class in `type(self).__mro__`, so a subclass writes only its own additions. Hidden names do not appear in the callables, so an LLM call gets `callable was not offered`, while Python control can still call them through `call_agent` or `call_tool`.

Skill Tools added by `register_run_tools` belong only to this execution's scope whose `owner` is self; a child agent's `run` creates a new scope and cannot see the Skill Tools loaded by the parent execution. `offered` is computed at the start of each step, so calling a new Tool after `read_skill` in the same response counts as not offered; it becomes available from the next LLM call.

`call_tool` is not `@final`; `agent/discord_output.py` and `agent/general.py` both override it. An override must call `super().call_tool` to keep the failure ledger, the Skill definition checks, and the `tool` event. When Python control calls `call_tool` directly, the arguments do not go through `llm_args`.

`_dispatch` resolves Tools first, so on a name clash a Tool takes precedence over a child agent. `register_run_tools` rejects Skill Tools with the same name as a child agent or as an existing Tool of a different instance.

The default `_execute_llm_loop` does not check unresolved failures on `FinalAnswer`; only when `repair_tool_failures=True` is passed and `fatal_tools` is declared does it append the repair prompt once (consuming another step), and if failures remain unresolved it returns error with the latest answer kept as the response. The loop returns that error without notes and only `run()`'s `_adjudicate` attaches them, so a test that calls the loop directly sees no `errors`. `agent/general.py` and `agent/project.py` use this option.

For a non-ok result, non-fatal unresolved failures are consumed but appear neither in `errors` nor in the `agent` event; for an ok result, non-fatal failures appear only in the error field of the `agent` event, and the result stays ok.
The `tool` event records only the arguments, status, and error; it does not record the Tool's `output`.

Child agents running in parallel in one response share `ctx.data` and the step budget: any child's change to `ctx.data` is visible to the others, and the parallel children compete for the same budget.

The final `agent` event and on_error run outside the `try`: the guarantee that `run` never raises outward depends on `LogRecorder.record` itself not raising (the implementation in `core/builtin/execution_log.py` swallows write failures).

`has_agent` only checks the name and does not guarantee that the run handle can return an instance. `child_meta` raises `KeyError` when the name is not a child name, `ctx.agents` is None, or the child cannot be obtained; in the same cases `call_agent` returns an error result with a `delegation` note and records no `agent` event.

The logger does not propagate between parent and child; each instance receives it from `build_agents`, and constructing an instance directly must pass it explicitly. Without `AgentContext.agents`, child agents do not appear in the callables and `call_agent` returns an error. Tests that do not use the version store pass a fixed run handle with `core/builtin/compose.StaticAgents`.

diagram.caption: This diagram shows how `BaseAgent` instances are built by name through `build_agents` from the version's `agent/compose.py`, which also registers the shared Tools and Skills, and how at run time execution enters the `run` boundary from `Runtime._call` and is dispatched through `_dispatch_calls` either to `call_tool` or to `call_agent`, which obtains the child instance through `ctx.agents`.

groups.overview: This group covers the shared contracts in `core/abc` other than `BaseAgent`. `call.py` and `context.py` define the input and output of one agent call, the mutable context shared by the whole agent tree, and `AgentLookup` for obtaining child agents by name; `tool.py`, `harness.py`, `llm.py`, and `source.py` are the ABCs for Tool, enforced Harness, the LLM port, and Source; `execution_log.py` is the execution log Protocol injected into the base class. `submission.py` is the message contract between the queue and runtime processes: the queue carries only one kind of execution request, `EventRequest`; publishers construct and publish it, and `QueueConsumer` and `Runtime` on the runtime side read messages with the same model and convert them into the `AgentContext` and `AgentCall` handed to the dispatch agent. These modules depend only on pydantic and the values in `core/builtin/domain`, and do not import the ORM, concrete Stores, or Providers. Concrete implementations live in `trackeverything.llm`, `tools/`, `sources/`, `harnesses/`, and `core/builtin`, and `BaseAgent` in `core/abc/agent.py` ties them together during execution.

modules.role: Defines the input of one agent call, `AgentCall`, the output `AgentResult`, and the completion status type `AgentStatus`.
modules.summary: `AgentCall` is a `frozen=True, slots=True` dataclass holding the `ctx` (`AgentContext`) shared by the whole agent tree and this call's `request`. `child(request)` returns a new call that references the same `ctx` and replaces only `request`. `AgentResult` holds `status`, `response`, and the structured failures `errors` (a tuple of `ErrorNote`). `AgentStatus` is defined with a `type` statement as the Literal of `ok`, `max_steps`, `error`, `cancelled`. `Runtime._run` builds the dispatch agent's entry call with `request=None` (for a named run, dispatch passes the `request` to the child agent through `call_agent`), and `BaseAgent.call_agent` builds child agent calls with `call.child(request)`. `max_steps` is returned by `_execute_llm_loop` when the shared step budget runs out. `cancelled` is built by `Runtime`: a `RUN_TIMEOUT` timeout attaches a `deadline` note, and cancellation by the caller attaches a `cancellation` note. Finally, `Runtime` records the result through `PostgresSessionStore.finish_run`.
modules.flow: `Runtime` creates an entry `AgentCall` for each queue message and passes it to the entry agent's `run`. Child agent delegation derives calls with `child` through `call_agent`; every level of `run` returns an `AgentResult`, and `Runtime` finally writes it to the session record.

key_symbols.name: AgentStatus
key_symbols.explain: A Literal of `ok`, `max_steps`, `error`, `cancelled` representing the completion status of one agent call. `cancelled` means the run's deadline or the caller cancelled the whole agent tree.

key_symbols.name: AgentCall
key_symbols.explain: Immutable input value holding the shared `ctx` (`AgentContext`) and this call's own `request` (default `None`).

key_symbols.name: AgentCall.child
key_symbols.explain: Returns a child call that references the same `ctx` and replaces only `request`; used by `BaseAgent.call_agent`.

key_symbols.name: AgentResult
key_symbols.explain: Immutable output value holding `status`, `response`, and `errors` (a tuple of `ErrorNote`, empty by default). Callers read the failure reason from `errors` and do not parse `response`.

invariants: `AgentCall` and `AgentResult` are both `frozen=True, slots=True` dataclasses; their attributes cannot be reassigned after creation.
`AgentCall.child` does not copy `ctx`; the child call and the parent call share the same `AgentContext` object.
`AgentStatus` is restricted to `Literal["ok", "max_steps", "error", "cancelled"]`.

A non-`ok` result returned through the `BaseAgent.run` boundary has at least one entry in `errors`: `_adjudicate` adds a `budget` note for `max_steps` and a note whose stage is the agent name for other statuses.
pitfalls: `AgentCall` itself is immutable, but `ctx` is a mutable `AgentContext`. Child calls read and write the same `data` and consume the same step budget; the dispatch agent calls `clear()`/`update()` on `ctx.data` directly before delegating.

`PostgresSessionStore.finish_run` stores only `status` and `response`, not `errors`. That is why the module function `_failed` in `core/builtin/runtime.py` and the dispatch agent's `_failed` also write the reason into `response`.

`AgentResult` can be constructed with empty `errors`. Only results that pass through the `BaseAgent.run` boundary are guaranteed to carry notes; results built directly in Python inside an agent are not filled in automatically.

The queue process loads this module indirectly through `integration/discord.py` → `core.builtin.database` → `core.builtin.session_store`, but the queue side neither constructs `AgentCall` nor executes agents.

modules.role: Defines `AgentContext`, the mutable context shared by the whole agent tree within one complete agent run: shared `data`, the LLM step budget, run/session/message identifiers, and in-process state that is not exposed to the LLM (including the run handle for child agents, `agents`).
modules.summary: `AgentContext` is a mutable `slots=True` dataclass. `data` is business data shared between agents; `BaseAgent` serializes it together with `request` into the LLM user message. `max_steps` and the private counter `_step` form the LLM step budget shared by the whole tree: `advance_step` increments the counter by 1 for each step consumed and returns `False` when the budget is exhausted. `run_id` and `session_id` default to `uuid4().hex`; `Runtime._run` explicitly passes a `run_id` generated by `new_id()`, uses the `session_id` given by the request (creating one with `new_id()` only when absent), and attaches `parent_session_id`, `message_id` (the Redis stream id), and `acknowledger=self.queue.ack`. `ack(message_id)` calls `acknowledger` only when both are non-`None`, i.e. `QueueConsumer.ack` → `XACK` + `XDEL`. `authorization` is set by the dispatch agent after re-verification and before calling the child agent, and is read by `tools/fix/tool.py`, `agent/discord.py`, and `agent/issue.py`. `tool_failures` is the `ToolFailures` ledger: `BaseAgent.call_tool` records or resolves failures in it, and `_adjudicate` at the `run` boundary consumes it. `tool_state` holds Tools' in-run working state, such as the fetch task of `fetch_source` and the changes staged by `tools/project/store.py`. `agents` is an `AgentLookup` (a Protocol with `agent(name) -> BaseAgent | None`): `Runtime._run` sets it to the run's `RunVersions`, and `BaseAgent.call_agent` obtains child agents by name through it; scripts and tests that bypass the version store can pass `core/builtin/compose.StaticAgents`.
modules.flow: `Runtime._run` builds one `AgentContext` before executing each message (with `agents` set to that run's run handle) and puts it into the entry `AgentCall`. From then until the run ends, parent and child agents, Tools, and Harnesses all read and write this same instance through `call.ctx`.

key_symbols.name: DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS
key_symbols.explain: Default value of `max_steps` (12) when `AgentContext` is constructed directly. `Runtime` passes `config.MAX_STEPS` explicitly when constructing it.

key_symbols.name: AgentLookup
key_symbols.explain: Protocol for a run's agent handle: `agent(name)` returns an instance, or None if there is none. Which version is chosen is up to the implementation (`core/versioning/repo.RunVersions` pins to the main obtained first; `core/builtin/compose.StaticAgents` is a fixed mapping).

key_symbols.name: AgentContext
key_symbols.explain: Mutable context shared by the whole agent tree, holding `data`, the step budget, `run_id`/`session_id`/`parent_session_id`/`message_id`, `acknowledger`, `authorization`, `tool_failures`, `tool_state`, and the run handle for child agents, `agents`.

key_symbols.name: AgentContext.ack
key_symbols.explain: Calls `acknowledger(message_id)` when both `message_id` and `acknowledger` are non-`None`, marking the queue message as processed; does nothing in a run that did not come through the queue.

key_symbols.name: AgentContext.__post_init__
key_symbols.explain: Raises `ValueError` when `max_steps` is less than or equal to 0.

key_symbols.name: AgentContext.step
key_symbols.explain: Read-only property returning the number of LLM turns this agent tree has consumed.

key_symbols.name: AgentContext.advance_step
key_symbols.explain: Consumes one LLM turn and returns `True`; when `_step` has already reached `max_steps` it does not increment and returns `False`.

invariants: `max_steps` must be positive; `__post_init__` raises `ValueError` for 0 or a negative number.
Once `_step` reaches `max_steps`, `advance_step` returns `False` and the counter stays unchanged; `step` is read-only.
`_step`, `tool_failures`, and `tool_state` are `init=False` fields and cannot be passed as constructor arguments.

`acknowledger`, `authorization`, `tool_state`, and `agents` are `repr=False, compare=False`, and `tool_failures` is `repr=False`. LLM messages and agent event snapshots use only `request` and `data` and do not include this in-process state.
`ack` does nothing when `message_id` or `acknowledger` is `None`.
pitfalls: `DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS` (12) applies only to direct construction. `Runtime` always passes `config.MAX_STEPS` (300), so the budget of production runs is governed by config.

The step budget is shared by the whole agent tree and the Harnesses. Child agents and LLM translation in an `ErrorHarness` (such as `FailureNotify._translate_frame`) all call `advance_step` on the same budget.

`ack` does not read `self.message_id`; the caller must pass `ctx.message_id` explicitly. `Runtime` does not ACK; only the dispatch agent's `_execute` calls `ctx.ack` after `_handle` returns normally. When `_handle` raises or the run is cancelled, the message stays pending and is later reclaimed and redelivered by `XAUTOCLAIM`.

`tool_failures` hangs off the shared Context but is partitioned by `current_agent_execution_id`. A child agent's unresolved failures are consumed at the child's own `run` boundary and do not enter the parent agent's `_adjudicate`.
Child agents running in parallel share `data` and `tool_state`. If they read-modify-write the same key across an `await`, they overwrite each other (the convention in `agent/fanout.py`).
The queue process loads this module indirectly through `core.builtin.session_store` → `abc/call.py`, but the queue side does not construct `AgentContext`.
`agents` defaults to `None`: in a directly constructed Context, `call_agent` returns error for every child name, and the LLM does not see any child agents.

modules.role: Defines the `LogRecorder` Protocol, the execution log recording port injected into the base classes, separating the implementation of the recording destination from `BaseAgent` and the LLM wrappers.
modules.summary: `LogRecorder` is a structural `Protocol` with a single coroutine `record(event: LogEvent)`; `LogEvent` comes from `core.builtin.domain.execution_log`. The persistent implementation is `PostgresExecutionLogger` in `core/builtin/execution_log.py`, created by `open_execution_logger()` in `core/builtin/database.py`. `open_host_services` in `core/builtin/app.py` (shared by the runtime's `build_runtime` and the check CLI `core/versioning/__main__.py`) puts it into `HostServices.logger` and also passes it to `build_llms`. `BaseAgent` receives it through the constructor argument `logger` and records `agent`, `tool`, and `harness` events in `_log`. `TrackedLLM` in `llm/tracking.py` records `llm` events, and `tools/review.py` opens its own recorder to write events.
modules.flow: At runtime startup, `build_runtime` opens one recorder and injects it through `HostServices` into every version's agents and all LLM clients. During agent execution, `record` is called once when each Agent, Tool, Harness, or LLM call finishes.

key_symbols.name: LogRecorder
key_symbols.explain: The minimal contract separating the recording destination from the base classes; it requires only a `record` coroutine.

key_symbols.name: LogRecorder.record
key_symbols.explain: Receives a `LogEvent` for a completed execution and records it.

invariants: The contract requires only `async def record(self, event: LogEvent) -> None`. Any object with this signature can be injected; no inheritance is needed.
This module depends only on `core.builtin.domain.execution_log.LogEvent` and does not import the ORM or concrete Stores.
pitfalls: `BaseAgent.run` does `await self._log(...)` outside the try/except, and `TrackedLLM` also does `await self._logger.record(...)` directly, so implementations must swallow write failures themselves. `PostgresExecutionLogger.record` catches `Exception` and only logs it; if an implementation raises, the agent run or LLM call fails.

The `logger` of `BaseAgent` is optional; when it is `None`, `_log` records nothing. The logger does not propagate between parent and child; `build_agents` passes the same logger to every instance in the version.
The Protocol is not declared `runtime_checkable`, so `isinstance(x, LogRecorder)` cannot be used.
The queue process loads this module indirectly through `core.builtin.database` but never opens a recorder.

modules.role: Defines the ABCs for the gates enforced before and after agent execution, `PreHarness` and `PostHarness`, and the reaction hook on failure, `ErrorHarness`.
modules.summary: All three ABCs require subclasses to declare the ClassVars `name` and `description`, and receive the host agent's `LLMClient` at construction, storing it as `self._llm`. `BaseAgent.__init__` instantiates the types declared in the class variables `pre`, `post`, and `on_error` with `harness(llm)` and registers them in declaration order. `BaseAgent.run` evaluates `PreHarness.check(call)` in order before `_execute`: the first Harness that returns `False` or raises an `Exception` makes the run return an error result with a `harness:<name>` note immediately. When `_execute` returns `ok`, `PostHarness.check(call, result)` is evaluated in order; on a veto the result is replaced by an error and the original result is written to the harness log event as `original_result`. When the final result is `error`, `_handle_error` calls `ErrorHarness.handle(call, result)` in order, and exceptions it raises are written only to the warning log and a `failed` event. Harnesses never appear in the LLM prompt or callables. The concrete implementations in the current code are all in `harnesses/failure_notify.py`, and all of them are `ErrorHarness`es: `FailureNotify` (`on_error` of `pr_event`), `IssueFailureNotify` (`on_error` of `issue_investigation`), and `SentryFailureNotify` (`on_error` of `sentry_autofix` and `sentry_autofix_item`).
modules.flow: At version composition, `build_agents` constructs each agent, and each agent instantiates its declared Harnesses in `__init__`. During agent execution, `BaseAgent.run` calls them before and after `_execute` and when the run ends with error.

key_symbols.name: PreHarness
key_symbols.explain: Execution gate evaluated before `_execute`; blocks execution when it returns `False` or raises.

key_symbols.name: PreHarness.__init__
key_symbols.explain: Stores the host agent's `LLMClient` as `self._llm`; all three ABCs are constructed the same way.

key_symbols.name: PreHarness.check
key_symbols.explain: Decides whether this call may run. `True` continues the chain; `False` or an exception short-circuits to an error result.

key_symbols.name: PostHarness
key_symbols.explain: Result gate evaluated only for results with `status="ok"`.

key_symbols.name: PostHarness.check
key_symbols.explain: Observes `(call, result)` without modifying it; vetoes the result when it returns `False` or raises.

key_symbols.name: ErrorHarness
key_symbols.explain: Reaction hook called when a run ends with error, used for failure notifications and the like.

key_symbols.name: ErrorHarness.handle
key_symbols.explain: Reacts to a failed result without modifying it. Exceptions are swallowed at the run boundary and logged.

invariants: The pre, post, and error chains all run in registration order: first the class-declared `pre`/`post`/`on_error`, then those added by `register_*_harness`. Registering a duplicate name is rejected with `ValueError`.
pre and post are fail-closed: an `Exception` raised by `check` counts as a refusal, and the first refusal short-circuits the remaining Harnesses.
post runs only for results with `status="ok"`; after a pre refusal, neither `_execute` nor post runs.

Error Harnesses run only when the final `status="error"`, including pre refusals, post vetoes, converted exceptions, and `fatal_tools` flips; `max_steps` and cancellation do not trigger them. Their exceptions never replace the original failure.
Harnesses are invisible to the LLM and never enter `_build_callables`.
pitfalls: Treating `ctx.data` as read-only, not dispatching agents, claiming the step budget before calling the LLM, and holding no state across runs are all docstring conventions; the framework does not enforce them.

A Harness instance is created once when its agent is constructed and is shared, along with that version's agent instance, by every run of that version, so state that spans runs must not be stored on instance attributes.

A Harness that uses the LLM must first call `call.ctx.advance_step()`; otherwise it bypasses the shared step budget. `FailureNotify` falls back to the original English text when the budget is exhausted or translation fails.

`FailureNotify` delivers the notification by calling `NotifyTool().run(args, ctx=call.ctx)` directly. This path does not go through `call_tool`, so it writes no tool event and nothing to the failure ledger.
The version catalog (`build_catalog` in `core/builtin/catalog.py`, and `declared_harnesses` in `publish_catalog`) lists only `PreHarness`/`PostHarness`; `ErrorHarness` never appears in the catalog.
The `check` signatures of pre and post differ, so one class implements only one stage; when both stages are needed, write two Harnesses.

modules.role: Defines `LLMClient`, the single port between the agent loop and the LLM, along with the value types for messages, call requests, responses, and usage metadata.
modules.summary: An agent builds a list of `Message` (`system`/`user`/`assistant`/`tool`) and calls `LLMClient.respond` with it together with a list of callable metadata in a uniform format for Tools and child agents, receiving an `LLMResponse`, i.e. `FinalAnswer | Calls`. `FinalAnswer` carries the final text; `Calls` carries a set of `Call(name, args)`. This layer does not distinguish Tools from child agents; `BaseAgent._dispatch_calls` routes them by name. `Calls.raw` holds the provider-native assistant message; `BaseAgent` attaches it to the appended assistant `Message.raw`, and `OpenAIChatLLM` replays it verbatim on the next turn to preserve `reasoning_content` and the native tool_call ids. `LLMMetadata` and `LLMUsage` record the provider, model, token usage, request id, and raw response; `TrackedLLM` uses them to record `llm` events and computes cost with `llm/pricing.py`. Concrete implementations live in `trackeverything.llm`, including `OpenAIChatLLM`, `FallbackLLM`, `ThrottledLLM`, and `TrackedLLM`, and `build_llms` in `llm/compose.py` assembles them into four named clients: `max`, `high`, `low`, and `flash`.
modules.flow: At runtime startup, `build_llms` creates the named clients; `build_agents` hands one of them to each agent and its Harnesses according to the agent class's `llm` name. During agent execution, `_respond_one_step` calls `respond` once for each step consumed.

key_symbols.name: Message
key_symbols.explain: One turn of the conversation, holding `role`, `content`, and an optional provider-native message `raw` (for replay).

key_symbols.name: LLMUsage
key_symbols.explain: The input, output, and total token counts reported by the provider, plus the cached input token count and reasoning token count.

key_symbols.name: LLMMetadata
key_symbols.explain: `provider`, `model`, `usage`, `request_id`, and `raw_response`, kept for logging and cost calculation.

key_symbols.name: FinalAnswer
key_symbols.explain: Signal that the LLM is done, holding `text` and `metadata`; on receiving it the agent returns an `ok` result.

key_symbols.name: Call
key_symbols.explain: One call request: `name` is a Tool name or child agent name, and `args` is an argument dict the agent core does not parse.

key_symbols.name: Calls
key_symbols.explain: Signal to execute a set of calls and continue, holding a tuple of `calls`, the provider-native message `raw`, and `metadata`.

key_symbols.name: LLMResponse
key_symbols.explain: Type alias `FinalAnswer | Calls` for one turn of LLM output, distinguished with `isinstance`.

key_symbols.name: LLMClient
key_symbols.explain: The single LLM port, responsible for serializing messages and callables into the provider format and parsing the response into `FinalAnswer` or `Calls`.

key_symbols.name: LLMClient.respond
key_symbols.explain: Returns one `LLMResponse` from the message history and the callable list, without distinguishing Tools from child agents.

invariants: `LLMClient.respond` is an `abstractmethod`; a subclass that does not implement it raises `TypeError` on instantiation.
`Message`, `LLMUsage`, `LLMMetadata`, `FinalAnswer`, `Call`, and `Calls` are all `frozen=True` dataclasses.
`LLMResponse` distinguishes its two variants with `isinstance`; the agent core parses neither strings nor `Call.args`.
Each callable entry has only `name`, `description`, and `arguments`; Tools and child agents have the same shape (`BaseAgent._meta`).
pitfalls: `_respond_one_step` does not convert exceptions raised by `respond`; the `BaseAgent.run` boundary turns them into an error result with an `execution` note. `TrackedLLM` records an error event first and then re-raises; `FallbackLLM` switches to the fallback client only for status codes 429/500/502/503/504, connection errors, or an HTTP 200 body carrying `error` without `choices` (`UpstreamResponseError`).

`OpenAIChatLLM` replays `raw` only when the assistant `content` parses as a JSON list of the form `[{"name", "args"}]` and `raw` contains a `tool_calls` list. Otherwise it reassembles tool_calls from `content`, or treats the message as plain text.
When `ZAI_API_KEY` is not set, `high`, `low`, `flash`, and `flash_low` degrade to the same client instance as `max`.

The docstring of `LLMClient` says the concrete clients live in `trackeverything.core.builtin`, but the actual implementations are in the `trackeverything.llm` package. The provider is chosen by `build_default_llm` in `llm/compose.py`.
Python control paths also reuse `Call` to call Tools; for example, `require_source` calls `call_tool` with `Call("fetch_source", {})`, and this path does not go through `llm_args`.

modules.role: Defines the Source contract ABC: a concrete Source provides the identity and payload of an entity snapshot, plus I/O-free identity derivation and a material view.
modules.summary: A concrete Source implements the coroutines `get_identity` and `get_payload`, plus `get_source_description` and the classmethod `from_config`. `get_project` returns the instance's `_project`: the class attribute defaults to `None`, and concrete Sources set it in `__init__`. `identity_for` and `material_view` are I/O-free classmethods that by default return `None` and the payload unchanged, respectively. `identity_for` is called by two agents: the `github` agent (`agent/github.py`) requires a non-`None` result when handling GitHub events, while the dispatch agent calls it under `suppress` for the Source form of a named run and puts `identity` into `ctx.data` only when a value is derived. The Runtime does not reference Sources. An agent that receives a Source definition calls the fixed tool `fetch_source` through `require_source` at the start of `_execute`: `FetchSourceTool` creates the instance with `from_config(**source_kwargs, project=...)` and writes `identity`, `payload`, `project`, and `source_description` into `ctx.data`. `ProjectMemoryAgent` calls `material_view` through `FetchSourceTool.material_view`. The version's `agent/compose.py` maps source keys to 9 concrete classes with `SOURCES`.
modules.flow: When the `github` agent handles GitHub events and the dispatch agent handles the Source form of a named run, they only perform I/O-free identity derivation. The actual fetch happens during agent execution inside the `fetch_source` Tool called by the agent that receives the Source definition, and happens only once per run.

key_symbols.name: Source
key_symbols.explain: Contract for an entity snapshot whose identity and payload format are defined by the concrete Source. Entry routing is decided by the dispatch agent and the `github` agent (GitHub events through `route_github`), not by the Source.

key_symbols.name: Source.get_identity
key_symbols.explain: Returns a correlation key that is unique and stable within the Source.

key_symbols.name: Source.get_payload
key_symbols.explain: Returns the current entity snapshot as defined by the Source.

key_symbols.name: Source.get_project
key_symbols.explain: Returns the optional project grouping label `_project`.

key_symbols.name: Source.get_source_description
key_symbols.explain: Returns a string describing the Source and the meaning of its payload; `fetch_source` writes it to `ctx.data["source_description"]`.

key_symbols.name: Source.from_config
key_symbols.explain: Abstract classmethod that constructs a Source instance from `source_kwargs`.

key_symbols.name: Source.material_view
key_symbols.explain: Without I/O, reduces the payload to the parts that can change the project material; returns it unchanged by default.

key_symbols.name: Source.identity_for
key_symbols.explain: Without I/O, derives from `source_kwargs` the same value as `get_identity`; returns `None` by default.

invariants: `get_identity`, `get_payload`, `get_source_description`, and `from_config` are `abstractmethod`s; a class cannot be instantiated unless it implements all of them.
`identity_for` and `material_view` are classmethods, and the contract requires them to do no I/O.
An override of `identity_for` must return the same string as `get_identity` for the same locator, but the code does not check that the two agree.
An override of `material_view` must be pure and idempotent, because stored records also pass through the same function.
pitfalls: When `FetchSourceTool` calls `from_config`, it adds a `project` keyword on top of `source_kwargs`, so a concrete `from_config` must accept an optional `project`. If `source_kwargs` itself contains a `project` key, the call fails with a duplicate keyword and is returned as a Tool failure.
`fetch_source` overwrites `ctx.data["project"]` with `src.get_project()`.

The GitHub path of the `github` agent (`agent/github.py`) calls `identity_for` directly and does not swallow exceptions; when it returns `None`, the run fails with `identity cannot be derived`. Sources used by GitHub routing must therefore override it.
Only `GithubPullRequest` overrides `material_view`.

The dispatch agent's named run swallows exceptions from `identity_for` and runs the child agent as usual; unregistered source keys and derivation failures are left for `fetch_source` to record during execution.

The agent core (`BaseAgent`) does not reference Sources. Apart from the concrete Source implementations, Sources are referenced only by the dispatch agent, the `github` agent, `FetchSourceTool`, the version's `agent/compose.py` (`SOURCES`), and `compose` and `catalog` in `core/builtin`.

modules.role: Defines `EventRequest`, the single transport-independent execution request model in the queue, and the ContextVar that records the ID of the message being executed.
modules.summary: `EventRequest` is a pydantic model configured with `extra="forbid", strict=True, frozen=True`, with `kind` (default `event.handle`), `provider` (`github`/`discord`/`slack`/`internal`), `external_id`, `payload`, and the optional `session_id` and `parent_session_id`. The kind of request is expressed by `provider` and `payload`: `github`, `discord`, and `slack` are external events that the intake publishes as raw events; `internal` is a publish from outside the external services, and when `payload` has `agent_name` it is a named run (`agent_name`, an optional `request`, and either `data` or `source` + `source_kwargs` + `project`), otherwise it is the start of auto-development. `kind` keeps its default `event.handle`: `EventRequest`s published by an old queue process around a deploy remain readable, while messages in the old formats (`agent.run`, `source.run`) are judged unreadable. The publishers are the GitHub webhook, Discord, and Slack intake logic in `integration/` and `ScheduleTrigger` (`integration/schedule.py`, in the queue process), which fires on the cron schedules of the `schedule` table, `queue/cli.py`, and the runtime's `auto_submit`, `sentry_submit`, and PR retirement sweep, all publishing through `Producer.publish`. `QueueConsumer.next` reads the stream with `EventRequest.model_validate_json`, and messages that fail validation (including the old formats) are moved to the dead stream. `Runtime._run` does not interpret the content; it hands each request to `config.DISPATCH_AGENT` (`dispatch`) with `data` set to `{"event": {provider, external_id, payload}}`. `REQUEST_ID` holds the stream id of the current message and is set by `Runtime.execute` for the duration of the run.
modules.flow: The queue process's intake logic, the CLI, and the publishers on the runtime side construct or validate requests with this model and `XADD` them to the Redis stream through `Producer.publish`. The runtime process's `QueueConsumer` parses messages with the same model, and `Runtime` converts each into an `AgentContext` and executes the dispatch agent.

key_symbols.name: EventRequest
key_symbols.explain: The single execution request in the queue (`kind="event.handle"`), carrying `provider`, `external_id` (1-256 characters), `payload`, and the session, and interpreted by the dispatch agent. For `internal`, the presence or absence of `agent_name` in `payload` distinguishes a named run from the start of auto-development.

key_symbols.name: REQUEST_ID
key_symbols.explain: Queue stream id of the message being executed (the ContextVar is named `logical_request_id`), set by `Runtime.execute` for the duration of the run; `auto_submit` and `sentry_submit` read it and uses it as the parent message to build the `external_id`.

invariants: Requests forbid extra fields, use strict types, and are immutable after creation (`extra="forbid", strict=True, frozen=True`); the top level cannot carry trusted values such as `authorization` or `run_id`.
`external_id` is 1-256 characters long; `provider` can only be `github`, `discord`, `slack`, or `internal`; `kind` accepts only `event.handle`.
Requests do not carry a run ID; `run_id` is issued only by `Runtime._run` with `new_id()`.

All publishers share the single publish entry point `Producer.publish(EventRequest)`; `publish --file` in `queue/cli.py` accepts JSON for any provider, and the `data` in the dead stream can be republished as is.
`REQUEST_ID` defaults to `None`. `Runtime._read_loop` first sets it to `None` in each run's new context; `Runtime.execute` sets it to the message id during execution and resets it at the end.
pitfalls: `frozen=True` only forbids reassigning fields; dicts such as `payload` remain mutable. `Runtime` copies them with `dict(...)` and `deepcopy` before putting them into the `AgentContext`.
The queue does not deduplicate by `external_id` (`Producer` does no deduplication). `external_id` is handed to the dispatch agent only as part of `ctx.data["event"]`.

Publishing validates only the top-level fields, not the contents of `payload` (including `agent_name`, `data`, and `source` of a named run): an undeclared `agent_name` can still be published, and the dispatch agent ends it with error at execution time and ACKs it.

`REQUEST_ID` has a value only inside a run in the runtime process; `auto_submit` rejects with `ValueError` when it cannot read it. The ContextVar's name is `logical_request_id`, which differs from the variable name.
Messages that fail validation (including the old formats `agent.run` and `source.run`) are moved to the dead stream by `QueueConsumer` and never reach agent execution.

modules.role: Defines the Tool execution contract ABC `Tool`, and `ToolResult`, which returns success or failure as a value.
modules.summary: A concrete Tool declares the ClassVars `name`, `description`, and `arguments` (the argument JSON Schema), and implements `run(args, *, ctx=None) -> ToolResult` as a coroutine. `BaseAgent.__init__` instantiates the types in the class variable `tools` without arguments; Tools that need dependencies (such as `FetchSourceTool`) are constructed by the version's `agent/compose.py` and registered through `register`; `agent/compose.py` also constructs one shared instance of each base tool in `BASE_TOOLS` (`shell`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`) and registers it on every agent instance through `register`, so an agent's `tools` must not declare a Tool with the same name. For LLM-initiated calls, `BaseAgent._dispatch` first converts the arguments with `llm_args` and then passes them to `call_tool`; Python control code calls `call_tool` directly. `call_tool` converts leaked exceptions to `ToolResult(ok=False)`, uses `error_key(args)` as the target key to record the failure or resolve failures for the same target in `ctx.tool_failures`, and then records the `tool` event. `error_key` defaults to the canonical JSON of all arguments; `tools/skill.py`, `tools/docs/write.py`, `tools/files.py` (the base file Tools target `path`), and several Tools under `tools/project/` override it with a narrower target, while `tools/memory/store.py` overrides `llm_args`.
modules.flow: During agent execution, a `Call` returned by the LLM or a call from Python control runs a Tool through `BaseAgent.call_tool`. The result goes back to the LLM as a `tool`-role message, and unrecovered failures are arbitrated by `_adjudicate` at the run boundary.

key_symbols.name: ToolResult
key_symbols.explain: Immutable execution result holding the success flag `ok`, the observed `output`, and the failure description `error`.

key_symbols.name: Tool
key_symbols.explain: Shared ABC for Tools that declares callable metadata (same shape as child agents) and implements `run`.

key_symbols.name: Tool.llm_args
key_symbols.explain: Converts arguments from the LLM without side effects; returns them unchanged by default. Calls from Python control do not go through it.

key_symbols.name: Tool.run
key_symbols.explain: Runs the Tool itself and returns success or failure as a `ToolResult`. `ctx` is injected by the Python side and can read and write the shared `data`.

key_symbols.name: Tool.error_key
key_symbols.explain: Returns the target key for failure tracking; `None` means a failure with no clear target (unaddressed).

invariants: `run` is an `abstractmethod`; a concrete Tool that does not implement it cannot be instantiated.
`ctx` is a keyword-only argument injected by the Python side and never appears in the LLM's JSON arguments.
`ToolResult` is a `frozen=True` dataclass holding `ok`, `output`, and `error`.

`error_key` returns `json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)` by default, so a failure is resolved only by a later success with the same arguments; a failure whose key is `None` is resolved by any success of the same Tool (`ToolFailures.resolve`).
pitfalls: Only `BaseAgent.call_tool` turns exceptions into failure values and updates the failure ledger and the tool event. In code that calls `Tool.run` directly (such as `FailureNotify` calling `NotifyTool().run`), exceptions propagate as is and leave no record.
`llm_args` applies only to LLM-initiated calls; `call_tool` calls from Python control do not go through it.

Tools declared in the class variable `tools` must be constructible without arguments; Tools that need injected dependencies must be constructed at composition time and then passed to `register`. `register` raises `ValueError` when the name duplicates an already registered Tool.
The docstring of `run` requires I/O to be done with `await`, with no synchronous calls that block the event loop.
