diagram.caption: This diagram shows how the `core/abc` contracts connect within one execution: an `EventRequest` reaches `Runtime._run` through the Redis stream and becomes the shared `AgentContext` and the entry `AgentCall`; `BaseAgent.run` ties together the LLM, Tools, Sources, Harnesses, and the execution log; the returned `AgentResult` is recorded by the `Runtime`; and the ACK returns to the queue through `ctx.ack`.

groups.overview: This group is the execution and composition layer of the runtime process (`python -m trackeverything.core.builtin`, started by `scripts/start_runtime.sh`). `__main__.py` calls `app.serve`. `app.py` is the composition root: it assembles the LLM clients, execution log, and session store with `open_host_services`, builds the component version store `Repo` (`open_repo`, whose default store is the `GitVersionStore` over the bare mirror of the component repository, plus `prepare_components`) and loads the mirror's main, connects the queue package's `QueueConsumer`/`Producer`, installs that `Producer` in `queue/child.py` for the child requests of components, and handles startup preparation, the 30-second maintenance tick, the periodic sync with the component repository (`repo.sync()` every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`), and shutdown. `Runtime` in `runtime.py` is the execution center: within the concurrency limit it reads execution requests from the queue one at a time; for each message it first confirms the mirror's main with `repo.refresh()`, then pins the dispatch version with the run handle `repo.run()`, builds the `AgentContext`, records the `session_run` (runs of the same session also execute in parallel), runs the dispatch agent under `RUN_TIMEOUT`, and calls `repo.release(run)` at the end. ACK is left to the dispatch agent; reclaiming (`XAUTOCLAIM`), the delivery limit, and the dead stream belong to `QueueConsumer`/`RedisStream` on the queue side. `compose.py` defines the `HostServices` the Host passes to the version's `agent/compose.py`, the `ComponentGraph` it returns, and `build_agents`, which instantiates agents by name; `catalog.py` converts main's component graph into catalog values. `process_registry.py` (the entry point for Tools that start subprocesses) and `callable_mesh.py` (the experimental full-mesh wiring for `AGENT_FULL_MESH`) are Host-side helpers used by version-owned components.

modules.role: Initialization module of the `core.builtin` package; it only describes the package's responsibilities in a docstring.
modules.summary: Has no public names and imports no modules. The docstring states: the package is responsible for execution, sessions, logs, errors, and the instance composition of core; `Runtime` manages units of work, and `app` assembles queue consumption, LLMs, and connections; concrete Agents, Tools, and Sources are used through the version's composition module.
modules.flow: Executed as package initialization whenever any `trackeverything.core.builtin.*` submodule is imported; it takes no part in the runtime flow itself.

modules.role: Module entry point of the runtime process; running `python -m trackeverything.core.builtin` starts consumption and execution.
modules.summary: `main` first calls `trackeverything.process.configure_logging`, which writes logs to standard error in the shared format (`logging.basicConfig` does not specify `stream`, so the default `StreamHandler` writes to `sys.stderr`; the docstring of `configure_logging` says "standard output", which does not match the actual behavior), and then runs `app.serve` with `asyncio.run(serve())` until it returns. `scripts/start_runtime.sh` runs this module in the foreground through `scripts/run_local.sh`. The module imports only `app.serve` and `configure_logging`, and does not import the queue process's HTTP, `api`, or Discord/Slack intake (`tests/queue/test_lifecycle.py` checks this).
modules.flow: Sits at the outermost layer of the runtime process: the startup script runs it, and it hands control to `app.serve`.

key_symbols.name: main
key_symbols.explain: Configures logging and then runs the whole runtime process with `asyncio.run(serve())`; called when `__name__ == "__main__"`.

invariants: The entry point does not import `trackeverything.api`, `trackeverything.integration.discord`, or `trackeverything.integration.slack`.
The whole process has a single event loop created by `asyncio.run`, shared by every component in `serve`.
pitfalls: `main` itself does not handle signals; SIGTERM/SIGINT are registered by `run_host` inside `serve` to trigger shutdown.

modules.role: Composition root of the runtime process: assembles the shared services (`open_host_services`), the component version store `Repo`, `QueueConsumer`/`Producer`, the maintenance tick, and the periodic sync with the component repository, and handles startup preparation and shutdown; the check CLI also uses its `open_host_services`.
modules.summary: `serve` runs `require_schema_head`, `prepare_runtime_environment`, and `load_code_version` in order, closes `session_run` rows still `running` from before startup as `interrupted` with `recover_interrupted_runs`, calls `build_runtime`, then runs `prepare_runtime_state` and `publish_catalog`, and keeps running through `run_host` until it receives SIGTERM/SIGINT. `open_host_services` gathers the execution log, the four LLM clients `max`/`high`/`low`/`flash` returned by `build_llms`, the session store, `config.AGENT_FULL_MESH`, and the Skill directory override into `HostServices` (no I/O at construction); the runtime and the check CLI (`core/versioning/__main__.py`) create it with the same function. `build_runtime` creates this process's version store singleton with `open_repo(prepare_components(services))` (by default a `GitVersionStore` over the mirror `COMPONENT_REPO_DIR`) and runs `await repo.start()`: it loads the mirror's main, and when the mirror has none it fetches GitHub's main, loads it, and adopts it; on failure it closes the version store and raises, aborting startup. It then creates the `QueueConsumer` with the `RedisStream` from `Producer.from_env()` and assembles a not-yet-started `TrackingRuntime` with `sync_interval=config.COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL` (the environment variable `RUN_CONCURRENCY` can override the concurrency). Before assembling, it creates an `Optimizer` with `services.llms` and `read_recent_runs` bound to `config.DATABASE_URL` (the optimizer gets main from the version store singleton) and calls `install`; only the runtime process holds it (`optimizer` is not in `ENTRANCES` but a child agent declared by dispatch: a named run is delegated by dispatch to `OptimizerAgent`, which calls `optimizer.handle()`). On top of `Runtime`, `TrackingRuntime` runs two periodic tasks through `_every`: the maintenance tick every `RECONCILE_INTERVAL` (30 seconds; `publish_catalog` and `stream.heartbeat`) and `repo.sync()` every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL` (300 seconds), which fetches GitHub's main and adopts it when it loads. `publish_catalog` builds the catalog snapshot from the component graph of the loaded main (`repo.main_version`) and the loaded modules, uses main's `label` as `code_version`, and writes it to Redis through `save_catalog` for the queue process's catalog API to read; the tick calls neither `refresh` nor `sync`. `prepare_runtime_state` only calls `child.install(runtime.producer)`, so that components can publish requests with the running message as parent through `publish_child` in `queue/child.py`. This module imports and calls no component module (`agent/`, `tools/`, `skills/`, `harnesses/`, `sources/`); daily component maintenance runs as the agent `maintenance`, started from the `schedule` table.
modules.flow: Handles startup, shutdown, periodic maintenance, and the component repository sync of the runtime process, connecting the queue package's `QueueConsumer`/`Producer` and `queue/child.py`, the `llm` package's clients, and the component version store to `Runtime`.

key_symbols.name: TrackingRuntime
key_symbols.explain: Application composition that adds the maintenance tick, the component repository sync, and a `producer` reference on top of `Runtime`; its constructor arguments are `queue`, `repo`, `sessions`, `tick_hook`, `reconcile_interval` (default `config.RECONCILE_INTERVAL`, 30 seconds), `sync_interval` (default 0, which disables the sync; `build_runtime` passes `config.COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`), and `concurrency`.

key_symbols.name: TrackingRuntime.start
key_symbols.explain: After running `Runtime.start`, creates the `_every` task of the maintenance tick when `tick_hook` exists and the interval is positive, and the `_every` task of `_sync` when `sync_interval` is positive.

key_symbols.name: TrackingRuntime._sync
key_symbols.explain: Calls `repo.sync()`: fetches GitHub's main and adopts it when it loads.

key_symbols.name: TrackingRuntime._every
key_symbols.explain: The periodic loop shared by the tick and the sync: waits on the stop event for `interval`; if not stopped, awaits `action()`, and on an exception logs `<label> failed` (`runtime maintenance failed` or `component repository sync failed`) and continues to the next round.

key_symbols.name: TrackingRuntime.stop
key_symbols.explain: Sets the stop event and waits for both periodic tasks to end (including a round in progress), then runs `Runtime.stop`, and finally calls `producer.close()` in `finally`.

key_symbols.name: _skills_override
key_symbols.explain: Returns the resolved path only when `config.SKILLS_DIR` is set (non-empty); otherwise returns `None` so each version's own `skills` file view is used.

key_symbols.name: open_host_services
key_symbols.explain: Assembles the `HostServices` shared by all versions: the execution log, the four named clients from `build_llms(logger)`, the session store, `full_mesh`, and `skills_root`. Shared by the runtime and the check CLI; no I/O at construction.

key_symbols.name: build_runtime
key_symbols.explain: Calls `open_host_services`, creates the `Repo` with `open_repo` and runs `start()` (on failure it calls `close` and re-raises), and returns a not-yet-started `TrackingRuntime` connected to the `QueueConsumer` and `Producer`, with the maintenance tick and `sync_interval=config.COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`.

key_symbols.name: build_runtime._tick_maintenance
key_symbols.explain: Body of the maintenance tick: runs `publish_catalog` and `producer.stream.heartbeat()` in order. Component maintenance is not here; the `maintenance` agent runs it daily from the `schedule` table.

key_symbols.name: publish_catalog
key_symbols.explain: Builds the catalog from `graph.agents`, `graph.sources`, and `graph.entrances` of `repo.main_version` and the Agents/Tools/Harnesses declared in that version's loaded modules, with `config.DISPATCH_AGENT` as `webhook_entrances`, adds `code_version` (main's `label`), `as_of`, and `entrances`, and writes it to Redis with `save_catalog`; does nothing when there is no `producer`.

key_symbols.name: prepare_runtime_state
key_symbols.explain: Installs the runtime's `Producer` in `queue/child.py` with `child.install(runtime.producer)`; components then publish child requests with `publish_child`.

key_symbols.name: serve
key_symbols.explain: Main flow of the runtime process: check the schema, prepare the environment, resolve the code version, reclaim interrupted runs, assemble (load main), install the child-request Producer, publish the catalog, and run through `run_host`. In `finally` it calls `runtime.stop()` and then `runtime.repo.close()` (which also releases the loaded versions and file views when startup fails before the start).

invariants: When the mirror's main cannot be loaded (including when the mirror has none and GitHub's main cannot be fetched or loaded), `build_runtime` closes the version store and raises, aborting startup. Startup is likewise refused when a deploy changes a Host contract (such as the arguments of `build_agents`) so that the adopted main no longer loads; deploy such a change in a form the current components still load with and push the components afterwards (to recover, push a main that loads and point the mirror's `refs/heads/main` at it).

Before message intake starts (`run_host` calls `start`), the schema head check, reclaiming of interrupted runs, loading of main, installing the child-request Producer, and catalog publishing are all complete.

The Host imports and calls no component module: the maintenance tick only publishes the catalog and the heartbeat, startup preparation only installs the Producer in `queue/child.py`, and component code runs only from versions of the version store.
Order of `TrackingRuntime.stop`: stop the maintenance tick and the sync and wait for a round in progress → `Runtime.stop` (drain, close the version store) → `producer.close()` in `finally`.
`QueueConsumer` and `Producer` share the same `RedisStream`, i.e. the same Redis client.

`child.install` stores the Producer in the module-level `_producer` of the Host module `queue/child.py`; the components of every version import that one Host module, so they all publish through the same Producer.
pitfalls: `TrackingRuntime.stop` is called twice (in the `finally` of `run_host` and the `finally` of `serve`); `Runtime.stop` stays idempotent through `_started`, but `producer.close()` runs every time.

If `prepare_runtime_state` or `publish_catalog` fails before `start`, `Runtime.stop` returns immediately because it has not started, and `repo.close` does not run; the version store is instead released by `runtime.repo.close()` in the `finally` of `serve`.

When `publish_catalog` raises in the maintenance tick, `heartbeat` is skipped for that round; when the heartbeat has not been updated for more than 60 seconds, the queue-side catalog shows `online` as false.
The `RUN_CONCURRENCY` environment variable is read only in `build_runtime`; constructing `TrackingRuntime`/`Runtime` directly uses `config.RUN_CONCURRENCY` (20).
`recover_interrupted_runs` closes every `running` row from before startup as `interrupted`, which assumes only one runtime process runs against the same database.

The runtime does not read component files from a checkout, and `process.restart_roles` does not special-case the five folders: components change by a push to the component repository's main, which the periodic `sync` adopts within `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL` without a restart. When `SKILLS_DIR` is set, Skills are read from that fixed location and do not switch with versions.

`_tick_maintenance` references, in a closure, the `runtime` that is assigned only later in `build_runtime` (`producer` is assigned before the closure is defined), so it can be called by the tick only after `build_runtime` returns.
Changing this module is a Host-side change; `process.restart_roles` restarts only the runtime role.

The catalog reflects only the loaded main: after a push and until `sync` adopts it (or a message's `refresh` loads a new mirror main), the catalog still shows the old main's `label`; the next tick publishes the new one.
`sync_interval` defaults to 0 (no sync) when `TrackingRuntime` is constructed directly; only `build_runtime` passes `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`.

modules.role: Experimental full-mesh wiring used when `AGENT_FULL_MESH` is enabled, letting every agent in a version call all of that version's Tools and agents.
modules.summary: `wire_full_mesh(agents)` receives all of a version's agents (name → instance), collects by Tool name the first Tool instance encountered during traversal (`setdefault`), and passes this set of Tools and all non-empty agent names to each agent's `BaseAgent.extend_callables(tools, names)`: already declared entries with the same name take precedence, and an agent never adds its own name. Only names are added for child agents, and at execution time they are obtained by name through `ctx.agents` just like declared children. The function returns `(tool_count, agent_count)`. It is called by `build` in the version-owned `agent/compose.py` when `services.full_mesh` is true, after `fetch_source` and the base tools are injected and before `bind_skills`.
modules.flow: Runs once whenever a version builds its component graph (`agent/compose.build`), and changes the agents' callable sets only when `HostServices.full_mesh` (`config.AGENT_FULL_MESH`) is true.

key_symbols.name: wire_full_mesh
key_symbols.explain: Collects the Tool instances shared within the version and all agent names, adds them to each agent through `extend_callables`, and returns the number of Tools and the number of agent names.

invariants: Never removes or replaces declared Tools and child agent names; it only adds missing names.

The added Tools are shared instances: a Tool with a given name is the same object across all agents. Only names are added for child agents, and instances are provided by the run handle at execution time.
An agent is never added as its own child agent (compared by name).
Cyclic delegation is bounded by the shared step budget (`MAX_STEPS`) and `MAX_AGENT_DEPTH` (16); when nesting gets too deep, `BaseAgent.run` returns a structured `error` result.
pitfalls: Among different Tool instances with the same name, only the one encountered first in `agents` dict order is kept.
Names added by the mesh appear in `list_agent_names()`, so the catalog's parent-child relationships and the `read_skill` conflict check in `bind_skills` both reflect the post-mesh wiring.

`fetch_source` and the base tools are registered before the mesh, so they are shared with all agents; `bind_skills` runs after the mesh, and `read_skill` is still registered per agent and does not enter the shared set.
`agent/compose.build` does not use the return value.

modules.role: Converts a version's component graph (in the runtime, the loaded main) and the classes declared in that version into catalog pydantic values (`CatalogView`).
modules.summary: `build_catalog` iterates over all of the version's agents (`graph_agents`), links Tools and Harnesses with `list_tools`, `list_pre_harnesses`, and `list_post_harnesses`, looks up child agents in the same dict with `list_agent_names()` and records parent-child pairs (names not in the dict are skipped), and assembles each agent's entrance, parent-child, Tool, and Harness links, plus the Tools' `used_by` and the Harnesses' `guards`; names in `entrances` become the respective agents' `entrances`. It then appends the declared classes passed as arguments that are not yet linked as unlinked entries; for declared agents, child agents, Tools, pre, and post are derived from the class attributes `agents`, `tools`, `pre`, and `post`. Display module names strip the prefix `_te_versions.v_<version id>.` of the version-reserved namespace, and a Source's description is the first paragraph of its docstring. `_declared_in` collects declared classes only from modules the version has already loaded and performs no new imports. The runtime's `publish_catalog` (`core/builtin/app.py`) calls these functions on `repo.main_version` with `graph.entrances` as `entrances` and `(config.DISPATCH_AGENT,)` as `webhook_entrances`, adds `code_version` (main's `label`), `as_of`, and `entrances`, and writes the result to Redis through `save_catalog`; the queue's `GET /api/catalog` only reads that snapshot and adds `online` based on the heartbeat.
modules.flow: When the runtime's `serve` starts, and in `publish_catalog` on every maintenance tick, the catalog is built from the loaded main and saved as a Redis snapshot.

key_symbols.name: ToolView
key_symbols.explain: A Tool's LLM-facing contract (`name`, `description`, `arguments`), its origin (`module`, `cls`), and the agents that use it (`used_by`).

key_symbols.name: HarnessView
key_symbols.explain: A Harness's `phase` (`pre`/`post`), origin, and the agents it guards (`guards`).

key_symbols.name: AgentView
key_symbols.explain: An agent's metadata plus its `entrances` (its own name when the version lists it as an entrance), `parents`, `children`, `tools`, `pre`, and `post` links.

key_symbols.name: SourceView
key_symbols.explain: The `key`, docstring summary, and origin of a registered Source class.

key_symbols.name: CatalogView
key_symbols.explain: Outer layer of the catalog, holding four lists (`agents`, `tools`, `harnesses`, `sources`) and `webhook_entrances`.

key_symbols.name: _doc_summary
key_symbols.explain: Joins the first paragraph of a docstring into a single line.

key_symbols.name: _meta_name
key_symbols.explain: Returns the `name` attribute as the display name, falling back to an alternative name (the class name) when it is empty.

key_symbols.name: _module_name
key_symbols.explain: Strips the `_te_versions.v_<version id>.` prefix from a class's module name.

key_symbols.name: _declared_in
key_symbols.explain: Collects, from modules the version has already loaded and without new imports, the public subclasses defined under the given package, sorted by class name and module.

key_symbols.name: build_catalog
key_symbols.explain: `build_catalog(graph_agents, sources, entrances, *, webhook_entrances, declared_agents, declared_tools, declared_harnesses)`: aggregates the links of all agents in the version and the unlinked declared classes, and returns a `CatalogView`.

key_symbols.name: build_catalog.agent_entry
key_symbols.explain: Gets or creates the `AgentView` by name and records the instance's class as linked.

key_symbols.name: build_catalog.wire_tools
key_symbols.explain: Records an agent's Tools in both `AgentView.tools` and `ToolView.used_by`.

key_symbols.name: build_catalog.wire_harnesses
key_symbols.explain: Records an agent's pre/post Harnesses in both `AgentView.pre`/`post` and `HarnessView.guards`.

invariants: Each agent in the version is registered only once, and child agents are looked up only by name in the same dict, so shared or cyclic children never cause repeated traversal.
Agents and Tools are keyed uniquely by name, and Harnesses by `(name, phase)`; later occurrences of the same key merge into the existing entry, and list items are appended without duplicates.
A declared class is not appended if it is already a linked class or an entry with the same key already exists.
`_declared_in` collects only subclasses that are defined in that module, whose names do not start with `_`, and that are not the base class itself.
Sorting: agents with an entrance first and then by name, Tools by name, Harnesses by phase and then by name, Sources by key, and `webhook_entrances` deduplicated and sorted.
This module only reads agent instances and classes; it never modifies the component graph.
pitfalls: Different classes with the same name are merged into one entry, keeping the module and description of the class encountered first.
`_declared_in` is a private name, but `core/builtin/app.py` and `optimizer/consolidation.py` import and use it directly.
The phase of a declared Harness is decided only by whether it derives from `PreHarness`; everything else counts as `post`. `ErrorHarness` (`on_error`) does not enter the catalog.

When `full_mesh` is on, `list_agent_names` and `list_tools` include the names and shared instances added by `extend_callables`, so the catalog's parent-child links and `used_by` reflect the post-mesh wiring.

The field names of `CatalogView` are a shared contract among the Redis snapshot, the defaults in `RedisStream.catalog`, and `api/static/js/catalog*.js`; renaming a field requires changing the readers too.

modules.role: Defines the shared services the Host passes to the version's composition module (`HostServices`) and the composition result (`ComponentGraph`), and provides `build_agents`, which builds agent instances by name, `prepare_components`, the component graph builder handed to the version store, and `StaticAgents`, a run handle backed by a fixed mapping.
modules.summary: The Host does not import concrete Agents, Tools, or Sources. `prepare_components(services)` returns `prepare(version)`: it takes `trackeverything.agent.compose` from that version's namespace through `version.module(COMPOSE_MODULE)`, calls its `build(services, skills_root=...)` with `services.skills_root` (the version file view's `skills` when unspecified), and raises `TypeError` if the return value is not a `ComponentGraph`. The version-side `build` passes the list of agent classes and the dedicated dependencies keyed by agent name (`history` for `project_qa` and `general`, and `sources` for `dispatch` and `github`) to `build_agents`. `build_agents` checks, in list order, that each class's `name` is non-empty and unique and that `cls.llm` is in `llms`, and creates exactly one instance per name with `cls(llms[cls.llm], logger=logger, **dependencies[cls.name])`; it then rejects dependencies pointing to nonexistent names and validates that the child names in each instance's `list_agent_names()` are all in the list. It does not bind child instances; child agents are obtained by name through `ctx.agents` at execution time. `HostServices.llms` maps tier names to clients: `open_host_services` in `core/builtin/app.py` creates the four clients `max`, `high`, `low`, and `flash` with `build_llms` in `llm/compose.py`, and each agent class picks one with `llm` (default `max`). `ComponentGraph` holds all of the version's agents (`agents`), the entrances that queue requests can start by name (`entrances`, currently only `dispatch`; a name not in `agents` raises `ValueError` at construction), and the mapping from source keys to Source classes (`sources`). `StaticAgents` is the `AgentLookup` for scripts and tests that bypass the version store.
modules.flow: When the version store loads a version (`Repo._load`, in a thread), it calls `prepare` after loading all of that version's modules; the version's `agent/compose.build` calls `build_agents` inside it, and the resulting `ComponentGraph` is stored as `version.graph`. The Runtime reads the entrance from the version pinned by the run handle, `publish_catalog` reads main's component graph, and the check CLI validates a commit with the same function.

key_symbols.name: COMPOSE_MODULE
key_symbols.explain: Logical name `trackeverything.agent.compose` of the version-owned composition module.

key_symbols.name: SYSTEM_PATH
key_symbols.explain: Path `agent/SYSTEM.md` of the version-owned text that `prepare` binds to every agent with `configure_system`; `_respond_one_step` puts it in front of each LLM call. The optimizer never writes it.

key_symbols.name: SYSTEM_LIMIT
key_symbols.explain: Upper bound (8000) on the characters of `agent/SYSTEM.md` after stripping surrounding whitespace; a longer or non-UTF-8 file fails the version's composition with `ValueError`.

key_symbols.name: HostServices
key_symbols.explain: Host services shared by all versions (frozen): `llms` (tier name → `LLMClient`; `build_llms` provides `max`, `high`, `low`, `flash`, `flash_low`), `logger`, `session_store`, `full_mesh` (default `False`), and `skills_root` (the fixed location when `SKILLS_DIR` is set; default `None`, meaning each version's file view).

key_symbols.name: ComponentGraph
key_symbols.explain: A version's component graph (frozen): `agents` (all of the version's agents, name → `BaseAgent`), `entrances` (the entrances that queue requests can start by name), and `sources` (source key → `type[Source]`, read by the catalog).

key_symbols.name: ComponentGraph.__post_init__
key_symbols.explain: Raises `ValueError` (`unknown entrances: ...`) when `entrances` contains a name not in `agents`.

key_symbols.name: StaticAgents
key_symbols.explain: An `AgentLookup` that returns agents by name from a fixed mapping. It is not tied to a version; a script or test uses it to pass the result of `build_agents` to `AgentContext.agents`.

key_symbols.name: StaticAgents.agent
key_symbols.explain: Returns the instance from the mapping, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: build_agents
key_symbols.explain: Creates one instance per name (checking names, duplicates, LLM tier, and dependency targets), then validates that the child names each instance declares are all in the list. Returns a dict of name → instance; any inconsistency is rejected with `ValueError`. Child instances are not bound.

key_symbols.name: prepare_components
key_symbols.explain: Wraps `HostServices` and returns the per-version component graph builder handed to `Repo`.

key_symbols.name: prepare_components.prepare
key_symbols.explain: Takes the composition module from the version namespace, determines `skills_root`, calls its `build`, checks that the return value is a `ComponentGraph`, and returns it.

invariants: The composition module is read from that version's namespace through `version.module(COMPOSE_MODULE)`; the Host never imports the canonical `trackeverything.agent.compose`.
`HostServices` and `ComponentGraph` are frozen dataclasses, and all versions share the same `HostServices`.

`build_agents` creates only one instance per name, and the return value includes instances that serve only as child agents. `ComponentGraph.agents` is all of the version's instances, and `entrances` is only the subset of names the Runtime can start (`ENTRANCES` in `agent/compose.py`, currently only `dispatch`).
An agent's LLM client is decided once at construction by `llms[cls.llm]`.

The failure conditions of `build_agents` are all `ValueError`: a class without `name`, a duplicate name, `cls.llm` not in `llms`, `dependencies` containing an agent name not in the list, or a declared child name not in the list. `ComponentGraph` `entrances` containing a name not in `agents` is also a `ValueError`.

A version that fails to build is never adopted or kept: `sync` does not adopt GitHub's main, `fork` keeps no fork ref, `merge` pushes nothing, and the check CLI exits with 1. If loading main fails at startup, startup is aborted; if loading fails during `refresh`, the already loaded main keeps being used.
pitfalls: The dependency name check happens after all instances are created, so when an unknown dependency name exists, every class's constructor has already run once. Dependency keys are the agent's `name`, not the class name; a dependency argument the class's `__init__` does not accept produces a `TypeError`, which likewise fails the preparation.

`build_agents` does not detect cycles in declarations (A declaring B and B declaring A both pass); at run time, `MAX_AGENT_DEPTH` (16) in `core/abc/agent.py` limits the delegation depth. Duplicate names in one parent agent's `agents` are deduplicated in `BaseAgent.__init__` without an error.

`HostServices.llms` must contain every tier name declared by the agent classes. Without `ZAI_API_KEY`, `high`, `low`, `flash`, `flash_low`, and `max` from `build_llms` are the same client, so the tier declaration does not change the actual model.

The fields of `ComponentGraph` and the arguments of `build_agents` are a contract between the Host and stored versions: the Runtime reads `graph.entrances` and `graph.agents`, `publish_catalog` reads `agents`, `sources`, and `entrances`, and `Repo._load` sets each agent's `version_label`. Changing them can make the adopted main incompatible with the new Host, so the runtime refuses to start; deploy such a change in a form the current components still load with, then push the components (the pre-push hook checks them with the deployed Host).
`full_mesh`, `fetch_source` injection, and Skill binding are handled by the version's `build` after `build_agents`; `build_agents` itself does not read `HostServices`.
`StaticAgents` does not pin a version and is not counted as a user of the version store; it is only for scripts and tests.

modules.role: Single entry point for Tools to start subprocesses; a thin wrapper around `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`/`create_subprocess_shell`.
modules.summary: `spawn_exec` and `spawn_shell` forward all arguments unchanged and return an `asyncio.subprocess.Process`; they do not register, track, or reap child processes. On normal completion, timeout, or cancellation, the caller reaps them with `stop_process_group` in `core/builtin/base_tools.py`, which sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL through `os.killpg` and `wait`s for the process. The callers are the Host base tool `bash`, the Host helpers `run_captured` / `run_bounded`, and component Tools such as `tools/skill.py`; all of them start subprocesses with `start_new_session=True` so they can be terminated by process group.
modules.flow: Called during an agent run when a Tool needs to execute an external command (shell, git, scripts, code execution).

key_symbols.name: spawn_exec
key_symbols.explain: Calls `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*args, **kwargs)` directly and returns the process object.

key_symbols.name: spawn_shell
key_symbols.explain: Calls `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(*args, **kwargs)` directly and returns the process object.

invariants: The module keeps no state; the caller is fully responsible for the child process's lifecycle.
It is a Host-side module (`core/builtin`): Tools in all versions share the same implementation, and it does not switch with component versions.
pitfalls: Despite "registry" in the name, it does not register child processes or reap them at startup; child processes left behind after a crash are not cleaned up by this module.
When the caller does not pass `start_new_session=True`, `os.killpg(process.pid, ...)` in `stop_process_group` cannot terminate the whole subtree by process group.

modules.role: The Host-owned base tools `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `bash` that `BaseAgent` builds into every instance, and the shared base helpers every agent's Tools use: process execution with deadlines, output caps and process-group reaping, and text windows.
modules.summary: Implements the four pi-style base tools. File paths are absolute, `~`-based, or relative to the workspace root `REPOS_DIR` (`service_path`, which creates the root when missing); text is UTF-8 and line endings are kept; disk work runs in `asyncio.to_thread`; failures become `ToolResult`s whose tracked target is `path` or `command`. `read` returns up to `limit` lines from line `offset` (1-based) capped by `READ_CHARS`, with the total line count and `next_offset`; `write` creates or replaces a whole file and its parent directories; `edit` replaces `old_text` only when it matches exactly once; `bash` runs `/bin/bash` in a new session from the workspace root with the full service environment, keeps the last `OUTPUT_CHARS` characters of the combined output, and on completion, timeout, or cancellation stops the process group with `stop_process_group`. Deletion goes through `bash`. `shared_tools()` creates one instance per tool for the whole process, and `BaseAgent.__init__` registers them before the agent's own Tools, so a component Tool with a base tool name fails composition. Version updates and optimizer repairs never change these tools. The module imports no component code. The same module provides the shared base helpers that component Tools import instead of carrying copies: `run_captured` and `run_bounded` (child processes with a deadline, an output cap, and process-group reaping), `stop_process_group`, `text_window`, and `bounded_int`.
modules.flow: Registered on every agent instance when a version is composed; called during an agent run through `call_tool` like any other Tool.

key_symbols.name: READ_LINES
key_symbols.explain: Default number of lines `read` returns (2000).

key_symbols.name: READ_CHARS
key_symbols.explain: Upper bound on the characters one `read` returns (50,000); lines beyond it move to `next_offset`.

key_symbols.name: OUTPUT_CHARS
key_symbols.explain: Number of trailing characters of the combined `bash` output that are kept (50,000).

key_symbols.name: BASH_TIMEOUT
key_symbols.explain: Default `bash` timeout in seconds (120).

key_symbols.name: BASH_TIMEOUT_MAX
key_symbols.explain: Largest `timeout` a `bash` call may request (3600 seconds).

key_symbols.name: service_path
key_symbols.explain: Resolves an absolute, `~`-based, or workspace-relative path; relative paths are placed under `REPOS_DIR`, which is created when missing.

key_symbols.name: stop_process_group
key_symbols.explain: Sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to a child's process group and reaps the child; a group that is already gone is tolerated. Components that start processes reuse it.

key_symbols.name: CHUNK_CHARS
key_symbols.explain: Maximum characters `text_window` returns per call (16,384).

key_symbols.name: bounded_int
key_symbols.explain: Validates an optional integer argument: `default` when omitted, otherwise an `int` within `[low, high]`, else `ValueError`.

key_symbols.name: text_window
key_symbols.explain: Returns up to `CHUNK_CHARS` characters of a long text from `offset`, with `next_offset` (null at the end) and `total_chars`; component Tools use it to page long outputs.

key_symbols.name: run_captured
key_symbols.explain: Runs a short child process in a new session and returns `(exit code, stdout, stderr)`; on timeout it raises `TimeoutError` after reaping the process group.

key_symbols.name: ProcessResult
key_symbols.explain: Result of `run_bounded`: `stdout`, `exit_code`, `error` (`timeout`, `output_limit`, or None), and `stderr`.

key_symbols.name: run_bounded
key_symbols.explain: Runs a child process with a deadline and an output cap through temporary files (no pipe stalls), stops it on the cap, and always reaps its process group, also on cancellation.

key_symbols.name: ReadTool
key_symbols.explain: `read`: line window (`offset`, `limit`) of a UTF-8 file with `total_lines` and `next_offset` (null at the end).

key_symbols.name: WriteTool
key_symbols.explain: `write`: creates or overwrites a whole file, creating parent directories, and reports whether it was created.

key_symbols.name: EditTool
key_symbols.explain: `edit`: replaces `old_text` with `new_text` only when it matches exactly once; otherwise the file is unchanged.

key_symbols.name: BashTool
key_symbols.explain: `bash`: runs a command with the full service environment from the workspace root, with a timeout and process-group reaping; a non-zero exit code is a failure that still carries the output.

key_symbols.name: BASE_TOOLS
key_symbols.explain: The four base tool classes, in registration order.

key_symbols.name: shared_tools
key_symbols.explain: Returns the process-wide shared instances of the base tools, creating them on the first call; `BaseAgent.__init__` registers them.

invariants: The names `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `bash` are reserved: registering another Tool with one of them raises `tool already registered`.
Imports only Host modules (`core/abc`, `core/builtin/process_registry`, `config`), never component code.
pitfalls: `bash` reads the whole output before keeping its tail, so a command that prints without bound still uses memory until it ends or times out.
Deleting through `bash` has no guard for the home directory or the workspace root.

modules.role: Transport-independent execution infrastructure in the runtime process: reads execution requests from the queue one at a time and runs the dispatch agent directly on a run handle for the latest main adopted in the mirror; the Runtime does not ACK.
modules.summary: `Runtime.start` first runs `await queue.prepare()` so the consumer group is ready, then starts the read loop `_read_loop`. Each iteration of the loop first acquires a slot of `asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)` and then calls `queue.next()`; once it gets a message, it sets `REQUEST_ID` to `None` in a context copied with `contextvars.copy_context()` and creates a `_handle` task, and `_finished` returns the slot when the task completes. `execute` sets `REQUEST_ID` to the stream id during execution, first runs `await repo.refresh()` (loading the new version if the mirror's main changed), then creates a run handle with `repo.run()` and calls `_run`, and at the end (success, failure, cancellation, or timeout) calls `repo.release(run)` in `finally`. The Runtime itself does not ACK; the dispatch agent does it through `ctx.ack`. `_run` does not interpret the request content: the entrance is fixed to `config.DISPATCH_AGENT` (`dispatch`), `run.version(name)` pins the entrance name to the current main, `data` is `{"event": {provider, external_id, payload}}`, `request` is `None`, and the session and parent session come from the message (a new session is created when absent). It then generates `run_id`, builds an `AgentContext` with `max_steps`, `message_id`, `acknowledger=self.queue.ack`, and `agents=run`, takes the entrance instance only when the name is in the version's `graph.entrances`, and runs `begin_run`, `_call`, and `finish_run` in order inside `component_scope(version.label)`, so that `session_run` carries the entrance version's `code_version`. Runs are not serialized per session; runs of the same session also execute in parallel. `_call` wraps `agent.run` in `asyncio.timeout(config.RUN_TIMEOUT)`, converts a timeout to `cancelled`, and converts a missing entrance (`unknown entrance`) and exceptions to an `error` result. `stop` stops reading, waits for all running tasks to finish, and then runs `await repo.close()`. Reclaiming, the delivery limit, and the dead stream are not in this module; they are handled by `QueueConsumer.next` in `queue/consumer.py` and `RedisStream.reclaim`/`dead` in `queue/redis_stream.py`. Choosing the entrance, assembling Source definitions, and interpreting events per business object are the dispatch agent's job, and the Runtime does not reference Sources.
modules.flow: Sits between the queue and the agents: takes an `EventRequest` from `QueueConsumer`, converts it to an `AgentCall`, and calls the dispatch agent in the version pinned by the run handle; at the end it records the `session_run` and releases the run handle. ACK is performed by the dispatch agent.

key_symbols.name: MessageQueue
key_symbols.explain: The Runtime's read source: `prepare` prepares for reading, `next` returns one (stream id, `EventRequest`) or `None`, and `ack` marks a message as processed. The actual implementation is `QueueConsumer` in `queue/consumer.py`.

key_symbols.name: MessageQueue.next
key_symbols.explain: Returns the next message to execute; returns `None` when there is no readable message (or the message was moved to the dead stream).

key_symbols.name: MessageQueue.ack
key_symbols.explain: Confirms completion by stream id; the `QueueConsumer` implementation is `XACK` plus `XDEL`.

key_symbols.name: Runtime
key_symbols.explain: Holds the read loop, the `Semaphore` for the concurrency limit, the set of running tasks, and the stop event; responsible for executing individual messages and draining on stop.

key_symbols.name: Runtime.__init__
key_symbols.explain: Raises `ValueError` when `concurrency` or `max_steps` is not positive; the defaults are `config.RUN_CONCURRENCY` (20) and `config.MAX_STEPS` (300). Stores `queue`, `repo`, and `sessions`.

key_symbols.name: Runtime.start
key_symbols.explain: Does nothing if already started; clears the stop event, runs `await queue.prepare()`, and starts `_read_loop` as a task named `trackeverything-runtime-read`.

key_symbols.name: Runtime.stop
key_symbols.explain: Returns immediately if not started; sets the stop event, waits for the read loop, gathers repeatedly until all running tasks finish, and finally runs `await repo.close()`.

key_symbols.name: Runtime._read_loop
key_symbols.explain: Each iteration first acquires a slot and then calls `queue.next()`; on a read failure it logs and waits up to 1 second; when there is no message or it has stopped, it returns the slot; otherwise it creates a `_handle` task in a copied context (`REQUEST_ID` set to `None`) and registers the `_finished` callback.

key_symbols.name: Runtime._finished
key_symbols.explain: Task completion callback: removes the task from the set and returns the slot.

key_symbols.name: Runtime._handle
key_symbols.explain: Calls `execute`; `CancelledError` is re-raised as is, and other exceptions only log `queue message %s remains pending`, leaving the message un-ACKed.

key_symbols.name: Runtime.execute
key_symbols.explain: Executes one message: sets `REQUEST_ID`, calls `_run` with `repo.run()` after `repo.refresh()`, converts exceptions from `_run` to an `error` at the `execution` stage, calls `repo.release(run)` in `finally`, and returns the `AgentResult`; it does not call `queue.ack`.

key_symbols.name: Runtime._run
key_symbols.explain: Uses `config.DISPATCH_AGENT` as the entrance and pins the entrance version through `run.version(name)`, with `{"event": ...}` as data and `None` as request; generates `run_id` (and also `session_id` when the message has no session), builds an `AgentContext` with `agents=run` (deep-copying `data`), and runs `begin_run` → `_call` → `finish_run` in order inside `component_scope(version.label)` (not serialized per session). When cancelled, it records `cancelled` and re-raises.

key_symbols.name: Runtime._call
key_symbols.explain: When the entrance does not exist (the name is not in the version's `graph.entrances`), returns an `error` at the `entrance` stage (`unknown entrance: <name>`); runs `agent.run(call)` within `asyncio.timeout(config.RUN_TIMEOUT)`; a timeout returns `status="cancelled"` with `ErrorNote("deadline", ...)`, and an exception returns an `error` at the `execution` stage.

key_symbols.name: _failed
key_symbols.explain: Builds a `status="error"` result, writing the reason into both `response` and `ErrorNote(stage, cause)`, because `session_run` stores only `response`.

invariants: The number of messages executing at once never exceeds `concurrency`: a slot is acquired before reading the queue, and it is returned immediately when no message is obtained or a message is read after stopping.

Each message runs on the mirror's main as of the start of the run: the run handle created after `refresh` pins each agent name to the main obtained first, so an agent with a given name does not switch versions within one run; after main switches, runs in progress finish on their original version. Tasks start in a copied context where `REQUEST_ID` is first set to `None` and then set to this message's stream id during execution.

Runs of the same `session_id` also execute in parallel, and the number of concurrent executions is limited only by `concurrency`. The agent is called only after `begin_run` succeeds; on failure the agent does not run and an `error` at the `session` stage is returned.

The Runtime does not ACK; messages are confirmed only by the dispatch agent's `ctx.ack`. When the run is cancelled (`CancelledError`), `execute` raises, or dispatch ends before the ACK, the message stays pending.
A timeout result is `status="cancelled"` with `ErrorNote("deadline", ...)`; the Runtime does not retry, and `finish_run` records the result as usual.

A failure of `finish_run` is only logged and does not change the returned result; the row stays `running` and is closed as `interrupted` by `recover_interrupted_runs` in `app.serve` at the next startup.

The run handle is released in the `finally` of `execute`: whether the run ends in success, failure, cancellation, or timeout, the version's user count goes down, and a version that is not main and has no users is released immediately. The `code_version` of `session_run` is `<Host version>+c.<first 8 chars of the entrance version id>`.
Shutdown order: set the stop event → wait for the read loop → wait for all tasks → `repo.close()`.
pitfalls: `stop` does not cancel running tasks. Each run's agent execution is bounded by `RUN_TIMEOUT` (default 3600 seconds), but `begin_run` and `finish_run` do not count toward that deadline, so the drain time can exceed `RUN_TIMEOUT`.

Reclaiming is done by `RedisStream.reclaim` with `XAUTOCLAIM` based on the idle time `QUEUE_CLAIM_IDLE` (1800 seconds), and the consumer name is fixed to `runtime`. A message still un-ACKed after more than 1800 seconds of execution is reclaimed again by the same process and runs in parallel with the original execution (even with the same `session_id`), and the default `RUN_TIMEOUT` is longer than that idle time.

If a message ends before the dispatch agent reaches `ctx.ack` (an exception, a `RUN_TIMEOUT` timeout, or `dispatch` not being in main's `entrances`), it stays pending, is reclaimed after 1800 seconds, and runs again; once the delivery count exceeds `QUEUE_MAX_DELIVERIES` (3), `QueueConsumer` moves it to the dead stream. A named run cancelled by `RUN_TIMEOUT` is likewise run again.
When runs of the same session execute in parallel, the conversation history may be recorded in a different order from the publish order, and the runs cannot see each other's messages.
When `begin_run` fails, dispatch does not run, the message is not ACKed, and it is reclaimed and retried after 1800 seconds of idle time.

The Runtime starts only `config.DISPATCH_AGENT`: `graph.agents` contains all of the version's agents, but only names in `graph.entrances` can serve as entrances. A named run can reach only child agents declared by dispatch; for an undeclared name, dispatch returns error and ACKs.

The root `session_run` recorded by `begin_run` always has `agent_name="dispatch"` and `request=None`, including for named runs; when a named run with a session (such as `general`) reads the conversation history, past request text reads as `None`.
Messages that were read but not executed before shutdown are reclaimed only at the next startup, after more than 1800 seconds of idle time.

When `refresh` fails to load a new main, it logs only once and later messages keep using the already loaded main; a failure to read the mirror's main likewise keeps the current one without failing the run. `refresh` and `repo.run()` sit outside the inner `try` of `execute`, so a `RuntimeError` such as a closed version store is logged by `_handle` and the message stays pending.

sync"| rp tr -->|"prepare, next"| qc["QueueConsumer"] tr -->|"30 s maintenance tick"| pub["publish_catalog
also called at serve startup"] pub -->|"repo.main_version"| cat["catalog.build_catalog"] mesh ~~~ tool["version-owned Tools"] tool -->|"start subprocesses"| prr["process_registry
spawn_exec and spawn_shell"]
diagram.caption: How the `core/builtin` modules are assembled and call each other in the runtime process: `serve` assembles the version store and `TrackingRuntime` through `build_runtime`; the version store builds the component graph through `compose` when it loads a version; the catalog is published at startup and on the maintenance tick, and a separate periodic task syncs the version store with the component repository; and Tools start subprocesses through `process_registry`.

groups.overview: These 4 modules are the PostgreSQL-facing session persistence layer in `core/builtin`: `PostgresSessionStore` stores `session / session_run` (the input, status, and response of each run); `PostgresChannelStore` stores the mapping between external chat rooms and sessions (`channel`), the external material URLs referenced by a session (`session_source`), and the project announcement channels (`project_channel`); `PostgresCodexSessionStore` stores the link between an app session and a Codex CLI thread (`codex_session`). Every Store reads and writes only through the `core.orm` models and the engine shared per URL by `sessions_for`, does no I/O at construction, and never creates or alters tables. The `open_*` factories in `database.py` create these Stores and the execution log recorder, requiring `config.DATABASE_URL`. On the runtime side they are used by `core/builtin/app.py`, `Runtime`, and version-owned Agents and Tools; on the queue side only the Discord intake uses them, resolving sessions through `open_channel_store().resolve_session`.

modules.role: Stores the one-to-one mapping between external chat rooms and sessions (`channel`), the external material URLs referenced by a session (`session_source`), and the project announcement channels (`project_channel`).
modules.summary: `resolve_session` first looks up `(provider, channel_id)`; if absent, it generates a session ID with `str(uuid4())`, inserts it with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the primary key, commits, and reads again, so concurrent creation converges on one row. `channel` and `session_source` have no foreign key to the `session` table, because a mapping can be established before the first message's `begin_run` creates the session row. `attach_source` idempotently appends the raw URL, `channels_for_source` joins the two tables on session, and `clear_sources_for_channel` deletes all source links of the session mapped to that channel but keeps the `channel` row. `project_channel` has project as its primary key with a unique `channel_id`; `set_project_channel` upserts with project as the conflict key and updates `channel_id` and `updated_at`, and `project_for_channel` looks up in reverse by `channel_id` only. Read methods convert ORM rows into frozen dataclasses (`ChannelMapping`, `ProjectChannelMapping`, `SessionSource`) or a single string.
modules.flow: Before publishing an `EventRequest`, the queue process's Discord intake resolves with `resolve_session` the session and parent session mapped to the channel (and to a thread's parent channel). In the runtime, the dispatch agent uses `channel_for_session`, `list_sources`, and `project_for_channel` to decide the entrance for Discord messages, and the `channel_link` and `issue_workflow` Tools read and write the mappings and source links.

key_symbols.name: ChannelMapping
key_symbols.explain: Mapping value made of provider, channel_id, session_id, and creation time.

key_symbols.name: ProjectChannelMapping
key_symbols.explain: Mapping value between a project label and its announcement channel_id, including creation and update times.

key_symbols.name: SessionSource
key_symbols.explain: Link value between a session and one raw external material URL, including the time it was added.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore
key_symbols.explain: Store that owns channel→session resolution, session source links, and project mapping writes; rejects an empty DSN with `ValueError` at construction.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.resolve_session
key_symbols.explain: Reuses an existing mapping or inserts one with a new `uuid4`, and returns the session ID; raises `LookupError` if the row still cannot be read after the insert.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.get_channel
key_symbols.explain: Returns the stored `ChannelMapping`, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.channel_for_session
key_symbols.explain: Read-only; returns the channel_id under the provider that points to the session, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.attach_source
key_symbols.explain: Links a source URL to a session; duplicates are ignored idempotently.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.channels_for_source
key_symbols.explain: Returns all channel mappings under the provider whose session is linked to the URL.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.clear_sources_for_channel
key_symbols.explain: Deletes all source links of the session mapped to the channel and returns the number of deleted rows; returns 0 when there is no mapping.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.list_sources
key_symbols.explain: Returns the session's source links ordered by `added_at`, `source_url`.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.resolve_project_channel
key_symbols.explain: Read-only; returns the project's announcement channel_id, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.project_for_channel
key_symbols.explain: Looks up the project in reverse by channel_id; returns None if it is not a project channel.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.set_project_channel
key_symbols.explain: Upserts the mapping with project as the conflict key, overwriting `channel_id` and `updated_at`.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore.list_project_channels
key_symbols.explain: Returns all project→channel mappings ordered by `created_at`, `project`.

key_symbols.name: PostgresChannelStore._select_session
key_symbols.explain: Reads the session_id mapped to `(provider, channel_id)` within the given DB session.

invariants: One `(provider, channel_id)` maps to exactly one session; an existing mapping is only reused, never rewritten.
`attach_source` produces no duplicate rows for the same `(session_id, source_url)`; URLs are stored raw, and interpreting them is up to the reader.
`clear_sources_for_channel` returns 0 instead of failing when the channel has no mapping, and never deletes the `channel` row.
A `channel_id` can belong to only one project; `set_project_channel` overwrites `channel_id` for the same project and keeps `created_at`.
`channel_for_session`, `resolve_project_channel`, and `project_for_channel` are read-only and return None when absent.
pitfalls: `resolve_session` generates a hyphenated `uuid4` string, while `Runtime` and `record_event_in` use `new_id()` (`uuid4().hex`), so session IDs in both formats coexist.

`resolve_session` does not create the `session` row; the row exists only after `begin_run` or `record_event` (for example when `issue_workflow` appends an investigation report) first writes it. Writes with a foreign key to `session` (such as `codex_session`) cannot rely only on the mapping this Store establishes.
When the `channel_id` given to `set_project_channel` is already taken by another project, the unique constraint raises a database exception; no transfer happens.
`project_for_channel` does not distinguish providers; `project_channel.channel_id` is unique across all providers.

modules.role: Stores the link between an app session and a Codex CLI thread ID for a given checkout, project, and mode (`codex_session`), never overwriting another ID already stored.
modules.summary: `get` reads by the composite primary key `(session_id, cwd, project, mode)` and returns `codex_session_id` or None. `bind` inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the primary key and re-reads within the same transaction; if the row does not exist or the stored value differs from the given one, it raises `ValueError` without committing (the transaction rolls back when the DB session closes), and saving the same ID again is idempotent. Rejects an empty DSN with `ValueError` at construction. Only the version-owned `tools/codex_session.py` (the `codex_session` Tool) uses it, with the current `AgentContext.session_id` as the app session.
modules.flow: When an agent in the runtime calls the `codex_session` Tool, `action` `get` calls `get` and `bind` calls `bind`; the Tool accesses this Store only when the Context has a session_id.

key_symbols.name: PostgresCodexSessionStore
key_symbols.explain: Store that owns reads and writes of the `codex_session` table; rejects an empty DSN with `ValueError` at construction.

key_symbols.name: PostgresCodexSessionStore.get
key_symbols.explain: Returns the stored Codex thread ID for `(session_id, cwd, project, mode)`, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresCodexSessionStore.bind
key_symbols.explain: Inserts the link, confirms that the stored value matches the given ID, and commits; raises `ValueError` on a mismatch.

invariants: Once stored for a given `(session_id, cwd, project, mode)`, `codex_session_id` is never rewritten.
`bind` commits only after confirming that the stored value matches the given value.
pitfalls: `codex_session.session_id` has a foreign key to `session.session_id`, so `bind` requires the session row to exist (in the runtime, `begin_run` creates it first); a session that has only a `channel` mapping and has never run cannot be bound.

The `codex_session_id` column is unique, but conflict handling covers only the primary key; binding the same Codex ID to a different `(session_id, cwd, project, mode)` raises a database unique-constraint exception, not `ValueError`.
The queue process loads this module because of the import in `database.py` but does not use it; `process.restart_roles` classifies changes to this file as requiring only a runtime restart.

modules.role: Factory entry point that creates the built-in PostgreSQL Stores and the execution log recorder from `config.DATABASE_URL`.
modules.summary: `_require_dsn` reads `config.DATABASE_URL` on every call and strips whitespace; an empty value fails with `ValueError`, and there is no other persistence backend. Each call of the 4 `open_*` functions creates a new Store instance (`PostgresExecutionLogger`, `PostgresSessionStore`, `PostgresChannelStore`, `PostgresCodexSessionStore`); constructing an instance does no I/O, and the connection pool is shared per URL by `core.orm.connection.engine_for`. The return type of `open_execution_logger` is the `core.abc.execution_log.LogRecorder` protocol, so callers depend only on `record`. Engine ownership lies with `core.orm.connection`; each Store module takes `sessions_for` directly from there and never imports this module in reverse.
modules.flow: At runtime startup, `serve()` and `build_runtime()` in `core/builtin/app.py` build the shared services through `open_session_store` and `open_execution_logger`; during execution, Tools and the dispatch agent call `open_*` as needed. When the queue builds the Discord intake, `build_discord_gateway` calls `open_channel_store`.

key_symbols.name: _require_dsn
key_symbols.explain: Reads `config.DATABASE_URL` with whitespace stripped and raises `ValueError` when it is empty (PostgreSQL is the only backend).

key_symbols.name: open_execution_logger
key_symbols.explain: Returns a new `PostgresExecutionLogger` typed as `LogRecorder`.

key_symbols.name: open_session_store
key_symbols.explain: Returns a new `PostgresSessionStore`.

key_symbols.name: open_channel_store
key_symbols.explain: Returns a new `PostgresChannelStore`.

key_symbols.name: open_codex_session_store
key_symbols.explain: Returns a new `PostgresCodexSessionStore`.

invariants: When `DATABASE_URL` is empty (including whitespace only), every `open_*` raises `ValueError` and never falls back to other storage.
The factories only construct objects; they do not connect to the database or check the schema. Whether the schema is at head is checked by `require_schema_head` when each process starts.
Store modules never import this module (this module imports every Store, so a reverse import would be circular).
pitfalls: This module loads all 4 Store modules and `builtin/execution_log.py` at import time, so even when the queue process pulls in this module only for `open_channel_store`, it also loads `session_store.py`, `codex_session_store.py`, and `execution_log.py`. `process.restart_roles` classifies changes to `database.py`, `session_store.py`, and `channel_store.py` as restarting both roles, while `codex_session_store.py` and `execution_log.py` restart only the runtime.
The DSN is read when `open_*` is called: changing `config.DATABASE_URL` affects only Stores opened afterward, and already constructed Stores keep using the DSN from construction time.

modules.role: Stores conversation sessions and the run record of each entry agent execution (`session / session_run`) in PostgreSQL and provides queries over them.
modules.summary: `begin_run` reuses or creates the session row and inserts the run row in one transaction: `status` takes the table default `running`, `started_at` takes `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `data` and `request` are stored as JSONB through `snapshot`, and `code_version` is `current_code_version()` (`Runtime._run` calls it inside the entrance version's `component_scope`, giving `<Host version>+c.<first 8 chars of the entrance version id>`; `record_event_in` during agent execution carries that agent's version). When creating a new session with `parent_session_id`, it first creates a placeholder row for the parent session with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` to satisfy the self-referencing foreign key `session.parent_session_id`; when reusing an existing session, the given parent is ignored. `finish_run` writes the final status, response snapshot, and end time with `UPDATE ... RETURNING`, and `recover_interrupted_runs` uses row locks to close runs still `running` from before startup as `interrupted`. `record_event` / `record_event_in` start no agent; they append externally confirmed input (and an optional response) as a completed run with status `ok`, and `record_event_in` joins the caller's transaction without committing. `get_session`, `get_run`, and `list_runs` convert ORM rows into the public frozen dataclasses `Session` and `SessionRun`, and session IDs are stored as is. The queue process loads this module only because of the import in `database.py` and never calls its methods.
modules.flow: When the runtime process starts, `serve()` first calls `recover_interrupted_runs(before=now)`; afterwards `Runtime._run` records the start of each message with `begin_run` and records the result with `finish_run` after the agent finishes or is cancelled. During execution, `tools/session_history.py` (including the history loading `conversation_turns` of conversation agents) reads sessions and runs, and `tools/issue_workflow.py` uses `record_event` to append delivered Issue investigation reports.

key_symbols.name: Session
key_symbols.explain: Public immutable value holding the session ID, creation time, and parent session ID.

key_symbols.name: SessionRun
key_symbols.explain: Public immutable value holding one run's agent name, input `data` and `request`, status, response, and start and end times.

key_symbols.name: _row_to_session
key_symbols.explain: Converts an ORM `Session` row into the public dataclass.

key_symbols.name: _row_to_run
key_symbols.explain: Converts an ORM `SessionRun` row into the public dataclass, copying `data_json` into a dict.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore
key_symbols.explain: Store that owns session and run records; rejects an empty DSN with `ValueError` at construction.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.begin_run
key_symbols.explain: Rejects a parent equal to the session itself, writes the parent and creates the parent placeholder row only when creating a new session, and commits the session and the `running` run row in the same transaction.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.finish_run
key_symbols.explain: Updates the run's status, response, and end time; raises `LookupError` when the target does not exist.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.recover_interrupted_runs
key_symbols.explain: Takes row locks on `running` runs started before `before`, sets them to `interrupted`, writes the end time, and returns the count.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.record_event
key_symbols.explain: Opens its own session, calls `record_event_in`, and commits, appending external input and an optional confirmed response as a completed run.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.record_event_in
key_symbols.explain: Within the caller's transaction, creates the session row if missing and inserts a run row with status `ok`, returning the new run_id; assigns a new ID when no session_id is given.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.get_session
key_symbols.explain: Returns the stored `Session`, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.get_run
key_symbols.explain: Returns one `SessionRun` with input, response, and status, or None if absent.

key_symbols.name: PostgresSessionStore.list_runs
key_symbols.explain: Returns all runs of the given session ordered by `started_at`, `run_id`.

invariants: `begin_run` raises `ValueError` when `parent_session_id` equals `session_id`.
The parent is written only when creating a new session; the parent of an existing session is never rewritten by later runs.
The session row and the run row are committed in the same `begin_run` transaction; a duplicate run_id fails the whole transaction on the primary key conflict.
`finish_run` raises `LookupError` when it cannot find the run; it neither retries nor creates a row.
`record_event_in` writes status `ok` and `finished_at`; committing is the caller's responsibility.
`list_runs` only returns records; it does not control the execution order of agents.
pitfalls: `recover_interrupted_runs` closes every `running` run started before `before` regardless of which process wrote it, assuming only one runtime runs against the same database (`serve()` calls it before building the runtime).

`finish_run` does not check the current status and overwrites rows in any status. When `finish_run` fails in `Runtime._run`, it only logs, and the row stays `running` until it is closed as `interrupted` at the next startup.

When `begin_run` fails, `Runtime._run` returns an error result with `stage` `session` and does not run the agent; an `EventRequest` is confirmed only by the dispatch agent through `ctx.ack`, so the message is not ACKed and stays pending until it is reclaimed.
`get_run` has no callers in `src` or `tests`, and `record_event_in` is called only by `record_event`.
