diagram.caption: The `open_*` functions in `database.py` create the three session-related Stores from the required `DATABASE_URL`; the queue's Discord intake, the runtime's `serve`, `Runtime._run`, the dispatch agent, and the Tools read and write their tables through them.

groups.overview: This group is core's foundation for failure shapes and execution observability. `builtin/domain` defines the ORM-free `ErrorNote`, `ToolFailures`, and `LogEvent`, plus the correlating contextvars and helpers for ids, time, and JSON copies; `BaseAgent` in `core/abc/agent.py`, `TrackedLLM` in `llm/tracking.py`, `core/builtin/runtime.py`, `session_store.py`, and the Tools use them. `PostgresExecutionLogger` in `builtin/execution_log.py` appends `LogEvent`s to the `logs` table: `BaseAgent` writes `agent`, `tool`, and `harness`, `TrackedLLM` writes `llm`, and `tools/review.py` writes `cli`; the `read_*` functions in the same module read these rows for the queue process's management API; in the runtime, the optimizer also reads recent runs through `read_recent_runs`, `read_error_rows` in `optimizer/errors.py` reads non-`ok` `agent` rows directly through the ORM, and `read_usage` in `optimizer/consolidation.py` counts `agent`, `tool`, and `read_skill` rows and each component's first row the same way. Events within one run share `run_id` (the same as `session_run.run_id`), and `parent_execution_id` points to the execution id of the Agent that was running when the event started, which forms a tree of the entry agent (parent None), child agents, Tools, harnesses, LLM calls, and cli calls. `builtin/code_version.py` resolves the Host's git version and combines it with `current_component_version` (the running Agent's component version, `c.<first 8 chars of version id>`) into the version label shown in execution logs and session records; the queue process also loads it through the Store imports.

modules.role: Resolves the version of the executing code (git SHA plus uncommitted changes that affect execution) only once per process, and provides execution logs and session records with a display value that includes the running Agent's component version.
modules.summary: `load_code_version` runs `git -C REPO_ROOT` as an asyncio subprocess and uses the first 12 chars of HEAD as the version only when `rev-parse --show-toplevel` matches `REPO_ROOT`. If `WATCHED_PATHS` has uncommitted changes (including untracked files), it computes the first 8 chars of a SHA-1 over `diff HEAD` and the paths and contents of untracked files, and records `<sha12>+dirty.<hash8>`. A toplevel mismatch, a HEAD resolution failure, a missing git, or a `rev-parse` call exceeding 5 seconds raises nothing and records `unknown` (a failed or timed-out `status` logs a warning and is treated as clean). The result is stored in the module-level `_current`, which `current_code_version_info` returns without waiting. The component version lives in the ContextVar `current_component_version` in `core/builtin/domain/execution_log.py`: `BaseAgent._enter` sets it to the instance's `version_label` while the Agent runs, and `Runtime._run` sets it to the entrance version with `component_scope(version.label)` while recording the run's start and end; `current_code_version` then returns `<Host version>+c.<first 8 chars of version id>`, or just the Host version when there is no component version.
modules.flow: The runtime's `serve` awaits `load_code_version` before building the Runtime; afterwards `execution_log` calls `current_code_version` when writing log rows, and `session_store`'s `begin_run` and `record_event_in` call it when writing session run rows. The queue process loads this module because `api/runs` and `api/usage` import `core.builtin.execution_log`, but it neither resolves the version nor calls its functions.

key_symbols.name: REPO_ROOT
key_symbols.explain: The repo root derived from this file's location (`parents[4]`; this file is in `<root>/src/trackeverything/core/builtin/`), not from the cwd.

key_symbols.name: WATCHED_PATHS
key_symbols.explain: Paths checked for dirtiness: `src`, `alembic`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `scripts`.

key_symbols.name: UNKNOWN
key_symbols.explain: Display value `unknown` used when the version cannot be resolved.

key_symbols.name: _GIT_TIMEOUT
key_symbols.explain: Limit of 5 seconds per git call.

key_symbols.name: CodeVersion
key_symbols.explain: The combination of display value `value`, `git_sha`, and `dirty` (frozen, slots).

key_symbols.name: resolve_code_version
key_symbols.explain: Resolves the version from git in `REPO_ROOT` (a substituted root in tests).

key_symbols.name: _git
key_symbols.explain: Runs git with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and a 5-second limit and returns stdout; returns None on failure, timeout, or missing git, and on cancellation kills the subprocess and re-raises.

key_symbols.name: _kill
key_symbols.explain: Kills a timed-out or cancelled git and waits for it to exit, leaving no zombie.

key_symbols.name: _from_git
key_symbols.explain: Confirms the toplevel matches and builds a `CodeVersion` from HEAD and `status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`.

key_symbols.name: _dirty_digest
key_symbols.explain: Computes the first 8 chars of a SHA-1 from `diff HEAD` and the paths and contents of untracked files.

key_symbols.name: load_code_version
key_symbols.explain: Resolves the process's version only once and stores it in `_current`; stores `unknown` on failure.

key_symbols.name: current_code_version_info
key_symbols.explain: Returns the stored Host version without waiting; returns `unknown` while it is not resolved yet.

key_symbols.name: component_scope
key_symbols.explain: Context manager that sets `current_component_version` to the given component version for the duration of the block and restores it with the token on exit; passing `None` changes nothing. `Runtime._run` uses it so that `session_run` carries the entrance version.

key_symbols.name: current_code_version
key_symbols.explain: The display value attached to logs and execution records: `<Host version>+<label>` when there is a component version, otherwise the Host version.

key_symbols.name: override_code_version
key_symbols.explain: Pins the version for tests; passing `None` clears the pin so the next `load_code_version` resolves again.

invariants: `load_code_version` never propagates exceptions raised during resolution; on failure it stores a `CodeVersion` of `unknown`.

Once the first resolved value is stored in `_current`, git is not called again; `_lock` (`threading.Lock`) only guards reads and writes of `_current`, so concurrent first calls may each run git, but only the first stored value is kept.
git runs in `REPO_ROOT`, not the cwd; a toplevel mismatch is recorded as `unknown`.
git calls are aborted at 5 seconds; timed-out or cancelled subprocesses are killed and awaited.
The dirtiness check only covers `WATCHED_PATHS`; changes in `docs/` and `data/` do not affect the version.
pitfalls: Until `load_code_version` completes, `current_code_version` returns `unknown` (`unknown+c.<...>` while an Agent is running).
When `git status` fails, a warning is logged and the tree is treated as clean.
When running as an installed package whose root is not a git toplevel, the version is `unknown`.
The catalog snapshot's `code_version` is main's `label` (`c.<first 8 chars of version id>`), not the value of `current_code_version`.

The queue process loads this module, but `process.restart_roles` classifies changes under `core/builtin/` other than `database.py`, `session_store.py`, and `channel_store.py` as runtime-only restart triggers, so the queue keeps using the already loaded module.
`override_code_version` only resets `_current`; it does not clear `current_component_version`.

Agents not constructed inside a version (`version_label` is `None`, e.g. scripts and tests) do not set a component version when they run, so records carry only the Host version or a value set by an outer scope.

modules.role: Marker for the `domain` package, which holds ORM-free values, in-execution state, and log correlation.
modules.summary: A package init file containing only a docstring, with no public names or re-exports. The contents live in `errors.py` and `execution_log.py`; callers import the concrete modules directly.
modules.flow: Takes no part in the runtime flow; it is loaded as a package only when the `errors` or `execution_log` submodule is imported.

modules.role: Defines `ErrorNote`, the shared shape of failures that cross run boundaries, and `ToolFailures`, which keeps unrecovered Tool failures per Agent execution.
modules.summary: `ErrorNote` is a frozen dataclass holding only a machine-readable `stage` and the verbatim `cause`; `render` joins `stage: cause` with `'; '` without translating or transforming anything. `ToolFailures` has exactly one instance per shared Context, as `AgentContext.tool_failures` (parent and child agents share the same Context through `call.child`); it partitions by the current value of `current_agent_execution_id` and records failures in `(tool, key)` slots. `BaseAgent.call_tool` calls `record` when a Tool fails (`stage` is the Tool name) and `resolve` when it succeeds; `BaseAgent._adjudicate` uses `take` at the run boundary to extract and consume the current Agent execution's partition, and `unresolved` lets the LLM loop of `repair_tool_failures` check `fatal_tools` without consuming. `ErrorNote` is also the element type of `AgentResult.errors`, and `Runtime` uses it for failures in stages such as `execution`, `session`, `entrance`, `deadline`, and `cancellation`.
modules.flow: While an Agent runs, `BaseAgent.call_tool` records whether each Tool call succeeded; at the end of the run `_adjudicate` uses `take` to extract the unrecovered failures. Failures of `fatal_tools` go into `AgentResult.errors` (turning an ok result into an error); non-fatal failures stay in the agent event's `error` only when the result is ok and there is no fatal failure, and are discarded otherwise. In a run that ends with an exception all of them go into `errors`; on cancellation they are discarded.

key_symbols.name: ErrorNote
key_symbols.explain: Frozen dataclass holding the failure stage `stage` and the verbatim cause `cause`.

key_symbols.name: render
key_symbols.explain: Joins a sequence of `ErrorNote`s into one string in `stage: cause` form, separated by `'; '`.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures
key_symbols.explain: Map of unrecovered Tool failures partitioned by Agent execution id.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures._current
key_symbols.explain: Returns the partition for the current value of `current_agent_execution_id`, creating it if absent.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures.record
key_symbols.explain: Records a failure into the `(tool, key)` slot, overwriting; when key is None it goes into the untargeted slot.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures.resolve
key_symbols.explain: Deletes the succeeded `(tool, key)` slot and that Tool's untargeted slot.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures.unresolved
key_symbols.explain: Returns the current partition's unrecovered notes without consuming them; when Tool names are given, only those Tools' slots are returned.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures.take
key_symbols.explain: Removes the current Agent execution's partition from the map and returns all its notes.

key_symbols.name: ToolFailures._slot
key_symbols.explain: Builds a slot name by joining the Tool name and key with `\x00`; uses `*` when key is None.

invariants: Recording, resolving, reading, and taking in `ToolFailures` always act only on the partition for the current value of `current_agent_execution_id`; a child agent's failures never mix into the parent's partition.
Besides the slot for the given key, `resolve` always also deletes that Tool's untargeted slot.
`take` performs a `pop` on the partition, so a second `take` within the same Agent execution returns an empty tuple.
`render` outputs `stage` and `cause` verbatim.
pitfalls: When key is the string `*`, `_slot` produces the same slot name as when key is None (untargeted), so the two cannot be distinguished.

A partition disappears only through `take`; failures recorded with `record` outside an Agent execution (`current_agent_execution_id` is None) stay in the None partition until someone in the same context calls `take`.

`unresolved(*tools)` matches Tool names against the part of the slot name before `\x00`, while `_adjudicate` matches `fatal_tools` against `ErrorNote.stage`; the two agree only because `call_tool` uses the Tool name as `stage`, so code that calls `record` itself must keep this convention.

modules.role: Provides `LogEvent`, which represents one completed execution; contextvars that carry the run and Agent-execution correlation ids and the running Agent's component version; and helper functions for ids, time, and JSON copies.
modules.summary: `LogEvent` is a frozen dataclass correlated by `run_id`, `execution_id`, and `parent_execution_id`, and also carries `event_type`, `component`, `started_at` (an ISO string), `duration_ms`, `status`, `request`, `result`, `error`, `usage`, and `cost_usd`. `current_run_id`, `current_agent_execution_id`, and `current_parent_agent_execution_id` are set by `BaseAgent._enter` for the duration of one Agent execution and restored when it ends. `BaseAgent.run` creates the agent's `_Span` before entering `_enter`, with its parent taken from the calling Agent's execution id (None for the entry agent, which runs in the context copied by the Runtime's read loop); after entry, the `_Span`s of Tools and harnesses, `TrackedLLM.respond`, and `_log_cli` in `tools/review.py` all read `current_agent_execution_id` as their parent, and `ToolFailures` uses it as its partition key. `current_component_version` holds the running Agent's component version (`c.<first 8 chars of version id>`); `BaseAgent._enter` sets it from the instance's `version_label`, and `core/builtin/code_version.current_code_version` reads it. `new_id` returns `uuid4().hex`, which `Runtime` uses to generate the run_id and the default session_id. `elapsed_clock` uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` on macOS and `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` on other systems, falling back to `time.monotonic()` when the constant does not exist; `elapsed_ms` computes the millisecond difference with the same clock. `snapshot` copies a value immediately through a JSON round trip (`asdict` for dataclasses, `str` for other objects), and on failure returns a dict with `snapshot_error` and a safe `repr` instead of raising.
modules.flow: While Agents run, `BaseAgent`, `TrackedLLM`, and the cli records of `review_pr` use it to build `LogEvent`s and read the correlating contextvars; `Runtime` and `PostgresSessionStore` use `new_id` and `snapshot` to generate run_ids and JSONB contents.

key_symbols.name: LogEvent
key_symbols.explain: Immutable value holding one completed execution's type, correlation ids, component name, start time, duration, status, input and output, usage, and cost.

key_symbols.name: current_run_id
key_symbols.explain: The current run id (default None); `TrackedLLM` uses it to determine the run of `llm` events.

key_symbols.name: current_agent_execution_id
key_symbols.explain: The current Agent execution id, used as the events' parent and as the partition key of `ToolFailures`.

key_symbols.name: current_parent_agent_execution_id
key_symbols.explain: The parent execution id of the current Agent execution, set by `BaseAgent._enter`.

key_symbols.name: current_component_version
key_symbols.explain: The running Agent's component version (`c.<first 8 chars of version id>`, default None); set by `BaseAgent._enter` and `code_version.component_scope`, read by `current_code_version`.

key_symbols.name: new_id
key_symbols.explain: Returns an opaque, unique id using `uuid4().hex`.

key_symbols.name: utc_now
key_symbols.explain: Returns the current time as an ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset.

key_symbols.name: elapsed_clock
key_symbols.explain: Returns the value of the OS-specific monotonic clock (including system sleep); uses `time.monotonic()` when the constant does not exist.

key_symbols.name: elapsed_ms
key_symbols.explain: Returns the milliseconds since the start (rounded) using the same clock as `elapsed_clock`.

key_symbols.name: snapshot
key_symbols.explain: Copies a value immediately through a JSON round trip; on failure returns a dict containing `snapshot_error` and a safe `repr`.

key_symbols.name: _json_default
key_symbols.explain: Converts to JSON with `asdict` for dataclass instances and `str` for other objects.

key_symbols.name: _safe_repr
key_symbols.explain: Catches a failing `repr` and returns a substitute string.

invariants: `snapshot` never raises an `Exception`; even when a value cannot be converted to JSON it returns a dict containing `snapshot_error` and `repr`.
`elapsed_ms` always takes the difference with the same clock as `elapsed_clock`.
`utc_now` returns an ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset, and `logs.started_at` is sorted by this text.

The parent of an agent event is the calling Agent's execution id; the parent of tool, harness, llm, and cli events is the execution id of the Agent active when the event started. Parallel child agents each set their execution id in the context copied by `TaskGroup`, so they do not overwrite each other.
pitfalls: `elapsed_clock` may be a different clock from `time.monotonic()`, so the start value must be obtained with `elapsed_clock()` before it is passed to `elapsed_ms`.
`current_parent_agent_execution_id` is set by `BaseAgent._enter`, but nothing in `src` reads it; event parent-child relationships come from `LogEvent.parent_execution_id`.
The `LogEvent` docstring mentions source executions, but there are no `source` events; Source fetches are recorded as `tool` events through the `fetch_source` Tool.
The parent of llm and cli events points to the Agent, not to the tool event that triggered them; cli events produced inside a Tool are siblings of that Tool's tool event.
`snapshot` converts unknown objects with `str`, so it never fails on type, but an object's content may be reduced to its `str()` result.

modules.role: Provides the recorder that appends `LogEvent`s to the PostgreSQL `logs` table, and the read functions behind the usage statistics and run flow pages.
modules.summary: `PostgresExecutionLogger.record` runs an ORM `insert` in one short DB session per event; `request` is converted to text with `json.dumps(default=str, ensure_ascii=False)`, `result`, `error`, and `usage` stay NULL when None, and `current_code_version()` is attached; any `Exception` is only logged with `log.exception` and swallowed. The writers are: `BaseAgent.run` writes `agent` (component is the Agent name, request is `{"request", "data"}`, result is the `AgentResult`, error is the list of remaining `ErrorNote`s); `BaseAgent.call_tool` and `_dispatch_calls` write `tool` (component is the Tool name, request is the arguments; names not offered to the LLM are recorded as `error`); `BaseAgent`'s pre, post, and on_error write `harness` (component is `harness:<Agent>.<harness>`); `TrackedLLM` writes `llm` (component is `<provider>/<model>`, or `llm` on failure, with usage and `cost_usd`); and `_log_cli` in `tools/review.py` writes `cli` (component `review_pr`). `read_usage` aggregates `agent` and `tool` events by component name and status, sorted by total descending and name ascending, and gives the earliest `started_at` per type. `read_run_trace` reads one run's detailed events: it truncates Tool arguments, the Agent's `response`, the LLM's `text`, and the result JSON of harnesses and cli calls to the first `PREVIEW_LIMIT + 1` characters, plus the Tool names the LLM chose (`calls`), and does not read LLM or Agent requests. `read_session_trace` and `read_recent_runs` return events of several runs using only lightweight columns, attaching the lightweight `session_run` record per `run_id`.
modules.flow: In the runtime, `open_host_services` wraps `TrackedLLM` with the single recorder created by `open_execution_logger` and injects it into every Agent through `build_agents`, and events are appended one by one while Agents run; in the queue, the management API `GET /api/usage`, `GET /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}`, and `GET /api/sessions/{session_id}` calls the `read_*` functions; in the runtime, `build_runtime` passes `read_recent_runs` bound to the DSN to the `Optimizer`, which uses it to observe recent runs.

key_symbols.name: log
key_symbols.explain: This module's logger; records swallowed write failures.

key_symbols.name: PostgresExecutionLogger
key_symbols.explain: The `LogRecorder` implementation that appends events to `logs` through `sessions_for(dsn)`; rejects an empty DSN with `ValueError` at construction.

key_symbols.name: PostgresExecutionLogger.record
key_symbols.explain: Converts a `LogEvent` into a row, attaches the version, and inserts it; exceptions are only logged, never raised.

key_symbols.name: _dump
key_symbols.explain: Converts a value to JSON text with `default=str` and `ensure_ascii=False`.

key_symbols.name: _dump_optional
key_symbols.explain: Keeps None as None and passes other values to `_dump`.

key_symbols.name: ComponentUsage
key_symbols.explain: One component name's total calls, counts per status, and last-used time.

key_symbols.name: UsageSummary
key_symbols.explain: The `ComponentUsage` lists for Agents and Tools, and the earliest `started_at` of each.

key_symbols.name: read_usage
key_symbols.explain: Aggregates the `agent` and `tool` rows in `logs` by component name and status and returns a `UsageSummary`.

key_symbols.name: PREVIEW_LIMIT
key_symbols.explain: Limit of 300 characters for page excerpts; reads fetch 1 extra character to detect truncation.

key_symbols.name: RunEvent
key_symbols.explain: The condensed form of one `logs` row read by the run flow page; JSON-derived fields are None in lightweight reads.

key_symbols.name: RunRecord
key_symbols.explain: The lightweight columns of one `session_run` row (without the input and response bodies).

key_symbols.name: RunTrace
key_symbols.explain: One run's event list plus its `session_run` record when it exists.

key_symbols.name: SessionTrace
key_symbols.explain: One session, its latest runs in start order, and the total number of runs.

key_symbols.name: _LIGHT_COLUMNS
key_symbols.explain: The lightweight columns of `logs`, without any JSON body.

key_symbols.name: _detail_columns
key_symbols.explain: Adds usage, error, the per-event-type truncated `request_head` and `result_head`, and the LLM's `calls` to the lightweight columns.

key_symbols.name: _event
key_symbols.explain: Converts a row into a `RunEvent`; when `detail` is false, JSON-derived fields are set to None.

key_symbols.name: _record
key_symbols.explain: Converts a `session_run` row into a `RunRecord`, converting times to ISO strings.

key_symbols.name: _light_traces
key_symbols.explain: Reads the lightweight events and `session_run` records of several runs, grouped by run id.

key_symbols.name: read_run_trace
key_symbols.explain: Reads up to `limit` detailed events of one run in start order, plus its record; returns None when neither exists.

key_symbols.name: read_session_trace
key_symbols.explain: Returns the session's latest `limit` runs (in start order), their lightweight events, and the total number of runs; returns None when the session does not exist.

key_symbols.name: read_recent_runs
key_symbols.explain: Returns the `limit` most recently active runs, ordered by the maximum `logs` `id` descending, with their lightweight events.

invariants: `record` never raises an `Exception` to its caller, and a write failure does not change the outcome of a Source, Agent, or LLM execution (`CancelledError` still propagates).

`logs` is append-only; this module never updates or deletes rows. `execution_id` is unique, and every row carries the `code_version` at write time (including the Agent's component version while an Agent runs).

`status` per `event_type`: `agent` is `ok`, `error`, `max_steps`, or `cancelled`; `tool` is `ok`, `error`, or `cancelled`; `harness` is `ok`, `blocked`, `rejected`, or `failed`; `llm` and `cli` are `ok` or `error`.

Detailed reads do not return LLM or Agent requests; a `result_json` that cannot be parsed as JSON is detected with `pg_input_is_valid` and skipped for JSONB extraction, so it does not fail the whole run's query.
`read_run_trace` and `_light_traces` sort by `started_at` and `id`; `read_session_trace` takes the latest `limit` runs and then reverses them into start order.
Every `read_*` raises `ValueError` when the DSN is empty.
pitfalls: `process.restart_roles` classifies changes to this file as runtime-only restarts, but the queue process's `api/runs.py` and `api/usage.py` also import its `read_*` functions; after a read function changes, the queue process keeps running the old code until its next restart.
`_detail_columns` uses `pg_input_is_valid`, available since PostgreSQL 16 (Compose uses `postgres:17-alpine`).
`started_at` is a TEXT column, so sorting and the comparisons with `since` and `last_used_at` are string comparisons that rely on every writer using the same ISO format from `utc_now()`.
`read_recent_runs` selects runs only from `logs`, so runs with no events (such as runs of external events appended by `record_event`) do not appear in the list.
`read_usage` counts only `agent` and `tool`; `llm`, `harness`, and `cli` events are not included in usage statistics.

`tools/memory/baseline.py` reads the `request_json` (shaped `{"request", "data"}`) of `agent` events whose `component` is `compare` directly through the ORM to restore a baseline, so changing the shape of an agent event's request affects that restore.

groups.overview: This group is core's persistence foundation and cross-version shared state. `orm/connection.py` provides a SQLAlchemy async engine shared per URL (`AsyncEngine`), `sessions_for` for creating `AsyncSession`s, and the startup schema head check; `orm/models.py` declares all 12 core tables on `Base` (3 of them keep their data but are neither read nor written by current code); `orm/__init__.py` re-exports the parts of both that current code uses. Both the queue and runtime processes depend on these ORM modules. `shared_state.py` is used only in the runtime process and gives version-owned components (mainly Tools) locks, `ContextVar`s, and caches that are unique across versions; no module inside core imports it. `core/__init__.py` is only the package root with a docstring.

modules.role: The root of the `core` package; its docstring states that the package gathers the shared contracts, execution infrastructure, domain, ORM, version management, and shared state.
modules.summary: A file with a single docstring line; it neither defines nor re-exports any name and does nothing else on import. Every `trackeverything.core.*` import loads this package first, so both the queue and runtime processes pass through it, but it carries no mechanism.
modules.flow: Takes no part in the runtime flow; it is only loaded first when a submodule under `trackeverything.core` is imported.
invariants: Exports no names; subpackages and modules must be imported by their full path (e.g. `trackeverything.core.orm`, `trackeverything.core.shared_state`).

modules.role: A shared store that knows nothing about specific components; it provides locks, caches, and `ContextVar`s that are unique across versions by name, plus `TaskLock`, which is exclusive per task and non-reentrant.
modules.summary: `shared(name, factory)` stores the result of the first `factory()` by name under `_guard` (`threading.Lock`) and afterwards returns the same object to every version; it rejects a value whose type's module starts with `_te_versions.` with a `TypeError` (only the outermost value is checked). `context_var` and `task_lock` are convenience functions built on `shared`. `TaskLock` is exclusive per task and non-reentrant: when the holding task requests it again, it raises `RuntimeError` immediately instead of waiting, and other tasks wait for release; it does not recognize parent-child relationships between tasks. `keyed_lock` shares a `TaskLock` per `(namespace, key)` with a user count and deletes the registration when the last user leaves. The version facade loads version copies only for `MODULE_FOLDERS` (`agent`, `tools`, `harnesses`, `sources`); this module is shared by all versions.
modules.flow: In the runtime process only component modules of versions (mainly Tools) use this module; the Host imports no component module. Discord's send lock, channel lock, and ensure lock, the Gmail token lock, and the pending lock of `tools/fix` use `task_lock`; `issue_lock` in `tools/issue_workflow.py` (i.e. `keyed_lock("issue", key)`) is used inside `_ensure_channel` and inside `_close` of Issue close; and the file locks in `tools/project/locks.py` and others keep cross-version registrations with `shared`. A lock only wraps a single operation inside a Tool and no Agent is called while it is held; `Runtime` and Agents hold no locks.

key_symbols.name: _VERSIONED_PREFIX
key_symbols.explain: The prefix `_te_versions.` of the reserved namespace where version modules live; matches `ROOT` in `core/versioning/loader.py`.

key_symbols.name: _objects
key_symbols.explain: Dictionary from name to shared object, updated under `_guard` and never cleared during the process lifetime.

key_symbols.name: _keyed
key_symbols.explain: Dictionary from `(namespace, key)` to `(TaskLock, user count)`, updated under `_guard` (line 27).

key_symbols.name: TaskLock
key_symbols.explain: An asyncio lock that excludes every task other than the holder; non-reentrant: the holding task raises `RuntimeError` when it requests it again.

key_symbols.name: TaskLock.locked
key_symbols.explain: Returns whether the internal `asyncio.Lock` is held.

key_symbols.name: TaskLock.hold
key_symbols.explain: Requires a running task; the holding task raises `RuntimeError` when it requests again; otherwise (first rebuilding the internal lock if it is idle and the loop has changed) it waits for and acquires the lock, and on exit clears the holder and releases.

key_symbols.name: shared
key_symbols.explain: Stores and returns the result of the first `factory()` by name; rejects instances of version-owned classes.

key_symbols.name: context_var
key_symbols.explain: Lets the Host and components refer to a single `ContextVar` under the same name through `shared`.

key_symbols.name: task_lock
key_symbols.explain: Returns a `TaskLock` shared by name through `shared`, used for mutual exclusion of Tool sends, pending jobs, and so on.

key_symbols.name: keyed_lock
key_symbols.explain: Async context manager that shares and holds a `TaskLock` per `(namespace, key)` with a user count, deleting it from `_keyed` when the last user leaves.

invariants: `shared` with the same name returns the same object to every version in the process, and `factory` runs only on the first call.
`shared` does not store a value whose type's `__module__` starts with `_te_versions.`; it raises `TypeError` instead.

`TaskLock.hold` raises `RuntimeError` when there is no running task; when the holding task requests the same lock again it raises `RuntimeError` without waiting, and other tasks wait for release; the internal `asyncio.Lock` is rebuilt for a new event loop only when it is not held.
The user count of `keyed_lock` includes waiting users; the registration is deleted only when the last user leaves.
`_objects` has no code that deletes registrations, and releasing a version does not clear it either; registrations stay until the process ends.
pitfalls: Passing a different `factory` or `default` for the same name later still returns the original value (the default of `context_var` is fixed on the first call); use a new name when the shape of the value changes.
The rejection of version-owned classes only checks the type of the outermost value; instances placed inside containers such as a dict are not detected.
`factory()` runs inside the non-reentrant `_guard`, so if the factory itself calls `shared`, `context_var`, or `task_lock`, the thread deadlocks.

`TaskLock` does not detect deadlocks: a task holding a lock that awaits a child task requesting the same lock, or two tasks each holding one lock and requesting the other's, wait on each other forever; that is why a lock only wraps a single operation inside a Tool and no Agent is called while it is held.

modules.role: The public surface of the ORM package; re-exports the engine and session utilities from `connection`, and `Base` plus the table classes that current code reads and writes from `models`.
modules.summary: Re-exports `engine_for`, `sessions_for`, and `sqlalchemy_url` from `connection`, and `Base` plus 11 table classes from `models` (`Channel`, `CodexSession`, `DiscordMessage`, `ExecutionLog`, `Memory`, `ProjectChannel`, `RunFeedback`, `Session`, `SessionRun`, `SessionSource`, `WorkspaceSlot`), listing all of them in `__all__`; The 3 table classes whose tables keep their data but are neither read nor written by current code are defined only in `models`; because this package imports `models`, they are registered on `Base.metadata` as well. Users are `channel_store`, `session_store`, `codex_session_store`, and `execution_log` in `core/builtin`, `memory/store.py`, `memory/baseline.py`, `pr_retire_sweep.py`, `workspace_pool.py`, `discord/deliver.py`, and `discord/feedback.py` in `tools/`, `queue/project_labels.py` and `integration/schedule.py` (`sessions_for`), `optimizer/errors.py` and `optimizer/consolidation.py` (`ExecutionLog`, `sessions_for`), and `alembic/env.py` (`Base`).
modules.flow: The queue process loads this package through `api/runs.py` and `api/usage.py` (`core/builtin/execution_log`), `integration/discord.py` (`open_channel_store`), and `integration/schedule.py` (`sessions_for`, `queue/models.py`); the runtime process loads it through the Stores built by `core/builtin/app.py` and through component Tools, and the check CLI loads it through `require_schema_head` and the Stores of `open_host_services`.

key_symbols.explain: Re-exported model of the `run_feedback` table.

key_symbols.name: Session
key_symbols.explain: Re-exported model of the `session` table (users often import it under the alias `SessionRow` to distinguish it from the `Session` dataclass in `core/builtin/session_store.py`).

key_symbols.name: SessionRun
key_symbols.explain: Re-exported model of the `session_run` table.

key_symbols.name: SessionSource
key_symbols.explain: Re-exported model of the `session_source` table.

key_symbols.name: WorkspaceSlot
key_symbols.explain: Re-exported model of the `workspace_slot` table.

invariants: `__all__` lists only `Base`, the 11 table classes current code reads and writes, and the 3 connection utilities (`engine_for`, `sessions_for`, `sqlalchemy_url`); the classes of unused tables (`ExecutionReceipt`, `ExecutionAttempt`, `ExecutionChild`) are not exported here.
Importing this package always imports `models`, so all 16 core table classes are registered on `Base.metadata`.
pitfalls: `schema_head` and `require_schema_head` are not part of the public surface; `api/app.py` and `core/builtin/app.py` import them directly from `trackeverything.core.orm.connection`.

The re-exported `Session` (the `session` table model) has the same name as the `Session` dataclass in `core/builtin/session_store.py`, so users import the table model under the alias `SessionRow`; the ORM session type is `sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncSession`, which does not clash with the table model's name.

modules.role: Provides a SQLAlchemy async engine shared per URL, a session factory that creates `AsyncSession`s, and the startup check that the DB schema is at the Alembic head.
modules.summary: `sqlalchemy_url` converts `postgresql://` and `postgres://` URLs and libpq keyword-style DSNs into a `postgresql+psycopg` URL; a URL that already has `+psycopg` is returned as is. `engine_for` caches one `AsyncEngine` per normalized URL with `create_async_engine` under `_ENGINES_LOCK` (psycopg async connections, `pool_pre_ping=True`, `pool_recycle=1800`); creating the engine does not connect to the DB, and the connection is established on the first operation. `sessions_for` returns an `async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]` bound to that engine with `expire_on_commit=False`; callers open an `AsyncSession` with `async with`, and I/O such as `execute`, `scalar(s)`, `get`, `commit`, and `rollback` is awaited directly on the event loop; transactions are delimited by the `AsyncSession`'s own `commit`, `rollback`, and `begin()`. `require_schema_head` obtains the head of `alembic.ini` at the repository root through `asyncio.to_thread`, then `_current_revision` reads the revision recorded in the DB with `run_sync(_revision)` on an async connection; a mismatch or a failure to connect refuses startup with `RuntimeError`.
modules.flow: The startup coroutine `serve` of both processes (`api/app.py`, `core/builtin/app.py`) awaits `require_schema_head(config.DATABASE_URL)` first; afterwards the runtime's Stores and Tools, the queue's run trace and usage APIs, the channel resolution of Discord intake, the scheduled trigger's reads of the `schedule` table, and the optimizer's reads of `logs`, `schedule`, and `reservation` in the runtime all access PostgreSQL through `AsyncSession`s created by `sessions_for`.

key_symbols.name: _ENGINES
key_symbols.explain: The in-process `AsyncEngine` cache keyed by normalized URL, guarded by `_ENGINES_LOCK` (`threading.Lock`, line 36).

key_symbols.name: sqlalchemy_url
key_symbols.explain: Converts a URL or a libpq keyword DSN into a `postgresql+psycopg` URL; the keyword form goes through `conninfo_to_dict` into the query part of `URL.create`.

key_symbols.name: engine_for
key_symbols.explain: Strips surrounding whitespace and normalizes the URL, then creates or reuses one `AsyncEngine` with `create_async_engine` under the lock.

key_symbols.name: sessions_for
key_symbols.explain: Returns an `async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]` bound to the shared `AsyncEngine` of `dsn` with `expire_on_commit=False`; calling it yields an `AsyncSession` that has not started yet.

key_symbols.name: _ALEMBIC_INI
key_symbols.explain: `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "alembic.ini"`, i.e. the Alembic configuration at the repository root, used as the schema's source of truth.

key_symbols.name: schema_head
key_symbols.explain: Returns the head revision from the checkout's Alembic script directory; raises `RuntimeError` when there is no revision.

key_symbols.name: _revision
key_symbols.explain: Synchronous function that reads the revision with `MigrationContext.configure(connection).get_current_revision()`; `_current_revision` calls it inside the async connection through `run_sync`.

key_symbols.name: _current_revision
key_symbols.explain: Reads the revision recorded in the DB with `run_sync(_revision)` on an async connection of the shared `AsyncEngine`; returns None when nothing has been applied.

key_symbols.name: require_schema_head
key_symbols.explain: Gets the head through `asyncio.to_thread`, then awaits `_current_revision` for the DB revision; raises a `RuntimeError` stating the DB is unreachable when the connection fails, and a `RuntimeError` that suggests running `alembic upgrade head` on a mismatch.

invariants: There is one engine per normalized URL in a process, created with `pool_pre_ping=True` and `pool_recycle=1800`.

This module provides only `AsyncEngine` and `AsyncSession`, and application DB I/O is awaited on the event loop; AS31 in `tests/entry/test_async_contracts.py` scans all of src, including this module, for imports of `sqlalchemy`'s synchronous `create_engine`, `engine_from_config`, `Session`, `sessionmaker`, and `scoped_session`, and for calls to `create_engine`. `alembic/env.py`, outside src, runs migrations with the synchronous `engine_from_config` (`NullPool`) and is outside the scope of that check.
`engine_for` and `sessions_for` only create objects and do not connect to the DB; the connection is established on the session's first operation, so building a Store does no I/O.
`require_schema_head` hands only `schema_head`, which reads the revision scripts synchronously, to `asyncio.to_thread`; the DB revision is read on the event loop through an async connection.
Sessions are created with `expire_on_commit=False`, so attributes are not implicitly reloaded after commit; models define no relationships, and related data is read with explicit queries.
`require_schema_head` only compares revisions and never creates or alters tables; tables are created and altered only by Alembic.
pitfalls: `_ENGINES` caches `AsyncEngine`s globally in the process, and the psycopg async connections in the pool belong to the event loop that created them; the queue and the runtime each use the engine in only one event loop, and reusing the same engine in another event loop (such as a separate `asyncio.run`) requires `dispose()` first. `AsyncSession` does no implicit I/O: accessing an attribute expired after `rollback` or an unloaded attribute raises `MissingGreenlet`, so such data must be read with an explicit query inside the session.

When `DATABASE_URL` is empty, `sqlalchemy_url` returns `postgresql+psycopg://`, which connects using libpq defaults (`PG*` environment variables, the local socket); `require_schema_head` itself does not check for an empty DSN. An explicit error for an empty DSN is raised only at Store entry points such as `_require_dsn` in `core/builtin/database.py`.

`schema_head` locates `alembic.ini` through `parents[4]`, which assumes an import from the checkout's `src/` layout; it is called outside the `try` of `require_schema_head`, so its own exceptions are not wrapped into the unreachable message.

modules.role: Declares the ORM models of all core tables on `Base`; serves as the schema's source of truth for Alembic autogenerate and as the only way Stores and Tools read and write tables.
modules.summary: Declares 14 tables on `Base` (`DeclarativeBase`): the 11 that current code reads and writes (`logs`, `memory`, `workspace_slot`, `session`, `session_run`, `discord_message`, `run_feedback`, `channel`, `project_channel`, `session_source`, `codex_session`), and 3 whose tables and data are kept but which current code neither reads nor writes (`execution_receipt`, `execution_attempt`, `execution_child`). Component versions live in git (`core/versioning/store.py`); the former PostgreSQL version store's `component_*` tables were dropped by revision `a583fc7a918f`. Models declare only column types, server defaults, CHECKs, unique constraints, indexes, and foreign keys, and define no relationships. `queue/models.py` registers on the same `Base` the scheduled-trigger definition table `schedule`, which `integration/schedule.py` only reads, and the legacy tables `subscription`, `schedule_cursor`, and `schedule_outbox`, whose data is kept (code reads only `subscription.project`); and `alembic/env.py` imports both and uses `Base.metadata` as the target of autogenerate and `alembic check`. All reads and writes go through the Stores in `core/builtin`, components in `tools/`, and the optimizer's `errors.py` and `consolidation.py`, which only read (`logs`, and for consolidation the `payload` of `schedule` and `reservation` through lightweight `table()` constructs), using SQLAlchemy expressions without holding SQL strings.
modules.flow: In the runtime, `Runtime._run` writes `session` and `session_run` through `PostgresSessionStore`, `PostgresExecutionLogger` writes `logs`, Tools read and write `memory`, `workspace_slot`, the `channel` family, and `codex_session`, the component delivery `tools/discord/deliver.py` writes `discord_message`, and `tools/discord/feedback.py` reads it with `session_run` and writes `run_feedback`; in the queue, the run trace and usage APIs read `logs`, `session_run`, and `session`, and Discord intake writes `channel` through `PostgresChannelStore.resolve_session`.

key_symbols.name: Base
key_symbols.explain: The `DeclarativeBase` shared by all application tables; the scheduled-trigger definition table `schedule` and the legacy subscription tables whose data is kept, both in `queue/models.py`, are also registered on its metadata, and Alembic uses `Base.metadata` as the schema target.

key_symbols.name: ExecutionReceipt
key_symbols.explain: `execution_receipt`, a message success receipt with primary key `(namespace, message_id)`; a CHECK limits `attempts` to 0 through 3. The table and its data are kept, current code neither reads nor writes it, and the ORM definition is kept only for Alembic's comparison.

key_symbols.name: ExecutionAttempt
key_symbols.explain: `execution_attempt`, a record of each delivery attempt; `(namespace, message_id, token)` is unique, with the index `idx_execution_attempt_message`. The table and its data are kept; current code neither reads nor writes it.

key_symbols.name: ExecutionChild
key_symbols.explain: `execution_child`, child process records (`pid`, `birth_time`, `state`) with a foreign key to `execution_attempt.id`. The table and its data are kept; current code neither reads nor writes it.

key_symbols.name: ExecutionLog
key_symbols.explain: Append-only execution log rows of the `logs` table; `id` is `Identity()` (`GENERATED BY DEFAULT`), `execution_id` is unique, and there are three indexes on run, parent, and type. Written by `PostgresExecutionLogger.record` in `core/builtin/execution_log.py` (runtime executions and `tools/review.py`); `read_usage`, `read_run_trace`, `read_session_trace`, and `read_recent_runs` serve reads for the queue's `api/usage.py` and `api/runs.py`; in the runtime, the optimizer observes recent runs through `read_recent_runs`, `optimizer/errors.py` reads non-`ok` `agent` rows from the last 24 hours directly through the ORM, and `optimizer/consolidation.py` counts the runs and calls of the last 30 days and each component's first row; `tools/memory/baseline.py` reads the successful records of the `compare` agent.

key_symbols.name: Memory
key_symbols.explain: The `memory` table, key-value records with primary key `identity`. `tools/memory/store.py` reads and writes it, `tools/memory/baseline.py` updates it with row locks and saves backup rows separately, and `tools/pr_retire_sweep.py` reads records matching `github:%:pr:%:classified`.

key_symbols.name: WorkspaceSlot
key_symbols.explain: The `workspace_slot` table: for each slot of the always-on clone rack, the holder, lease, PR, branch, the head being processed while busy (`head_sha`, mutually exclusive per PR and head), and process information; `(owner_repo, slot_no)` is unique, and rows are only added, never deleted. Read and written by `tools/workspace_pool.py`.

key_symbols.name: Session
key_symbols.explain: The `session` table, with an arbitrary string primary key and the self-referencing foreign key `parent_session_id`. `begin_run` and `record_event_in` of `PostgresSessionStore` insert with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; `get_session` and the queue's `read_session_trace` read it.

key_symbols.name: SessionRun
key_symbols.explain: The `session_run` table, recording a run's `agent_name`, `data_json`, `request_json`, `status`, `response_json`, and the `code_version` at insert time; a CHECK limits `status` to 7 values. `Runtime._run` writes it through `begin_run` and `finish_run`; at runtime startup `recover_interrupted_runs` changes leftover `running` rows to `interrupted`; `record_event` appends completed external events; `tools/session_history.py` and the queue's `api/runs.py` read it.

key_symbols.name: DiscordMessage
key_symbols.explain: `discord_message`, one row per Discord message (chunk) the bot sent: `channel_id`, `delivery_id` shared by the chunks of one delivery, and the nullable `run_id` and `execution_id` of the execution that sent it, with the index `idx_discord_message_run`. The component `tools/discord/deliver.py` writes it after sending; `tools/discord/feedback.py` reads it to find the run a rated message came from.

key_symbols.name: RunFeedback
key_symbols.explain: `run_feedback`, the owner's 👍/👎 on a bot Discord message, one row per rated message: `run_id`, `session_id`, and `execution_id` copied from `discord_message` and `session_run`, `rating` limited by a CHECK to `up` or `down`, `rated_at`, a unique `question_message_id` for the 👎 question, and `reasons` (JSONB array of `{message_id, text, at}`), with indexes on run and session. Written only by the component `tools/discord/feedback.py`.

key_symbols.name: Channel
key_symbols.explain: The `channel` table, mapping the `(provider, channel_id)` primary key to one `session_id` (no foreign key). Read and written by `PostgresChannelStore`: the queue's Discord intake assigns sessions with `resolve_session`, and in the runtime `tools/channel_link.py` (`get_channel` lookups, `resolve_session` writes), `tools/issue_workflow.py` (`get_channel`), and `agent/dispatch.py` (`channel_for_session`) read and write it.

key_symbols.name: ProjectChannel
key_symbols.explain: The `project_channel` table, mapping a project label (primary key) to its announcement channel (`channel_id` unique). Read and written by the project channel methods of `PostgresChannelStore`: `tools/channel_link.py` calls `resolve_project_channel` and `set_project_channel`, and `agent/dispatch.py` reads it with `project_for_channel`.

key_symbols.name: SessionSource
key_symbols.explain: The `session_source` table, with primary key `(session_id, source_url)` (no foreign key to `session`). Read and written by `attach_source`, `list_sources`, `channels_for_source`, and `clear_sources_for_channel` of `PostgresChannelStore`, called from `tools/channel_link.py`, `tools/issue_workflow.py`, and `agent/dispatch.py`.

key_symbols.name: CodexSession
key_symbols.explain: The `codex_session` table, with primary key `(session_id, cwd, project, mode)`, unique `codex_session_id`, and `mode` limited by a CHECK to `implement` or `review`. Read by `PostgresCodexSessionStore` (used by `tools/codex_session.py`) and written with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a different ID already saved is never overwritten.

invariants: All core table classes inherit from the same `Base`; schema creation and changes are made only by Alembic, and `alembic check` compares `Base.metadata` (including the 4 tables in `queue/models.py`: `schedule`, `subscription`, `schedule_cursor`, `schedule_outbox`) with the DB.

Models define no relationships; the only foreign keys are `session.parent_session_id`, `session_run.session_id`, and `codex_session.session_id` to `session`, and `execution_child.attempt_id` to `execution_attempt`; `channel` and `session_source` have no foreign key to `session`, and `discord_message` and `run_feedback` have none to `session_run`.

The CHECK on `session_run.status` allows `running`, `ok`, `error`, `max_steps`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, and `interrupted`; `workspace_slot`'s `(owner_repo, slot_no)`, `project_channel.channel_id`, `logs.execution_id`, and `codex_session.codex_session_id` are unique.
`logs.code_version` and `session_run.code_version` are filled by `current_code_version()` at insert time; `finish_run` and `recover_interrupted_runs` do not modify `session_run.code_version`.
The declaration order of columns matches the column order of the deployed tables.
pitfalls: Changing a type, default, CHECK, or index requires generating a revision with `alembic revision --autogenerate` and making `uv run alembic check` report no difference. The schema-related tests are `tests/entry/test_schema.py`, which checks revisions, and `tests/entry/test_cancelled_status.py` (AS18), which checks the CHECK on `session_run.status` and the migration history.

`include_object` in `alembic/env.py` excludes tables that exist in the DB but not in the metadata, so deleting a table class from this file makes autogenerate produce no drop and `alembic check` report no difference; dropping a table requires a hand-written drop in a revision (e.g. `d490c91bce9c`).
The CHECK on `session_run` allows `skipped`, but `AgentStatus` has only `ok`, `max_steps`, `error`, and `cancelled`, and current code never writes `skipped`.

Time column types are mixed: `workspace_slot` and the execution tables use `Double` epoch seconds, `logs.started_at` and `memory.saved_at` use `Text`, and `session`, `session_run`, `channel`, `session_source`, `codex_session`, and `project_channel` use `timestamptz`.

The queue process imports `queue/models.py` through the scheduled trigger's `integration/schedule.py`, and the runtime imports it through `queue/project_labels.py`, so `Base.metadata` in both processes contains this file's 12 tables and the 4 tables of `queue/models.py`.
