groups.overview: `core/versioning` is the component version store. Components (`agent/`, `tools/`, `skills/`, `harnesses/`, `sources/`) are versioned in git, and a version is a commit (version id = the 40-character commit SHA, label `c.<first 8>`). People work in the working copy `components/` and push to the shared main: the component repository on GitHub (`COMPONENT_REPO_URL`) or, in local mode, the mirror itself, whose first main is the package's default components. `snapshot` defines the five version-owned folders, which paths belong to a version, the path checks of a new tree, and logical module names. `store` defines `Commit`, the `VersionStore` Protocol, and its git implementation `GitVersionStore`, which reads and writes the bare mirror `COMPONENT_REPO_DIR` (`refs/heads/main` = the adopted main, `refs/remotes/origin/main` = GitHub's main at the last fetch, `refs/te/forks/<id>` = optimizer candidates) and, with GitHub, fetches from and pushes to its main; in local mode `fetch` reads the mirror's main, `push` fast-forwards it, and `initial_tree` gives the package's default components for the first main (the two modes are the internal strategies `_GitHubUpstream` and `_LocalUpstream`); the function `ensure_working_copy` clones the mirror into `components/`. `loader` loads the source of the version's 4 module folders into the reserved namespace `_te_versions.v_<version id>` and rewrites owned absolute imports, so old and new versions coexist. `Repo` in `repo` handles `start` (loading the mirror's main, or adopting the shared main when the mirror has none, or making the package's default components the first local main), `refresh` (loading a new mirror main), `sync` (reading the shared main and adopting it only when it loads), `fork` (writing and keeping a new version with a given version as its parent, without changing main), `merge` (putting a candidate on top of the latest shared main, pushing it or fast-forwarding the mirror, and only then switching), `ensure_working_copy`, `validate`, and releasing versions; `RunVersions` is a run's handle for obtaining Agents, pinning each Agent by name to the main at the time it was first obtained. `__main__` is the check CLI that the Host's `scripts/component-hooks` run (`pre-push` of a clone, `pre-receive` of the local mirror) (`python -m trackeverything.core.versioning check`): it loads a commit with the runtime's Host services and reads or writes neither the mirror nor main. `Runtime.execute` calls `refresh` at the start of each message and `TrackingRuntime` calls `sync` every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`, so new runs use the new main and running runs finish on their original version. Host-side composition (`HostServices`, `build_agents`), the catalog, and the code version display value live in `core/builtin`; the queue process does not load this package.

modules.role: Declaration of the `core/versioning` package; its docstring outlines the division of work: versions are commits of the component repository, the runtime loads the main of the bare mirror (store, snapshot, loader), repo provides sync, fork, merge (rebase and push), and the run handle, and the CLI checks commits.
modules.summary: Has no public names; it contains only a docstring and runs no code. Users import each submodule directly by its full path. The runtime process loads `repo` and `store` (plus `loader` and `snapshot` through `repo`) through `core/builtin/app.py` and `core/builtin/runtime.py`; the queue process does not load this package.
modules.flow: Takes no part in the runtime flow; it is loaded only as the parent package when any submodule is imported.

modules.role: The check CLI: loads a commit of the component repository with the same Host services as the runtime and reports whether it loads; the component repository's pre-push hook runs it for every push to `main`.
modules.summary: `main(argv)` parses the `check` subcommand, `--repo` (a git working tree or repository; default the current directory), and an optional revision (default `HEAD`) with argparse and runs `check_command` with `asyncio.run`. `check_command` first calls `require_schema_head(config.DATABASE_URL)`, then builds the component graph function with `prepare_components(open_host_services())` (the same services as the runtime), opens a read-only `GitVersionStore(repository)` (no URL, so it neither creates a mirror nor uses the network), resolves the revision to a commit SHA with `resolve`, reads the commit's five-folder tree with `read_tree`, and calls `Repo(source, components).validate(tree)`, which loads every module in this process, builds the component graph, and releases it without storing anything. Success prints `ok <SHA>` and returns 0; an unknown revision prints `unknown revision: <rev>`, and any other failure prints the single `describe_failure` line (path and line inside the version, and the exception) to stderr, returning 1; in `finally` it closes the `Repo` it created. It never reads or writes the mirror or main and does not use `open_repo` (no singleton). The Host's `scripts/component-hooks` run `bash "<checkout>/scripts/run_local.sh" python -m trackeverything.core.versioning check --repo <repository> <sha>` through the launcher of the checkout that holds them: `pre-push` (a clone's `core.hooksPath`) for each update of `refs/heads/main` (deletions excluded), stopping the push on failure, and `pre-receive` (the local mirror's `core.hooksPath`, set by the runtime) for the new tip of `refs/heads/main`, refusing the push on failure or when main is deleted.
modules.flow: Run by the pre-push hook of a clone of the component repository (or by hand) before a commit reaches GitHub's main; the runtime's `sync` validates the pushed main again before adopting it, so a bypassed hook cannot make the runtime run a main that does not load.

key_symbols.name: check_command
key_symbols.explain: Checks the schema, builds the Host services and the component graph function, resolves `revision` in `repository` with `GitVersionStore.resolve`, and calls `Repo.validate` on its tree; prints `ok <SHA>` and returns 0, or prints one line to stderr and returns 1, and finally closes the `Repo`.

key_symbols.name: main
key_symbols.explain: The CLI entry point `main(argv) -> int`: parses `check [--repo <git working tree>] [<rev>]` and runs `check_command`; when executed with `python -m`, its return value becomes the exit code.

invariants: The CLI neither reads nor writes the mirror (`COMPONENT_REPO_DIR`) or any ref; it reads only the given repository and stores nothing.

A commit passes only when all its modules load and its component graph builds with the same `open_host_services()` and `prepare_components` as the runtime; the tree is the five folders of the commit (other files of the component repository are not part of a version).
pitfalls: `require_schema_head`, `open_host_services()`, and the git reads are all inside the `try`: configuration errors such as a schema not at head or an unconfigured LLM also print the single `describe_failure` line to stderr (when there is no frame inside the version, it uses the path and line of the last frame), and the exit code is 1; run it through the deploy checkout's `scripts/run_local.sh` so the settings match the always-on service.

The hook checks against the deployed Host: deploy a Host contract change (such as the arguments of `build_agents`) in a form the current components still load with before pushing components that need it.
During validation, the top-level code of the version's modules runs once in the CLI process.
The hook checks only pushes to `refs/heads/main` and can be bypassed (`--no-verify`, a push from another machine or a cloud session); the runtime's `sync` still refuses a main that does not load.

modules.role: Loads a version's modules from the source in the version tree under the reserved namespace `_te_versions.v_<version id>`, and points the version's owned absolute imports at that version.
modules.summary: `install` registers `VersionFinder` at the head of `sys.meta_path` only once; it resolves only names starting with `_te_versions`. Ancestor namespaces, version roots, and intermediate packages without source use `_EmptyPackage` (empty `__path__`), `_te_versions.v_<version id>.trackeverything` uses `_Facade`, and modules with source use `SnapshotLoader`, whose origin is the path on the version's file view. `_Facade` uses a module-level `__getattr__` to forward `MODULE_FOLDERS` (`agent`, `tools`, `harnesses`, `sources`) to that version and other names to the canonical `trackeverything` package. `SnapshotLoader.exec_module` parses the source into an AST, and `OwnedImportRewriter` rewrites level-0 imports of owned modules and the `trackeverything` name into the version namespace, while imports of shared modules such as `core` stay canonical, which preserves type identity and keeps locks shared across versions. `register`/`unregister` maintain the registry from version name (`v_<version id>`) to `Version`, called by `Repo._load` and `Repo._dispose`.
modules.flow: When the version store loads a version (`Repo._load`: `start`, `refresh`, `sync`, `fork`, `merge`, `validate`), it loads all modules in a thread, executing the source through `VersionFinder` and `SnapshotLoader`; imports inside version modules during Agent execution are also resolved this way.

key_symbols.name: ROOT
key_symbols.explain: The root name `_te_versions` of the reserved namespace; `core/shared_state.py` uses the same prefix to refuse sharing instances of version-owned classes.

key_symbols.name: _OWNED_ROOTS
key_symbols.explain: The root names of the 4 owned modules such as `trackeverything.agent`, generated from `MODULE_FOLDERS`.

key_symbols.name: is_owned
key_symbols.explain: Decides whether a module name equals or lies under `_OWNED_ROOTS`, i.e. whether it is version-owned.

key_symbols.name: register
key_symbols.explain: Registers a `Version` under its version name (`v_<version id>`) under `_registry_lock` so that the finder can resolve its namespace.

key_symbols.name: unregister
key_symbols.explain: Deletes the registration only when the registered entry is the same `Version` object.

key_symbols.name: install
key_symbols.explain: Inserts `VersionFinder` at the head of `sys.meta_path` only once, using the `_installed` flag.

key_symbols.name: _EmptyPackage
key_symbols.explain: A loader that executes no code, used for namespace ancestors and intermediate packages without `__init__.py` source; `__path__` is empty, so the disk is not searched.

key_symbols.name: _Facade
key_symbols.explain: The loader of the `trackeverything` package inside a version; forwards version components to that version and other names to the shared package.

key_symbols.name: _Facade.exec_module
key_symbols.explain: Sets a module-level `__getattr__`: names in `MODULE_FOLDERS` import the version package; for other names it first takes the canonical package's attribute and then tries to import `trackeverything.<name>`; dunder names and names that cannot be found raise `AttributeError`.

key_symbols.name: SnapshotLoader
key_symbols.explain: An `InspectLoader` that loads one module from the version's source dictionary, holding the version, the logical name, and the origin on the file view.

key_symbols.name: SnapshotLoader.get_source
key_symbols.explain: Returns the source from the version's `sources`, or None when the logical name is absent; traceback formatting that still holds the loader after the version is released also calls it.

key_symbols.name: SnapshotLoader.exec_module
key_symbols.explain: Parses the source, rewrites it with `OwnedImportRewriter`, compiles it with `dont_inherit=True`, and executes it in the module's `__dict__`.

key_symbols.name: VersionFinder
key_symbols.explain: A meta path finder that resolves only the reserved namespace; returns None for modules absent from the version without falling back to disk.

key_symbols.name: VersionFinder.find_spec
key_symbols.explain: Returns, by name level, a spec for `_EmptyPackage`, `_Facade`, or a `SnapshotLoader` with `has_location`; returns None for unregistered version names or nonexistent modules.

key_symbols.name: OwnedImportRewriter
key_symbols.explain: An AST transformer that points owned absolute imports at one version; strings, relative imports, and shared imports are left unchanged.

key_symbols.name: OwnedImportRewriter.visit_ImportFrom
key_symbols.explain: Rewrites absolute `from` imports of version-owned modules and of `trackeverything` itself to the version namespace; relative imports and other modules are unchanged.

key_symbols.name: OwnedImportRewriter.visit_Import
key_symbols.explain: Rewrites each name of an `import` statement through `_rewrite`: a version-owned module is imported from the version (without an alias, the module is loaded and the `trackeverything` name is bound to the version facade), `import trackeverything [as x]` binds the facade, and other `trackeverything.*` imports keep the shared module and rebind `trackeverything` to the facade.

key_symbols.name: OwnedImportRewriter.visit_Call
key_symbols.explain: Raises `ImportError` when it finds `import_module` or `__import__` called on an owned module with a string constant, advising the use of an import statement instead.

invariants: `VersionFinder.find_spec` returns None for names that do not start with `_te_versions` and takes no part in other imports.
Names present in neither the version source nor `virtual_packages` return None; packages inside a version have an empty `__path__`, so the disk is not searched.
Only level-0 absolute imports and the `trackeverything` name are rewritten; the targets of relative imports, strings, and imports of shared modules are unchanged.
The `trackeverything` name in a version module is bound to that version's facade, so the 4 owned folders resolve to the same version and the shared parts resolve to the canonical package.
`install` registers the finder only once; `unregister` deletes only when the registered entry is the same `Version` object.
pitfalls: Calling `importlib.import_module` or `__import__` on an owned module with a string constant in a version module raises `ImportError` at load time (the version fails to load); use an import statement instead. Passing the name through a variable is not detected and loads the canonical module.

Code outside version modules (scripts and tests; the Host imports no component module) that imports version-owned names gets the modules of the installed `trackeverything` package, if it has them, which are not a version and do not follow main switches.
`skills/` is not in `MODULE_FOLDERS`, so imports of names under `trackeverything.skills` in version modules are not rewritten and go through the canonical import.
After a version is unregistered with `unregister`, modules under that version name that are not yet in `sys.modules` fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

modules.role: The version store: holds main, handles loading, syncing with the shared main, forking, merging (rebase, then push or fast-forward), validating, and releasing versions, and gives each run a handle for obtaining Agents by name; a process has only one version store, created as a singleton by `open_repo` and obtained with `current_repo()`.
modules.summary: `Version` is a loaded version: it holds `commit`, `id` (the commit SHA), `label` (`c.<first 8 chars of id>`), `namespace` (`_te_versions.v_<id>`), the read-only `tree` and `sources`, the file view directory, the component graph `graph`, and the user count `users` (held for a block with `in_use()`); its module index comes from `snapshot.index_modules`. `Repo._load` (run in a thread) first calls `loader.register`, writes the tree as a read-only file view, loads all modules in name order, then builds the `ComponentGraph` with the `build` passed at construction (the function returned by `prepare_components`) and sets each Agent's `version_label` to the version's `label`; if any step fails it calls `_dispose` and re-raises. `start` loads the mirror's main; when the mirror has none, `_adopt_first_main` takes the shared main with `store.fetch()` (or, when there is none, `_initial_version` writes `store.initial_tree()` as the root commit `INITIAL_MESSAGE` through `_new_commit`), loads it, and adopts it with `move_main(None, id)` (using the mirror's main instead if another process created one first), raising on failure (aborting startup). `refresh` returns without taking the lock when the mirror's main equals the loaded main; otherwise it loads and switches. `refresh` and `sync` load a candidate the same way through `_load_candidate`: a missing commit or a version that does not load is recorded in `_failed` and logged at error level (the latter with the single `describe_failure` line), and a read failure only logs a warning and is retried next time; in every case the loaded main stays in use. `sync` reads the shared main with `store.fetch()` (a fetch from GitHub, or the mirror's own main in local mode); when it differs from the loaded main and is not in `_failed`, it loads it and adopts it with `_advance_main` (compare-and-swap of the mirror's main, then switching this process); a failed fetch logs a warning; a force-pushed main outside the adopted history is adopted when it loads. New versions are created through `_new_commit`: `check_paths` checks the paths and the parent must be a stored commit; `store.write` writes the tree as a commit at the `clock()` time (whole seconds; when the same commit already exists it returns None and the time moves on one second, so every fork is a new version); the version is then loaded and built, and only then kept with `store.keep` (a fork ref); on any failure what was loaded is released and no ref is created. `fork(parent, tree, message)` creates such a version without changing main and returns its `Commit`. `merge(version_id)` reads the shared main R with `store.fetch()`: when R already contains the candidate, it pushes nothing and returns main; when R is the candidate's parent, it loads the candidate; otherwise `_merge_target` merges three ways with `store.merge_tree(candidate.parent, R, candidate)` into a new version whose parent is R and whose message is the candidate's plus `Rebased-From: <candidate id>` (through `_new_commit`). It then advances the shared main with `store.push` (a non-force push to GitHub, or a fast-forward of the mirror's main in local mode; a refusal raises `PushRejected`), and only after that succeeds moves the mirror's main and switches this process, returning the target's `Commit`. Conflicts raise `MergeConflict`, git and network failures `GitError`, and load failures their own exception; in every failure the mirror's main does not move. `validate(tree)` loads a tree under a random id and builds its graph without storing it, then releases it (the check CLI). Loading in `start`, `refresh`, and `sync`, and `fork`, `merge`, `validate`, and `close` are serialized by a single `asyncio.Lock`; `_exclusive()` takes it, checks that the store is open, and runs `_collect` at the end. `run()` returns a `RunVersions`: the first call of `version(name)` records the main at that moment (even if the version has no such name), later calls return the same version, and each version's `users` is incremented only once; `agent(name)` returns that version's `graph.agents.get(name)`. `release(run)` ends the run's use (`RunVersions.end`) and releases versions that are not main and have no users; when main switches, the old main is released immediately if nobody uses it. Releasing (`_dispose`) removes the loader registration, the namespace's modules and root package attribute in `sys.modules`, linecache entries, the component graph, and the file view; commits remain in the mirror, and references held outside its management are not broken. `close` releases all versions, and later operations raise `RuntimeError`.
modules.flow: The runtime's `build_runtime` creates the singleton with `open_repo(prepare_components(services))` and calls `start`, then in local mode `store.ensure_working_copy(config.COMPONENT_REPO_DIR, config.COMPONENTS_DIR)` (a failure only logs a warning); `Runtime.execute` runs `refresh` → `run()` → `release(run)` for each message, `TrackingRuntime` calls `sync` every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL`, and `publish_catalog` reads `main_version`. `fork` and `merge` are called by the optimizer's `errors` check through `current_repo()`: it forks the repaired tree from main and then merges it, which pushes to GitHub's main or fast-forwards the local mirror. The check CLI builds its own `Repo` over the repository being checked and calls only `validate`.

key_symbols.name: _VIEW_FILE
key_symbols.explain: Regex matching version file paths on the file view (`.../v_<id>/trackeverything/<relative path>`); `describe_failure` uses it to shorten paths to relative paths.

key_symbols.name: UnknownVersion
key_symbols.explain: A version id that is not stored (subclass of `LookupError`); no prefix matching is done (an id is the full 40-character SHA).

key_symbols.name: PushRejected
key_symbols.explain: Raised by `merge` when the shared main cannot be advanced: GitHub rejects the push, or the local mirror's main moved after it was read; nothing changed and the mirror's main is unchanged. `repo` also re-exports `Commit`, `GitError`, and `MergeConflict` from `store`.

key_symbols.name: Version
key_symbols.explain: A loaded version, holding `commit`, `id`, `label`, `name` (`v_<id>`), `namespace`, the read-only `tree` and `sources`, `packages`, `virtual_packages`, `view_dir`, and `users`; the module index comes from `snapshot.index_modules`, which raises `ValueError` for non-UTF-8 modules.

key_symbols.name: Version.graph
key_symbols.explain: Property returning the component graph; raises `RuntimeError` when it is not built yet or has been released.

key_symbols.name: Version.module
key_symbols.explain: Returns a module of this version (from `sys.modules` if loaded, otherwise loaded from the tree).

key_symbols.name: Version.modules
key_symbols.explain: Returns the modules this version has loaded (logical name → module), used by `publish_catalog` to collect declared classes.

key_symbols.name: Version.view_path
key_symbols.explain: Returns the path on the version's immutable file view (e.g. `skills/alpha/SKILL.md`), used for module origins and as the read location of Skills.

key_symbols.name: RunVersions
key_symbols.explain: A run's handle for obtaining Agents (an implementation of `AgentLookup`); holds the table pinning names to versions and the list of versions in use, and is placed in `AgentContext.agents`.

key_symbols.name: RunVersions.version
key_symbols.explain: Returns the version for a name: the first call records the main at that moment, later calls return the same version; each version's `users` is incremented only once; raises `RuntimeError` after `release`.

key_symbols.name: RunVersions.agent
key_symbols.explain: Returns `graph.agents.get(name)` of the pinned version, or None when the version has no such name.

key_symbols.name: describe_failure
key_symbols.explain: Condenses a version load or build failure into one line `<path>:<line>: <exception type>: <message>`: SyntaxError uses its filename and lineno, other exceptions use the last frame inside the version in the traceback; it includes no source lines and does not format the traceback.

key_symbols.name: Repo
key_symbols.explain: The version store: constructor parameters are the `VersionStore`, the component graph build function `build`, an optional `view_root` (when omitted, a temporary directory is created and deleted on `close`), and `clock` (creation time of new versions, default `datetime.now(UTC)`); calls `loader.install()` at construction.

key_symbols.name: Repo.main
key_symbols.explain: Property returning the `Commit` of the loaded main.

key_symbols.name: Repo.main_version
key_symbols.explain: Property returning the `Version` of the loaded main; raises `RuntimeError` before `start` or after `close`.

key_symbols.name: Repo.start
key_symbols.explain: Loads the mirror's main; when the mirror has none, `_adopt_first_main` takes the shared main (fetching GitHub's), or in local mode writes the store's `initial_tree()` (the package's default components) as the root commit `Initial components`; loads it and adopts it with `move_main(None, id)`. Raises on failure (no main to adopt, a failed fetch or load), which aborts startup.

key_symbols.name: Repo.refresh
key_symbols.explain: Loads and switches when the mirror's main differs from the loaded one (through `_load_candidate`); load failures and read failures are only logged, and the loaded main stays in use; returns main's `Commit`.

key_symbols.name: Repo.sync
key_symbols.explain: Reads the shared main (fetching GitHub's; nothing is fetched in local mode) and, when it differs from the loaded main and has not failed before, loads it through `_load_candidate` and adopts it as the mirror's main (compare-and-swap) and this process's main; a failed fetch or read is a warning retried next time, and a main that does not load is logged once at error level and not adopted; returns main's `Commit`.

key_symbols.name: Repo.fork
key_symbols.explain: Writes the tree as a new commit whose parent is the stored `parent`, loads and validates it, keeps it as a fork ref, and returns its `Commit`; the commit time moves on one second while the same commit exists, so every fork is a new version; main does not change; raises `UnknownVersion` when `parent` is unknown.

key_symbols.name: Repo.merge
key_symbols.explain: Advances the shared main to the candidate (rebased on top of it, with `Rebased-From`, when the shared main is not its parent): a non-force push to GitHub, or a fast-forward of the local mirror's main. Only after that succeeds does it move the mirror's main and return that `Commit`; returns main without changes when the shared main already contains the candidate. Raises `UnknownVersion`, `MergeConflict`, `PushRejected`, `GitError`, or the load exception without moving the mirror's main.

key_symbols.name: Repo.validate
key_symbols.explain: Loads a tree and builds its component graph without storing it, then releases it; raises on failure (used by the check CLI).

key_symbols.name: Repo.log
key_symbols.explain: Returns the versions reachable from main and the kept forks (newest first).

key_symbols.name: Repo.tree
key_symbols.explain: Returns a copy of the version's tree; raises `UnknownVersion` for an unknown id.

key_symbols.name: Repo.run
key_symbols.explain: Creates a run handle `RunVersions`.

key_symbols.name: Repo.release
key_symbols.explain: Ends the run's use of its versions (`RunVersions.end`) and releases versions that are not main and have no users; a second call does nothing.

key_symbols.name: Repo.close
key_symbols.explain: Waits for cancelled loads to finish, then releases all versions and deletes the view root it created; later operations raise `RuntimeError`; clears the singleton if it is the singleton.

key_symbols.name: Repo._new_commit
key_symbols.explain: Checks paths, confirms the parent is stored, writes the commit with `store.write` (moving the time on one second while the same commit exists), runs `_load` in a thread, and then keeps it with `store.keep`; releases the loaded version if keeping fails.

key_symbols.name: Repo._advance_main
key_symbols.explain: Reads the mirror's main and moves it to the version with `move_main` (compare-and-swap), holding the version with `in_use()` across the read and the move so a concurrent lock-free `release` cannot dispose it; when it moved and main is loaded, switches this process to it; returns whether it moved.

key_symbols.name: Repo._ensure_loaded
key_symbols.explain: Returns the loaded version, or reads the commit and tree from the store and runs `_load` in a thread when it is not loaded.

key_symbols.name: Repo._collect
key_symbols.explain: Releases every loaded version that is not main and whose `users` is not greater than 0.

key_symbols.name: Repo._load_in_thread
key_symbols.explain: Runs `_load` in a thread. When the caller is cancelled, the cancellation propagates immediately while the thread keeps loading to completion, and the resulting version is released when the thread ends; if a cancelled load of the same version id is still pending, it waits for that release before loading again (the namespace and file view are determined by the id).

key_symbols.name: Repo._load
key_symbols.explain: Loads a version outside the event loop: registers the loader, writes the read-only file view, loads all modules, builds the component graph, and sets each Agent's `version_label`; on failure it releases everything and raises.

key_symbols.name: Repo._dispose
key_symbols.explain: Releases one version: unregisters the loader, deletes the namespace's modules in `sys.modules`, the root package's attribute, and linecache entries, clears the component graph, and deletes the file view (directories that fail to delete are retried at the next release).

key_symbols.name: open_repo
key_symbols.explain: Creates this process's version store and sets it as the singleton: when `store` is omitted, uses `GitVersionStore(config.COMPONENT_REPO_DIR, config.COMPONENT_REPO_URL, ssh_key=config.COMPONENT_REPO_SSH_KEY, hooks=HOOKS_DIR, seed=PACKAGE_ROOT)` (an empty URL is local mode); raises `RuntimeError` when the singleton is already open; does not load main (`start` loads it).

key_symbols.name: current_repo
key_symbols.explain: Returns this process's version store singleton; raises `RuntimeError` when none has been opened with `open_repo` (or it has been closed with `close`). The optimizer uses it to call `refresh`, `fork`, and `merge`.

key_symbols.name: PACKAGE_ROOT
key_symbols.explain: The package root (`src/trackeverything`). `open_repo` passes it as the store's `seed`: in local mode its five folders (the default components) become the first main.

key_symbols.name: HOOKS_DIR
key_symbols.explain: The Host checkout's `scripts/component-hooks` (`pre-push`, `pre-receive`). `open_repo` passes it as the store's `hooks`, which becomes the mirror's `core.hooksPath`.

key_symbols.name: INITIAL_MESSAGE
key_symbols.explain: `Initial components`: the message of the first local main that `start` writes from the package's default components.

key_symbols.name: Version.in_use
key_symbols.explain: Context manager that holds the version as in use (`users` + 1) for a block, so the lock-free `release()` does not dispose it while an operation awaits.

key_symbols.name: RunVersions.end
key_symbols.explain: Decrements `users` once for every version the run used and marks the handle released; a second call does nothing. `Repo.release` calls it.

key_symbols.name: Repo._exclusive
key_symbols.explain: Async context manager for operations that change the store: takes the lock, checks that the store is open, and runs `_collect` when the block ends.

key_symbols.name: Repo._load_candidate
key_symbols.explain: Loads a main candidate for `refresh` and `sync`, or returns None after logging: a missing commit or a version that does not load goes into `_failed` (error), a read failure is a warning retried next time.

key_symbols.name: Repo._adopt_first_main
key_symbols.explain: With no mirror main: takes the shared main, or the version of the store's initial tree (`_initial_version`), loads it, and makes it the mirror's main; returns the main another process adopted first, if any.

key_symbols.name: Repo._merge_target
key_symbols.explain: The version a merge advances the shared main to: the candidate when the shared main is its parent, otherwise the candidate rebased onto the shared main with `merge_tree` (message with `Rebased-From`).

invariants: A version is a git commit and its id is the full 40-character SHA; the same tree can have several versions (forks of identical content get distinct commit times); Repo does not re-verify the id of a loaded version.

The mirror's main changes only through the compare-and-swap `move_main(expected, new)`: in `start` (when the mirror has none), in `sync` (adopting a shared main that loads), and in `merge` only after the push succeeds, so with GitHub the adopted main is always a commit GitHub's main has had; in local mode a person's push, checked by the `pre-receive` hook, moves it directly.

A new version is loaded and its component graph built before it is kept or pushed; if loading or building fails, whatever was loaded is released and the error is raised, leaving no fork ref and pushing nothing.
Only `merge` advances the shared main from the runtime (a push to GitHub's main, never with force, or a fast-forward of the local mirror's main); forks are never pushed.

Within one run, the same name returns the same version from its first lookup until `release`; different names can land on different versions (a name first looked up after main switches mid-run uses the new main).
A version that is not main and has no users is released immediately; releasing does not delete commits or clear `shared_state` objects.
An unknown version id (`merge`, `tree`, `parent` of `fork`) raises `UnknownVersion` (`LookupError`); no prefix matching is done.
Loading in `start`, `refresh`, and `sync`, and `fork`, `merge`, `validate`, and `close` are serialized by one `asyncio.Lock`; `refresh` does not take the lock when main is unchanged.
pitfalls: A main id that fails to load (in `refresh` or `sync`) is recorded in `_failed` and is not retried in this process until restart (the same applies when the commit is missing from the mirror); a transient read or fetch failure only logs a warning, is not recorded, and is retried the next time.
Parent and child agents in the same run can come from different versions: when a child agent's name is first looked up after main switches, the child uses the new main.

`merge` returns main without changing anything when the shared main already contains the candidate; the adoption of that main is left to `sync`, so the returned `Commit` can be the older mirror main. A candidate whose change conflicts with a person's push raises `MergeConflict`; fork again from the new main to retry.
A rebased version is a new commit: the pushed id differs from the candidate's, and its message records `Rebased-From: <candidate id>`.
When `move_main` loses after a successful push (another process moved the mirror's main), `merge` logs a warning and returns the pushed version; the next `sync` adopts the shared main.
Modules or Agent instances still referenced outside its management after release stay alive, but their file view has been deleted and `sys.modules` no longer has aliases for them.
`describe_failure` does not format the traceback (to keep linecache from re-holding the source of a released version) and gives only the path and line of the last frame inside the version.
`main` and `main_version` raise `RuntimeError` before `start` or after `close`; the Repo of the check CLI never calls `start`, so it has no main.

A process can have only one version store: two version stores would share the same version's module namespace `_te_versions.v_<id>`, and a release by one would remove the other's modules. `open_repo` raises `RuntimeError` while the singleton is not closed; a version store constructed directly with `Repo(...)` (for tests) does not become the singleton.

modules.role: Defines the five version-owned folders and which paths of the component repository belong to a version, checks the paths of a new tree, and maps module files to logical names.
modules.summary: `OWNED` is the five folders `agent`, `tools`, `skills`, `harnesses`, `sources`, and `MODULE_FOLDERS` the 4 of them loaded as modules (`.py` files under `skills/` and every other file are resources). `skipped` decides that a path is never part of a version (`__pycache__`, a segment starting with `.`, `.pyc`); `owned` decides that a path of the component repository belongs to a version (under one of the five folders, at least two segments, and not skipped), so files at the repository root such as `README.md` and `.githooks/` are not part of a version. `check_paths` raises `ValueError` for keys of a new tree that are absolute paths, contain empty segments, `.`/`..`, or backslashes, or are not under the five folders. `package_tree` reads the regular files of a package's five folders (the first local main). `logical_name` maps a `.py` under `MODULE_FOLDERS` whose segments are all identifiers to a logical name (`agent/review.py` → `trackeverything.agent.review`), and `module_path` is its inverse; `index_modules` builds a version's `ModuleIndex` (logical name → source, packages with source, and intermediate packages without source), raising `ValueError` for non-UTF-8 modules. It uses no git, hashing, or file system.
modules.flow: `GitVersionStore` uses `owned` to select a commit's files and `OWNED` to keep the parent's files outside the five folders when writing; `Repo._new_commit` and `Repo.validate` call `check_paths`; `Version` uses `logical_name` to tell modules from resources, and `loader` uses `MODULE_FOLDERS` and `module_path` to find the origin on the file view.

key_symbols.name: OWNED
key_symbols.explain: The five version-owned folders `agent`, `tools`, `skills`, `harnesses`, `sources` at the root of the component repository (the same relative paths as under `src/trackeverything`).

key_symbols.name: MODULE_FOLDERS
key_symbols.explain: The 4 folders loaded as modules, excluding `skills` (whose `.py` files are Skill script resources).

key_symbols.name: PACKAGE_NAME
key_symbols.explain: The package name `trackeverything`, used in logical names and file view paths.

key_symbols.name: skipped
key_symbols.explain: Decides whether a path contains `__pycache__` or a segment starting with `.`, or has the extension `.pyc`; such paths are never part of a version.

key_symbols.name: owned
key_symbols.explain: Decides whether a repository path belongs to a version: under one of the five folders (at least two segments) and not `skipped`.

key_symbols.name: check_paths
key_symbols.explain: Raises `ValueError` when a tree key is an absolute path, contains an empty segment, `.`, `..`, or a backslash, or is not under the five folders.

key_symbols.name: logical_name
key_symbols.explain: Maps `agent/review.py` to (`trackeverything.agent.review`, False); `__init__.py` maps to a package; returns None for a `.py` not under `MODULE_FOLDERS` or one containing a non-identifier segment.

key_symbols.name: module_path
key_symbols.explain: The inverse of `logical_name`; finds the relative path of a logical name in the file view.

key_symbols.name: package_tree
key_symbols.explain: Reads the regular files of a package's five folders (synchronous; symlinks and `skipped` paths are left out, as in a git tree): the tree of the first local main.

key_symbols.name: ModuleIndex
key_symbols.explain: The module index of a version: `sources` (logical name → source), `packages` (packages with source, `__init__.py` or the parent of another module), and `virtual` (intermediate packages without source).

key_symbols.name: index_modules
key_symbols.explain: Builds the `ModuleIndex` of a tree from the `.py` files `logical_name` maps; raises `ValueError` for non-UTF-8 modules.

invariants: A version's tree contains only paths for which `owned` is true; keys are POSIX paths relative to the repository root (equal to paths relative to `src/trackeverything`), and the first segment is always one of `OWNED`.
The module/resource distinction depends only on the path: a `.py` under `MODULE_FOLDERS` with identifier segments is a module, everything else is a resource.
pitfalls: Empty folders do not enter a tree (git does not store them); a folder containing only skipped files is treated as nonexistent.
A `.py` in `MODULE_FOLDERS` whose name contains a non-identifier segment has a `logical_name` of None and is loaded as a resource, not a module.
Non-UTF-8 module files are not detected here; they fail at `Version` construction with `ValueError` (`<relative path>: not UTF-8`).

`check_paths` applies only to trees the Host writes or validates (forks, rebased merges, the check CLI); a commit pushed by a person is filtered by `owned` instead, so its files outside the five folders are ignored rather than rejected.

modules.role: Defines `Commit`, the value of a stored version, the errors `GitError` and `MergeConflict`, the `VersionStore` Protocol of the storage side, and its git implementation `GitVersionStore`, which reads and writes the runtime's bare mirror. Where the shared main lives is a strategy: `_GitHubUpstream` fetches from and pushes to the component repository on GitHub, and `_LocalUpstream` keeps the shared main in the mirror itself, seeded from the package's default components. `ensure_working_copy` clones the local mirror into people's working copy.
modules.summary: A version is a git commit, and its id is the 40-character commit SHA. `Commit` is a frozen, slots dataclass (`id`, `parent` = the first parent, `message`, `created_at` = the committer time in whole seconds). All `VersionStore` methods are coroutines: `read_main` and `move_main(expected, new)` (the mirror's adopted main; compare-and-swap, never touching GitHub), `read_commit` and `read_tree` (None when the version does not exist), `list_commits` (versions reachable from main and the kept forks, newest first), `write` (writes a commit without a ref, keeping the parent's files outside the five folders; None when the same commit already exists), `keep` (a fork ref), `fetch` (the shared main: GitHub's after a fetch, or the mirror's own main in local mode; None when there is none), `is_ancestor`, `merge_tree(base, ours, theirs)` (a three-way merge of the five-folder trees; `MergeConflict` with the paths on conflict), `push` (a non-force push to GitHub's main, or a fast-forward of the local mirror's main; False when refused), and `initial_tree` (the first local main's tree, or None). `GitVersionStore(directory, url="", *, ssh_key="", hooks=None, seed=None)` runs the git CLI with `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `LC_ALL=C`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` with the deploy key when `ssh_key` is set; cancellation kills the child). The constructor picks the strategy: with a `url`, `_GitHubUpstream` sets `remote.origin.url` and implements `fetch` and `push` over the network; without one, `_LocalUpstream` returns the mirror's main from `fetch`, moves it only by fast-forward in `push` (`is_ancestor` then `move_main`), and reads the `seed` package's five folders with `snapshot.package_tree` off the event loop for `initial_tree`. The repository is created as a bare repository on first use only in GitHub mode or in local mode with a `seed`; otherwise it only reads an existing repository (the check CLI). `hooks` is set as `core.hooksPath` every time it opens. The module function `ensure_working_copy(mirror, path)` runs `git clone --branch main <mirror> <path>` when `path` does not exist. Refs of the mirror: `MAIN_REF` (`refs/heads/main`, the adopted main the runtime runs), `REMOTE_MAIN_REF` (`refs/remotes/origin/main`, GitHub's main at the last fetch), and `FORK_PREFIX` (`refs/te/forks/<id>`, optimizer candidates, never pushed). A version's tree is the regular files (modes 100644 and 100755) for which `snapshot.owned` is true; symlinks and submodules are left out, and file modes are not kept. `read_commit` and `list_commits` parse one `git log` format (`_parse_commits`); `move_main` runs `git update-ref` with the old value; `write` keeps the parent's entries outside the five folders (`_inherited_entries`), writes the blobs (`_blob_entries`), builds the tree in a temporary index (`_write_tree`), and writes a commit object with a fixed author; `fetch` updates `REMOTE_MAIN_REF` with `+refs/heads/main`; `merge_tree` runs `git merge-tree --write-tree` with an explicit merge base; a successful `push` also moves `REMOTE_MAIN_REF`. Only GitHub's `fetch` and `push` use the network, and error messages mask credentials in URLs.
modules.flow: `open_repo` constructs it with `config.COMPONENT_REPO_DIR`, `COMPONENT_REPO_URL`, `COMPONENT_REPO_SSH_KEY`, `HOOKS_DIR`, and `PACKAGE_ROOT` for the runtime; the check CLI constructs a read-only one over `--repo`. `Repo`'s `start`, `refresh`, `sync`, `fork`, `merge`, `log`, and `tree` read and write through it; `build_runtime` calls `ensure_working_copy` in local mode.

key_symbols.name: MAIN_REF
key_symbols.explain: `refs/heads/main` of the mirror: the adopted main (a version the current Host loaded); the runtime runs only this.

key_symbols.name: REMOTE_MAIN_REF
key_symbols.explain: `refs/remotes/origin/main`: GitHub's main at the last fetch (not yet validated); a successful push moves it too.

key_symbols.name: FORK_PREFIX
key_symbols.explain: `refs/te/forks/`: the prefix of the refs (`<prefix><id>`) that keep optimizer candidates so they are not garbage-collected; never pushed.

key_symbols.name: Commit
key_symbols.explain: A stored version (frozen, slots): `id` (the commit SHA), `parent` (the first parent; None for a root commit), `message`, `created_at` (the committer time in whole seconds, UTC).

key_symbols.name: GitError
key_symbols.explain: A git failure (unreachable remote, broken repository, unconfigured URL); the message is git's stderr with credentials in URLs masked.

key_symbols.name: MergeConflict
key_symbols.explain: A three-way merge conflicted; `paths` holds the conflicting paths.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore
key_symbols.explain: The storage side of versions; all methods are coroutines: `read_main`, `move_main`, `read_commit`, `read_tree`, `list_commits`, `write`, `keep`, `fetch`, `is_ancestor`, `merge_tree`, `push`, `initial_tree`.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.read_main
key_symbols.explain: The mirror's adopted main, or None.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.move_main
key_symbols.explain: Changes the mirror's main to `new` only when it is `expected` (None means there is no main yet), returning True if it changed; does not change GitHub.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.list_commits
key_symbols.explain: Returns the versions reachable from main and the kept forks, newest first.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.write
key_symbols.explain: Writes a version without creating a ref: the given five-folder tree plus the parent's files outside the five folders; returns None when the same commit (tree, parent, message, second) already exists.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.keep
key_symbols.explain: Keeps a written version as a fork ref.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.fetch
key_symbols.explain: Returns the shared main's id: fetches GitHub's main, or in local mode reads the mirror's main; None when there is none.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.merge_tree
key_symbols.explain: The five-folder tree of merging `ours` and `theirs` on the base `base`; raises `MergeConflict` on conflict.

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.push
key_symbols.explain: Advances the shared main to a version without force (a push to GitHub, or a fast-forward of the local mirror's main); returns False when that is refused as not a fast-forward.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore
key_symbols.explain: The git implementation of `VersionStore` over `directory` (a bare mirror or a clone). The constructor keeps its signature and picks the strategy for the shared main: `_GitHubUpstream(url)` with a `url`, otherwise `_LocalUpstream(seed)`. The repository is created on first use only in GitHub mode or in local mode with a `seed`; `hooks` becomes `core.hooksPath` on every open, and `ssh_key` sets the deploy key for git. Construction does no I/O.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.read_main
key_symbols.explain: Reads `MAIN_REF`; None when absent.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.resolve
key_symbols.explain: Resolves a revision (`HEAD`, a branch, a SHA) to a commit id, or None; used by the check CLI.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.read_commit
key_symbols.explain: Reads a commit by its 40-character id with `git log -1` in the same format as `list_commits`; None for a malformed or missing id.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.read_tree
key_symbols.explain: Returns the five-folder regular files of a commit (path → content), or None when the commit does not exist.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.list_commits
key_symbols.explain: Runs `git log` from `MAIN_REF` and every fork ref and returns the commits newest first.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.is_ancestor
key_symbols.explain: `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; raises `GitError` on errors other than yes or no.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.move_main
key_symbols.explain: `git update-ref` with the expected old value (all zeros when None); returns False when main is no longer `expected` and raises `GitError` on other failures.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.write
key_symbols.explain: Writes blobs, a tree built in a temporary index (keeping the parent's entries outside the five folders), and a commit with the fixed author `TrackEverything` at `created_at`; returns None without writing when that commit already exists.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.keep
key_symbols.explain: Creates `refs/te/forks/<id>`.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.fetch
key_symbols.explain: Delegates to the strategy: with GitHub, `git fetch origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main` (None when GitHub has no main, `GitError` on failure); in local mode, the mirror's main.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.merge_tree
key_symbols.explain: `git merge-tree --write-tree` with `--merge-base`; exit code 1 raises `MergeConflict` with the conflicting paths and other failures `GitError`; returns the merged five-folder files.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.push
key_symbols.explain: Delegates to the strategy: with GitHub, `git push --porcelain --no-verify origin <id>:refs/heads/main` without force (the merge has validated the version; the Host's `pre-push` is for people's clones), also moving `REMOTE_MAIN_REF`, False when rejected; in local mode, moves the mirror's main to `id` only when the current main is its ancestor (compare-and-swap).

key_symbols.name: VersionStore.initial_tree
key_symbols.explain: The tree that becomes the first main when there is no shared main (the package's default components in local mode); None when the store makes none.

key_symbols.name: GitVersionStore.initial_tree
key_symbols.explain: Delegates to the strategy: in local mode with a `seed`, the seed package's five folders read with `package_tree` in a thread; otherwise None.

key_symbols.name: ensure_working_copy
key_symbols.explain: Makes the local-mode working copy: when `path` does not exist, clones the mirror (`git clone -q --branch main <mirror> <path>`, so `origin` is the mirror's absolute path) and returns True; an existing path is left as it is (False). A failed clone raises `GitError`.

invariants: A version id is the commit SHA; the same tree, parent, message, and second always give the same commit, so `write` reports an existing commit instead of creating a duplicate.
`move_main` is a compare-and-swap through `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`: when several processes move main at the same time, only one succeeds; it never changes GitHub.
Writing a version replaces only the five folders; the parent's other files (such as `README.md`) are kept, so a pushed version keeps the repository's docs.
Only the GitHub strategy's `fetch` and `push` use the network, and `push` never forces; in local mode `push` only fast-forwards. Construction does no I/O; the mirror is created on first use.
pitfalls: Objects of a write whose load fails stay unreferenced in the mirror until git's garbage collection; only main and the kept forks protect versions.
File modes and symlinks are not part of a version: `write` stores every file of the five folders as 100644, so executable bits are lost when the optimizer rewrites a tree.
Requires git 2.40 or later (`merge-tree --write-tree` with `--merge-base`).
`list_commits` reads the whole history reachable from main and the forks without pagination.
