mechanisms.title: Component version store: versions are commits of the component repository, main is adopted only when it loads, pinned by name, released when unused
mechanisms.design: Components are versioned in git, and a version is a commit. The runtime reads only its bare mirror, whose `main` is the adopted version. With GitHub, every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL` `sync` fetches GitHub's main and adopts it only when the current Host loads it, and the optimizer's `merge` pushes to GitHub first and moves the mirror's main only after the push succeeds. In local mode the mirror holds the shared main itself: people push to it from `components/` through its `pre-receive` check, and `merge` fast-forwards it. The mirror's main is read at the start of each message: new runs use the new main, and runs in progress finish on their original version; a version that is not main and has no users is released immediately.
steps: Versions are git commits: the version id is the 40-character SHA and the label `c.<first 8>`. `GitVersionStore` runs the git CLI against the mirror `COMPONENT_REPO_DIR` (default `data/components.git`; with GitHub, remote `origin` = `COMPONENT_REPO_URL` and deploy key `COMPONENT_REPO_SSH_KEY`): `refs/heads/main` is the adopted main (in local mode also the main people push to), `refs/remotes/origin/main` GitHub's main at the last fetch, and `refs/te/forks/<id>` the kept optimizer candidates. A version's tree is the regular files under the five folders (`snapshot.owned`); other files of the repository, symlinks, submodules, and caches are not part of it.

A person changes components in `components/` with pull → edit → push. The Host's `scripts/component-hooks` run the check CLI (`python -m trackeverything.core.versioning check --repo <repository> <sha>`) through the launcher of the checkout that holds them: a GitHub clone's `pre-push` for every update of `refs/heads/main`, and the local mirror's `pre-receive` for its new tip (also refusing a deletion of main). `Repo.validate` loads the commit with that Host's services and builds its graph without storing anything, and a failure stops the push. In local mode the runtime clones the mirror into `components/` on startup when it is missing.

Adopting the shared main: `TrackingRuntime` calls `repo.sync()` every `COMPONENT_FETCH_INTERVAL` (300 seconds). `sync` fetches GitHub's main (in local mode it only reads the mirror's main); when it differs from the loaded main and has not failed before, it loads it in a thread and adopts it with `_advance_main` (the compare-and-swap `move_main(mirror main, id)`, then switching this process). A failed fetch or read only logs a warning and is retried; a commit that does not load is logged once at error level, recorded in `_failed`, and not adopted (`_load_candidate`, shared with `refresh`). On the first startup, when the mirror has no main, `start` fetches GitHub's main, or in local mode writes the package's default components as the root commit `Initial components`, and adopts it the same way; a failure aborts startup.

A new version is loaded before it is kept: `Repo._new_commit` rejects paths outside the five folders with `check_paths`, writes the commit with `store.write` (keeping the parent's files outside the five folders; when the same commit already exists, the time moves on one second), then runs `_load` in a thread: `loader.register`, writing the read-only file view (used by `__file__`, Skills, and scripts), importing all modules in name order, calling the version's own `agent/compose.build` through the function returned by `prepare_components` to obtain a `ComponentGraph`, and setting each agent's `version_label` to `c.<first 8 characters of the id>`. Only then does `store.keep` create the fork ref; when any step fails, it calls `_dispose` and raises, leaving no ref (unreferenced objects are left to git's garbage collection).

Isolation relies on the import machinery: `Repo.__init__` calls `loader.install()`, which puts a `VersionFinder` that resolves only `_te_versions.*` at the front of `sys.meta_path`; for a module that is not in the version it returns None and never falls back to disk. `SnapshotLoader.exec_module` parses the AST from the version's source and, through `OwnedImportRewriter`, rewrites absolute imports that point into the four module folders to the `_te_versions.v_<id>` namespace; `import trackeverything` is bound to the version's `_Facade` (module folders are forwarded to this version, other names to the canonical package); importing a version-owned module with a literal `import_module` raises `ImportError`. Shared modules such as `core` and `llm` stay canonical, so all versions share the same types and locks.

Merging a candidate: `fork(parent, tree, message)` creates a candidate without changing main. `merge(id)` reads the shared main R (fetching GitHub's): if R already contains the candidate, it returns main without pushing; if R is the candidate's parent, it pushes the candidate; otherwise `merge_tree(candidate.parent, R, candidate)` combines both changes into a new version with parent R and the message plus `Rebased-From: <candidate>`, loaded and validated through `_new_commit`. The push to GitHub never forces and the local mirror only fast-forwards (`PushRejected` when another push landed after the read), and the mirror's main moves only after that succeeds; `MergeConflict`, `GitError`, and load failures likewise leave the mirror's main unchanged.

Reading main: `Runtime.execute` calls `refresh()` first for every message; when the mirror's main equals the one already loaded it returns immediately without taking the lock, and otherwise it loads and switches to the new main (a main that `sync` adopted in this process is already loaded and switched). When loading fails, it records the id in `_failed`, logs it once through `describe_failure`, and keeps using the main it has already loaded.

Pinning by name: the `RunVersions` returned by `repo.run()` is put into `AgentContext.agents`. The first time `version(name)` is called it records the current main, and afterwards that name always returns this version within the same run; each version increments `users` only once. The Runtime uses it to get the entrance, and `BaseAgent.call_agent` and `_build_callables` use it to get child agents. During execution, `current_code_version()` carries the running agent's own `version_label`.

Release: when a run ends, `Repo.release(run)` ends the run's use (`RunVersions.end` decrements the users), and `_collect` releases every version that is not main and has 0 `users`; when main switches, the old main is also released immediately if it has no users. `_dispose` unregisters the loader, removes the namespace's modules from `sys.modules`, the attributes on the root package, and the linecache entries, clears the component graph, and deletes the file view (a directory that fails to delete is retried at the next release); the commits stay in the mirror.

`_load`: register, write the file view, import all modules, and build the component graph; on failure, release everything

notes: Global variables of version-owned modules exist once per version; locks and caches that must be unique across versions use `shared_state` (see the section on shared state across versions); releasing removes only the version's own references and does not touch shared objects.
The runtime does not watch files or read a checkout: a person's push reaches the runtime only through `sync`, and a deploy of this repository never changes components.

Host changes (`core/`, `llm/`, and so on) take effect when the supervisor restarts; when the new Host contract is incompatible with the adopted main, the runtime refuses to start. Deploy such a change in a form the current components still load with, then push the components (the pre-push hook checks against the deployed Host); to recover, push a main that loads and point the mirror's `refs/heads/main` at it.

mechanisms.title: Agent registry and LLM tiers: declared by name, built by name, resolved by name at run time
mechanisms.design: Child agents and LLMs are both declared by name. The Host provides only the LLM clients named `max`, `high`, `low`, `flash`, and `flash_low`, and the version's `agent/compose.py` passes the list of agent classes to `build_agents`, which builds exactly one instance per name and validates child agent names, so composition errors fail while the version is loaded; child agent instances are not bound, and are resolved by name through the run handle at run time.
steps: `BaseAgent` declares its composition with class variables: `name`; `llm` (default `max`, a key of `HostServices.llms`); `agents` (a tuple of child agent names); `tools`, `pre`, `post`, `on_error` (tuples of types); `fatal_tools`; `hidden_callables`. For example, `PrEventAgent` declares `llm` as `flash_low` and `agents` as `(*DiscordOutputAgent.agents, "project_memory", "review", "pr_cleanup", "document")`, and `ProjectAgent` declares `llm` as `flash`.

`BaseAgent.__init__(llm, *, logger)` instantiates the declared Tools with no-argument constructors and the Harnesses with the same `llm`, and registers them one by one (`_add_unique` rejects duplicate names with `ValueError`); it neither creates nor binds child agents (`agents` is deduplicated and stored as `_agent_names`), and it never replaces the LLM while running.

On the Host side, `open_host_services` calls `build_llms(logger)`: it creates one `asyncio.Semaphore(config.LLM_CONCURRENCY)` (default 10) and wraps every client as `TrackedLLM(ThrottledLLM(inner, sem), logger)`. `max` comes from `build_default_llm()`: with `ZAI_API_KEY` it is a z.ai reasoning client with effort `max` (wrapped in `FallbackLLM` when `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is also set); otherwise it is DeepSeek, then OpenAI, and when neither is available it raises `RuntimeError`. With `ZAI_API_KEY`, `high` and `low` are z.ai clients with the corresponding effort, and `flash` and `flash_low` are GLM-5.3-Flash (`config.ZAI_FLASH_MODEL`) clients with effort `high` and `low`; otherwise they are the same object as `max`. The result goes into `HostServices(llms=..., logger=..., session_store=..., full_mesh=..., skills_root=...)`.

The `prepare(version)` returned by `prepare_components(services)` takes the version's `trackeverything.agent.compose` and calls `build(services, skills_root=...)`; `agent/compose.build` calls `build_agents` with the `AGENTS` tuple, `services.llms`, `services.logger`, and the per-name constructor dependencies (`history` for `project_qa` and `general`; `sources` for `dispatch` and `github`).

The first phase of `build_agents` builds class by class: a class without `name`, a duplicate name, or a `cls.llm` that is not in `llms` raises `ValueError`; each class that passes the checks is built once with `cls(llms[cls.llm], logger=logger, **extra.get(cls.name, {}))`. It then checks whether the constructor dependencies mention any name that was not built.

The second phase only validates names: when any name in a parent instance's `list_agent_names()` is not in the set of built agents, it raises `ValueError`. It binds no instances and does not propagate the logger (every instance gets the same logger from its constructor arguments); each name has exactly one instance, and circular declarations also pass validation.

`agent/compose.build` then registers one shared `FetchSourceTool(dict(SOURCES))` on every instance whose `fatal_tools` includes `fetch_source`, and registers shared instances of the base tools (`BASE_TOOLS`) on all instances; when `AGENT_FULL_MESH` is on it calls `wire_full_mesh(agents)` (`extend_callables` adds only undeclared Tools and child names and skips the agent itself), then binds the Skill catalog with `bind_skills(agents, ...)`, and returns `ComponentGraph(agents=agents, entrances=frozenset(ENTRANCES), sources=dict(SOURCES))`.

Any `ValueError` during building is a failure to load the version: `sync` does not adopt that version, `fork` keeps no fork ref, the check CLI fails, a failure to load main at startup aborts startup, and a `refresh` failure keeps the current main. At run time, child agents can be called only through `call_agent`: it resolves the instance by name through `ctx.agents`, and when the name is not a declared child or cannot be resolved it returns an error result with `ErrorNote("delegation", ...)`.

notes: An agent instance is shared among all parent agents and all runs of the same version, and so are its instance attributes (such as the `_channel_store` that `DispatchAgent` creates lazily); per-run state lives in `AgentContext` or in the call scope `AgentToolScope`. Agents with the same name in different versions are different instances.

`ComponentGraph.agents` contains all agents of the version, but `entrances` contains only `ENTRANCES` (`dispatch`): the Runtime always executes dispatch, and other agents can be reached only as child agents. dispatch declares 17 child agents in the `agents` tuple of `agent/dispatch.py` (`github`, `general`, `project_qa`, `issue`, `pr_event`, `ci_failure`, `issue_investigation`, `issue_cleanup`, `project_memory`, `review`, `document`, `slack`, `pr_cleanup`, `sentry_autofix`, `sentry_autofix_item`, `optimizer`, and `reservation_fire`): event routing hands GitHub events to `github` (which further routes them to `pr_event`, `ci_failure`, `issue_investigation`, or `issue_cleanup`), Discord messages to `project_qa`, `issue`, or `general`, Discord confirmation buttons to `general`, Slack events to `slack`, and auto-development `internal` events to `issue`; a named run can specify any of these names (an `agent_name` of `discord` runs as a `general` conversation); when a name not in this list (such as `triage`) is given as the `agent_name` of a named run, dispatch runs no child agent, ends with an error, and ACKs.

When `ZAI_API_KEY` is not configured, `high`, `low`, `flash`, `flash_low`, and `max` are the same object, so an `llm` declaration never makes building fail; all tiers share the same Semaphore, so the LLM concurrency limit applies to the whole process.

mechanisms.title: The BaseAgent.run boundary and the LLM loop: Harness order, a shared step budget, parallel child agents, sequential Tools
mechanisms.design: `BaseAgent.run` is an agent's only execution boundary. It runs pre, `_execute`, post (only on ok), and adjudication in that order, and only cancellation propagates outward. The LLM only returns an answer or calls; BaseAgent decides when to stop, whether a call targets a Tool or a child agent, and whether calls run in parallel or in sequence.
steps: `run` is `@final`: it first creates an `agent`-type `_Span` (its request is a snapshot of `request` and `ctx.data`), then `_enter` sets four ContextVars, `current_run_id`, `current_agent_execution_id`, `current_parent_agent_execution_id`, and `_current_scope` (plus `current_component_version` when the instance has a `version_label`); `AgentToolScope.depth` is the outer depth plus 1 (1 for the entrance), and they are restored in reverse order in `finally`.

When the depth exceeds `MAX_AGENT_DEPTH` (16), it raises `RuntimeError` without running the pre Harnesses or `_execute`, and this becomes an error result directly. Otherwise it runs `await self._check_pre(call) or await self._execute(call)`: pre Harnesses are evaluated in declaration order through `_evaluate`, an exception raised by a check counts as a rejection (fail-closed), and the first rejection returns an error result with `ErrorNote("harness:<name>", ...)` without running `_execute`.

Post Harnesses run only when `status == "ok"`, and the first rejection replaces the result (the harness log keeps `original_result`); then `_adjudicate` adjudicates unresolved Tool failures. On `CancelledError` it takes and discards the failures, records `cancelled`, and re-raises; other exceptions become an error result with `ErrorNote("execution", ...)` plus the failures taken. Finally it writes the agent log, and on error it runs the on_error Harnesses in order, whose failures are only logged.

The default `_execute` calls `_execute_llm_loop`: `_build_messages` produces the system message (`get_prompt()`) and the user message (JSON of `request` and `data`), and `_add_system_extras(messages, ctx)` appends the Skill catalog once to the end of the first system message, plus `PARALLEL_CALL_RULE` when the callables include child agents. In each round, `_build_callables(ctx)` lists the Tools and the child agents resolved through `ctx.agents`, minus the `hidden_callables` merged along the MRO (hidden children are not resolved).

`_respond_one_step` first calls `ctx.advance_step()`: there is no await between the check and the increment, so a single event loop never overshoots; the same `AgentContext` is shared by the whole agent tree, so the budget (the `max_steps` given by the Runtime) belongs to the whole tree. When the budget is exhausted it returns None, and the loop ends with `max_steps`. A `FinalAnswer` returns ok (or enters the repair path); for `Calls`, the call JSON and `raw` are first appended as an assistant message and then handed to `_dispatch_calls`, and the observations are appended as tool messages.

`_dispatch_calls` processes calls in order: a name that was not offered to the LLM in this round is not executed; it writes a tool log entry and returns `callable was not offered`; a call that resolves to no Tool but belongs to a child agent is collected into a group; for a Tool call, it first runs the accumulated child agents with `_run_children` and then runs the Tool on its own. At the end it runs the remaining group, and the observations are returned in call order.

`_run_children` runs a single child agent in the current task and runs several in parallel with `asyncio.TaskGroup`. `_dispatch` calls `call_tool(ctx, LLMCall(name, tool.llm_args(args)))` for a Tool and `call_agent(agent_call, name, args.get("request"))` for a child agent; the observation contains `status`, `output`, and the rendered errors.

`call_agent` is `@final`, and both LLM calls and Python control (such as `DispatchAgent._delegate`) go through it: it resolves the child instance by name through `call.ctx.agents`, and when the name is not a declared child, there is no run handle, or it cannot be resolved, it returns an error result with `ErrorNote("delegation", ...)`; otherwise it runs `child.run(call.child(request))`, where the child call references the same `AgentContext`. Child agents in `hidden_callables` can be called this way too.

excerpts.caption: The `run` boundary: depth, pre, `_execute`, post, adjudication, cancellation, and exceptions
`_execute_llm_loop`: FinalAnswer, the repair prompt, call dispatch, and budget exhaustion
`_dispatch_calls`: consecutive child agents form a group, which runs before the next Tool
`call_agent`: resolves the child agent by name through `ctx.agents`; the child call shares the same Context

notes: Parallel child agents share the same `ctx.data`, `tool_state`, `authorization`, and step counter; dependent calls must go into later responses, and `PARALLEL_CALL_RULE` tells the LLM this rule.

The child tasks in a `TaskGroup` copy the same context and share the parent agent's version pins in `ctx.agents`; agents hold no locks, and no agent is called while a Tool holds a lock, so a parent agent never holds a lock while waiting for a child agent.
The step budget limits only LLM rounds; it does not limit the Tool and child agent calls made by Python control, and LLM calls inside external CLIs are not counted either.

mechanisms.title: The Tool failure ledger: bucketed per agent execution, resolved per target, adjudicated at the run boundary
mechanisms.design: All Tool side effects go through `call_tool()`; a failure becomes a `ToolResult` and is recorded in the shared Context's `ToolFailures`, and a later success on the same target resolves it. Each agent takes its unrecovered failures at its own run boundary, and only failures of `fatal_tools` turn ok into error.
steps: `AgentContext.tool_failures` is a `ToolFailures()` with `init=False`, and never enters repr, the LLM, or saved JSON. `_entries` is bucketed by `current_agent_execution_id.get()`; `BaseAgent._enter` sets this ContextVar for each agent execution, so although the whole tree shares one Context, every agent execution (including each child agent) has its own bucket.

`call_tool` executes through `_invoke`: when the name resolves to no Tool, the result is `ToolResult(ok=False, error="unknown tool: ...")`; a Tool that comes from a Skill first runs that Skill's definition check; an `Exception` raised by a Tool becomes `ToolResult(ok=False, error="<type>: <message>")`; `CancelledError` only writes a `cancelled` log entry and propagates, without entering the ledger.

The target key is `tool.error_key(call.args)` (None when the Tool does not exist). On success it calls `resolve(name, key)`; on failure, `record(name, key, ErrorNote(name, error or "tool failed"))`. A slot is formed from the Tool name and the key, using `*` when the key is None; `resolve` removes both the matching slot and that Tool's `*` slot, so at any time the ledger holds only unrecovered failures.

`Tool.error_key` defaults to the arguments as key-sorted JSON, so only a successful retry with the same arguments resolves a failure; Tools with narrower targets override it, for example `project_edit_doc`, `project_create_doc`, and `project_delete_doc` use `store.doc_error_key(args)`. `ErrorNote.stage` is the Tool name, so `fatal_tools` is checked against `note.stage`.

`_adjudicate` calls `take()` at the `run` boundary to take and delete the current agent execution's bucket: an ok result with fatal failures becomes error, with `errors` set to those fatal notes; an ok result without fatal failures is unchanged, and the other failures appear only in the error field of the agent log; for a non-ok result, `errors` is the existing notes plus the fatal notes, and when it is still empty, `max_steps` adds `ErrorNote("budget", ...)` and other statuses add a note whose stage is the agent name and whose reason is the `response`, so every non-ok result has at least one note.

The exception path puts `ErrorNote("execution", ...)` into `errors` together with the failures taken by `take()`; the cancellation path calls `take()` and discards the result. A child agent's failures are taken at its own boundary and reach the parent as the status and errors returned by `call_agent`, and a child agent's success cannot resolve failures in the parent's bucket either.

`_execute_llm_loop(call, repair_tool_failures=True)` (used by `ProjectAgent` and `GeneralAgent`) checks `ctx.tool_failures.unresolved(*self.fatal_tools)` when the LLM gives a `FinalAnswer`: when there are unresolved fatal failures, it keeps that answer and appends the assistant's text once, plus a user message with `_REPAIR_PROMPT` and the notes, so the LLM can repair them and give the complete answer again; when they are still unresolved at the next answer, or unresolved fatal failures remain when the budget runs out, it returns `_incomplete` (error whose response is the latest answer, or a list of the unfinished operations when no answer was given), and `_adjudicate` then attaches each fatal note once.

mechanisms.title: Structured execution log: an injected LogRecorder, the parent execution fixed at start, write failures never affect execution
mechanisms.design: Each execution of an Agent, Harness, Tool, or LLM, and of the PR review CLI (`review_pr`), is written as one `LogEvent` when it ends (other external CLIs appear only in the tool event that calls them); parent-child relationships are determined by ContextVars at the start of the execution, and the events within a run share a `run_id`; a log write failure is only logged and does not change the execution.
steps: `core/abc/execution_log.py` defines only the `LogRecorder` protocol (`async record(event)`); `LogEvent` and the four ContextVars `current_run_id`, `current_agent_execution_id`, `current_parent_agent_execution_id`, and `current_component_version` live in `core/builtin/domain/execution_log.py`. `open_host_services` opens one `PostgresExecutionLogger` with `open_execution_logger()` and hands it to both `build_llms(logger)` and `HostServices.logger`.
Injection on the agent side: `build_agents` passes the same logger to every constructor, and the logger is not propagated between parent and child. `_log` writes only when `self._logger` is not None.

`_Span` generates `execution_id` when it is created, takes `parent_id` from `current_agent_execution_id.get`, and records `started_at` and `elapsed_clock()` (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` on macOS, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` on Linux, including system sleep time); `end()` copies the request, result, and error with `snapshot()` to build the `LogEvent`.

Agent events: `run` creates the span before `_enter`, so the parent execution is the calling agent's execution (None for the entrance); `_enter` then sets this `execution_id` as `current_agent_execution_id` and sets `current_run_id`, the parent execution ID, and (when the instance has a `version_label`) `current_component_version`. At the end it writes the status (ok, error, max_steps, cancelled), and the error field holds the notes produced by adjudication.

Spans created within the same agent execution all have it as their parent: harness events have the component `harness:<Agent>.<Harness>`; pre records `ok` or `blocked`, post records `ok` or `rejected` (with `original_result`), and on_error records `ok` or `failed`; tool events are written by `call_tool` as `ok`, `error`, or `cancelled`, and a call that was not offered to the LLM writes one `error`.

LLM events are written by `TrackedLLM.respond`, the outermost wrapper of every client, independent of agents: `run_id` comes from `current_run_id` (newly generated when absent), and the parent execution from `current_agent_execution_id`; on success the component is `<provider>/<model>`, the result is final_answer or calls, and `usage` plus the `cost_usd` computed by `calculate_cost_usd` are attached; on an exception it records component `llm` with status `error` and re-raises. `ThrottledLLM` is the inner layer, so `duration_ms` includes the time spent waiting for the Semaphore.

CLI events are written by `_log_cli` in `tools/review.py`: it calls `open_execution_logger()` itself, the component is `review_pr`, `run_id` comes from `ctx.run_id` (`-` without a ctx), the parent execution from `current_agent_execution_id`, and the result contains measurements such as the CLI version, the model, and the exit code; a recording failure only calls `log.warning`.

`PostgresExecutionLogger.record` inserts each event into the `logs` table through the ORM with a short-lived session, and writes `code_version=current_code_version()` (during an agent execution, `<Host version>+c.<first 8 characters of that agent's version id>`); any exception goes to `log.exception` and is swallowed. `snapshot()` itself never raises; values that cannot be serialized are recorded as `snapshot_error` and `repr`. On the read side, `api/runs.py` turns events into steps with `id` and `parent`, and an agent event whose `parent_execution_id` is None is the root of the run.

excerpts.caption: `PostgresExecutionLogger.record`: attaches the code version; failures are only logged
excerpts.code:
async def record(self, event: LogEvent) -> None:
        """Append one event; never raise — a log write must not fail a run.

        Every row carries this process's code version, so each event can be
        traced to the version that produced it. Stamping here covers every
        logger instance, including the ones tools open on their own.
        """
        try:
            async with self._sessions() as session:
                await session.execute(
                    insert(ExecutionLogRow).values(
                        event_type=event.event_type,
                        run_id=event.run_id,
                        execution_id=event.execution_id,
                        parent_execution_id=event.parent_execution_id,
                        component=event.component,
                        started_at=event.started_at,
                        duration_ms=event.duration_ms,
                        status=event.status,
                        request_json=_dump(event.request),
                        result_json=_dump_optional(event.result),
                        error_json=_dump_optional(event.error),
                        usage_json=_dump_optional(event.usage),
                        cost_usd=event.cost_usd,
                        code_version=current_code_version(),
                    )
                )
                await session.commit()
        except Exception:
            # Observability must not change source, agent, or LLM behavior.
            log.exception("failed to persist %s log event", event.event_type)

notes: Events are written only when an execution ends; when the process is forcibly terminated, in-progress executions have no events, and the corresponding `session_run` rows are marked `interrupted` at the next start.
The tasks of parallel child agents copy the context when they are created, so the parent execution of each child agent in a `TaskGroup` is still the agent that made the call.
When an LLM is called outside an agent (no `current_run_id`), the LLM event gets a newly generated `run_id` and is not associated with any run.

mechanisms.title: Shared state and locks across versions: the same object by name; TaskLock is exclusive per task and not reentrant
mechanisms.design: Locks and caches that must be unique across versions stay in component modules and are obtained by name from the Host's process-wide container through `shared()`, `task_lock()`, and `keyed_lock()`; a lock wraps only a single operation inside a Tool, is exclusive per task, and is not reentrant: when the holding task requests it again, it fails immediately instead of waiting for itself.
steps: `shared(name, factory)` caches by name in the global dict `_objects`, guarded by `_guard`, a `threading.Lock`: the first call runs the factory, and afterwards every version gets the same object. When the module of the value's type starts with `_te_versions.` it raises `TypeError`, because instances of version-owned classes would keep old version code alive and `isinstance` would split by version; the check is shallow and looks only at the value itself. Releasing a version does not clear this container, and objects live until the process ends.

`context_var(name, default)` and `task_lock(name)` are convenience functions built on `shared`; the Discord send lock and channel cache, the Gmail token, and the pending lock of `tools/fix` use `task_lock` or `shared`.
`TaskLock.hold()` must run in a task: when the holder is the current task, it does not wait and immediately raises `RuntimeError` (not reentrant, so the same task never waits forever for itself).

Otherwise, when the internal `asyncio.Lock` is unlocked and belongs to a different loop, it is replaced with a new lock for the current loop; after `acquire` it records the holder, and on exit it clears the holder and releases; other tasks wait on `acquire`. It does not recognize parent-child relationships between tasks.

`keyed_lock(namespace, key)` takes or creates the `TaskLock` for `(namespace, key)` under `_guard` and increments its user count, decrementing it in `finally`; when the last user (including waiters) leaves, the key is deleted, so keys do not grow without bound.

Only Tools in versions use these (the Host calls no component module): the Discord send lock, channel lock, and ensure lock, the Gmail token lock, and the pending lock of `tools/fix` use `task_lock`, and `issue_lock` in `tools/issue_workflow.py` (that is, `keyed_lock("issue", key)`) wraps the channel decision and record in `_ensure_channel`, and, in `_close` of Issue close, the check and update of the development record, the deletion of the dedicated Discord channel, and the clearing of the source links. The Runtime and agents such as dispatch, pr_event, issue, the Issue engineering flow, project_memory, and project hold no locks, and runs for the same session, PR, Issue, or Source execute in parallel.

Lock rule: a lock wraps only a single operation inside a Tool and no agent is called while it is held, so a lock is never held while waiting for a child agent. The file locks in `tools/project/locks.py` (the project commit lock and the exclusive file lock used by the work docs store) work across processes and register their holders with `shared`; a second acquisition by the same task is allowed to reenter as nesting within a Tool (document reads during a commit, manual arbitration, or notification recording).

excerpts.caption: `shared`: caches by name and rejects instances of version-owned classes
`TaskLock.hold`: not reentrant; raises `RuntimeError` when the holding task requests it again
excerpts.code:
@asynccontextmanager
    async def hold(self) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        current = asyncio.current_task()
        if current is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.label}: a task-aware lock needs a running task")
        if self._owner is current:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.label} is not reentrant; the holding task requested it again")
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        if self._loop is not loop and not self._lock.locked():
            self._lock, self._loop = asyncio.Lock(), loop
        await self._lock.acquire()
        self._owner = current
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._owner = None
            self._lock.release()

excerpts.caption: `keyed_lock`: created per key and reclaimed when the last user leaves
excerpts.code:
slot = (namespace, key)
    with _guard:
        lock, users = _keyed.get(slot, (TaskLock(f"keyed_lock({namespace!r}, {key!r})"), 0))
        _keyed[slot] = (lock, users + 1)
    try:
        async with lock.hold():
            yield
    finally:
        with _guard:
            lock, users = _keyed[slot]
            if users == 1:
                del _keyed[slot]
            else:
                _keyed[slot] = (lock, users - 1)

notes: These objects are shared only within one process; they are not persisted and are not shared between the queue and runtime processes, so values needed after a restart belong in files or a Store. A `TaskLock` inside a Tool is therefore mutually exclusive only within a single process; cross-process exclusion uses the file locks in `tools/project/locks.py`.
`shared()` checks only the value itself: version-owned instances placed inside a container are not rejected; when the shape of a value changes, use a new name.
`TaskLock` is not a thread lock: it targets tasks on the same event loop, and the internal `asyncio.Lock` moves to a new loop only when it is unlocked.

The agent layer has no exclusion per business unit: review, comment handling, and docs sync for the same PR may overlap, and investigation, engineering progress, and Codex execution for the same Issue may overlap or write to the same workspace directory at the same time; project sync tries an optimistic commit at most `_ATTEMPTS` (3) times and fails when every attempt is stale.
